美保神社 | image = Mihojinja -01.jpg | caption = Miho Jinja | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|33|44|N|133|18|22|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Miho Jinja'''|美保神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] in [[Matsue, Shimane|Matsue]], [[Shimane Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. The [[Taisha-zukuri]] [[Honden]] of 1813 is an [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Cultural Property]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2968 |title=Miho Jinja Honden |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 January 2012}} A collection of 846 [[Traditional Japanese musical instruments|musical instruments]] dedicated to the shrine, and two dugout-canoes used in the Morotabune rite have been designated as [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Property]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/301/135 |title=Miho Jinja hōnōnarimono |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 January 2012}} ==References== {{神社 |名称= Miho Shrine |画像= [[File:Miho-jinja_haiden.jpg|250px|Haiden]] |所在地= [[Shimane Prefecture]], [[Matsue]], Mihonoseki-cho Mihonoseki 608 |位置= {{Coord|35|33|44.32|N|133|18|21.77|E|region:JP-32_type:landmark_scale:60000|display=inline,title|name=Miho Shrine}} |祭神= [[Kotoshironushi|Kotoshironushi-no-Kami]]
[[Mihotsuhime|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto]] |社格= [[Shikinai-sha|Shikinaisha]] (small)
former [[Kokuheichusha|National Intermediate Shrine]]
[[Bekkaku Kanpeisha|Bekkaku Shrine]] |創建= Unknown |札所等= [[Izumo no Kuni Shinpureijo]] #8 |例祭= [[April 7]] (Aoshikagaki Festival) |神事= Kamimukae Festival
Mushitaku Festival
Morotabune Festival |本殿= Miho-zukuri |地図= {{Switcher |{{Infobox mapframe|zoom=10|frame-width=180|type=point|marker=religious-shinto|shape-fill=#f5fffa|stroke-color=#006400|stroke-width=1|frame-latitude=35.508|frame-longitude=133.277}} |Wikimedia maps を表示 |{{Location map|Japan Shimane|float=center|width=180}} |島根県地図を表示 }} }} [[File:島根・美保神社の社紋.png|250px|thumb|Crest of Miho Shrine]] '''Miho Shrine''' (みほじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Matsue]], [[Shimane Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is a [[Shikinai-sha|Shikinaisha]], and its former rank was that of a [[Kokuheichusha|National Intermediate Shrine]]. The shrine is known for its deity of prosperity in business as Ebisu, and is also worshipped as a deity of fishing, maritime safety, and protection from pests in rice fields. Additionally, it is revered as a deity of musical instruments, leading to many offerings of musical instruments. == Deities == The right hall enshrines [[Kotoshironushi|Kotoshironushi-no-Kami]], a child of [[Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi-no-Kami]], and the left hall enshrines [[Mihotsuhime|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto]], the wife of Ōkuninushi-no-Kami. Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto is the consort of [[Ōmononushi|Ōmononushi-no-Kami]], the spirit of fortune and mystery, making her Kotoshironushi-no-Kami's stepmother. According to the ''[[Izumo no Kuni Fudoki]]'', ''Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto'', born to Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto (another name for Ōkuninushi-no-Kami) and Nunakawa-hime-no-Mikoto, resides in Miho no Sato. Originally, the shrine only enshrined Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto, but under the influence of the ''Kojiki'' and ''Nihon Shoki'' myths, it came to enshrine Kotoshironushi-no-Kami and Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto. == History == The exact origin of the shrine is unknown, but it is an ancient shrine listed in the ''[[Izumo no Kuni Fudoki]]'' compiled in the 8th century. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'' it is listed as a minor shrine. Since the medieval period, the Yokoyama clan has held hereditary control over the shrine. From the early modern period, it was said that visiting only the Grand Shrine (Izumo Taisha) was an incomplete pilgrimage, leading to an increase in visitors to both Izumo Taisha and Miho Shrine. Together, they are referred to as ''Izumo no Ebisu Daikoku''. In 1885 (Meiji 18), the shrine was ranked as a National Intermediate Shrine, and after World War II, it became a [[Bekkaku Kanpeisha|Bekkaku Shrine]] under the administration of the Association of Shinto Shrines. == Grounds == Miho-jinja-shaden.JPG|Shrine buildings Betsugo-nimishimae.JPG|Betsugo-nimishimae (Kotoshironushi-no-Ōkami) Betsugo-omishimae.JPG|Betsugo-omishimae (Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto) Miho-jinja-shinmon.JPG|Shinmon gate The current main shrine was rebuilt in 1813 (Bunka 10) after a fire in 1800 (Kansei 12). The shrine is in a unique style called ''Miho-zukuri'' or ''Hiyoku Taisha-zukuri'', which features two interconnected shrine buildings, and is designated as an Important Cultural Property of Japan. The origin of this style is unclear. A document from 1763 (Hōreki 13) called ''Hakusama Goyō no Oboe'' refers to the shrine as ''Miho Jinja'' in the 3rd year of Tenbun (1534), and as ''Miho Ryōsha'' in the 11th year of Tenshō (1583). According to the ''National Intermediate Shrine Miho Shrine Detailed Records'' from 1886 (Meiji 19), the main shrine was originally one building until it was destroyed during the wars of the Genki era (1570-1573). It was rebuilt in its current form with two interconnected buildings between 1593 and 1596 (Bunroku era). In 1928 (Shōwa 3), the shrine buildings were moved about 100 meters from their original location, and the grounds were expanded to their current form. The roofs of the main shrine, haiden, shinmon, corridors, and walls are currently made of cypress bark, but before the repairs, they were made of shingles. Between the two main shrines is a subsidiary shrine, Ōgo-sha, enshrining five deities. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === ; Buildings * Miho Shrine Main Shrine, including 18 ridge tags - Built in 1813 (Bunka 10) === Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Morotabune, 2 boats * Miho Shrine Dedicated Musical Instruments, 846 items * Soriko, 1 boat === Prefecturally Designated Tangible Cultural Properties === * Ink on Paper Hand Mirror (tekagami) ==== Prefecturally Designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties ==== * Abani, 1 boat (including 17 oars and 20 anchors) * Tomodo, 1 boat == Festivals == The Aoshikagaki Festival and the Morotabune Festival are based on the ''Kuniyuzuri'' myth. The December Morotabune Festival reenacts the story of Ōkuninushi-no-Kami sending a messenger to his son Kotoshironushi-no-Kami to consult on the transfer of the land, while the April Aoshikagaki Festival reenacts Kotoshironushi-no-Kami's decision to transfer the land and his subsequent revival as a deity. * [[January 1]] -- Saitansai * [[January 7]] -- Hatsuebisu Festival * Mid-January -- Bakuchiku-shiki (Tondosan) * [[February]] (Setsubun) -- Setsubunsai * [[April 7]] -- Annual Festival (Aoshikagaki Festival): The annual festival is held in the morning, and the Aoshikagaki Festival is held in the afternoon. * [[April 13]] -- Gyoko Festival * [[May 5]] -- Kamimukae Festival * [[August 7]] -- Mushitaku Festival * Mid-September -- Urajimai (performed by junior high school girls in traditional attire) * [[December 3]] -- Niiname Festival and Morotabune Festival === Namikiri Gohei and Tsukinami Gohei === ; Namikiri Gohei : Dedicated during the Aoshikagaki Festival. ; Tsukinami Gohei : Dedicated during the monthly festival held on the 7th of each month. == Access == From [[Matsue Station]], take the [[Ichibata Bus]] bound for Mihonoseki Terminal (approx. 40 minutes). Transfer to the Mihonoseki Community Bus at Mihonoseki Terminal and get off at the Mihonoseki stop (approx. 30 minutes). It is about a 1-minute walk from the Miho Shrine Entrance bus stop. During the New Year’s season, [[Golden Week]], Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays from summer to early winter, and on December 3rd, the direct bus "Ebisu Liner" runs from [[Yonago Airport]] and [[Sakaiminato Station]] operated by [[Hinomarubus|Hinomaru Bus]]. There is a parking lot (free, space for about a dozen cars) and a public restroom next to the community center, a 1-minute walk from the shrine. == Notes == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist}} == References == * [[Atsu Sone]] and [[Yoshihiko Umeda]], eds. ''Shinto Dictionary'' ([[Jinja Shinpō-sha]], 1968), p. 58 * [[Eiji Shirai]] and [[Masakuni Toki]], eds. ''Jinja Dictionary'' ([[Tōkyōdō Shuppan]], 1979), pp. 322-323 * [[Masaki Suda]], ''An Encyclopedia to Know Japanese Shrines'' ([[Nihon Bungeisha]], 1989), p. 203 * [[Shunpei Ueyama]] et al., ''Japanese Shrine Directory'' ([[Shin Jinbutsu Ōraisha]], 1992), pp. 238-239 * {{Cite book |和書 |author=Yasuhiro Nonomura|authorlink=野々村安浩 |chapter=The Origin of Miho Shrine |title=Quarterly Cultural Heritage April 2002 Issue|publisher=[[Soeisha]] |date=2002-4 |isbn=978-4-921070-13-7 |ref=Nonomura 2002 }} == See Also == {{Commons|Category:Miho-jinja}} * [[Hagoromo Legend]] * [[Miho Shrine (Shizuoka)]] * [[Izumo Taisha]] * [[Aoshi Ishidatami Street]] * [[Sunny Yokoyama]] - A descendant of the shrine’s priests, who became an aerobatic pilot and currently flies for [[Peach Aviation]]. == External Links == * [http://mihojinja.or.jp/ Miho Shrine Official Website] {{ja icon}} {{神道 横}} {{Normdaten}} {{shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:みほしんしや}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:National Intermediate Shrines]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines|*Miho Shrine]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties (buildings)]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Matsue]] [[Category:Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Shimane Prefecture designated tangible cultural properties]] [[Category:Prefectural designated tangible folk cultural properties]] [[Category:Edo period architecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Matsue]] [[Category:History of Matsue]] [[Category:Taisha-zukuri]] [[Category:Tourist attractions in Shimane Prefecture]] ==See also== * [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] * [[Modern system of ranked Shinto Shrines]] * [[Yaegaki Shrine|Yaegaki Jinja]] * [[Kamosu Jinja]] * [[Sada Jinja]] * [[Izumo Taisha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] ==References== {{Commons category|Miho-jinja}} {{Reflist}} {{Shinto shrine}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Uncategorized_Shinto_shrines]][[en:Miho Shrine]][[Category:Uncategorized_Shinto_shrines]] [[Category:Shikinai Shosha]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines]] [[Category:Shimane Prefecture designated tangible cultural property]] [[Category:Prefecture-designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Taisha-zukuri]] [[Category:Shinto]] [[ja:美保神社]] [[en:Miho Shrine]] {{Japan-religious-struct-stub}}

It is a [[Shikinai-sha|Shikinaisha]], and its former rank was that of a [[Kokuheichusha|National Intermediate Shrine]]. The shrine is known for its deity of prosperity in business as Ebisu, and is also worshipped as a deity of fishing, maritime safety, and protection from pests in rice fields. Additionally, it is revered as a deity of musical instruments, leading to many offerings of musical instruments. == Deities == The right hall enshrines [[Kotoshironushi|Kotoshironushi-no-Kami]], a child of [[Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi-no-Kami]], and the left hall enshrines [[Mihotsuhime|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto]], the wife of Ōkuninushi-no-Kami. Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto is the consort of [[Ōmononushi|Ōmononushi-no-Kami]], the spirit of fortune and mystery, making her Kotoshironushi-no-Kami's stepmother. According to the ''[[Izumo no Kuni Fudoki]]'', ''Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto'', born to Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto (another name for Ōkuninushi-no-Kami) and Nunakawa-hime-no-Mikoto, resides in Miho no Sato. Originally, the shrine only enshrined Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto, but under the influence of the ''Kojiki'' and ''Nihon Shoki'' myths, it came to enshrine Kotoshironushi-no-Kami and Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto. == History == The exact origin of the shrine is unknown, but it is an ancient shrine listed in the ''[[Izumo no Kuni Fudoki]]'' compiled in the 8th century. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'' it is listed as a minor shrine. Since the medieval period, the Yokoyama clan has held hereditary control over the shrine. From the early modern period, it was said that visiting only the Grand Shrine (Izumo Taisha) was an incomplete pilgrimage, leading to an increase in visitors to both Izumo Taisha and Miho Shrine. Together, they are referred to as ''Izumo no Ebisu Daikoku''. In 1885 (Meiji 18), the shrine was ranked as a National Intermediate Shrine, and after World War II, it became a [[Bekkaku Kanpeisha|Bekkaku Shrine]] under the administration of the Association of Shinto Shrines. == Grounds == Miho-jinja-shaden.JPG|Shrine buildings Betsugo-nimishimae.JPG|Betsugo-nimishimae (Kotoshironushi-no-Ōkami) Betsugo-omishimae.JPG|Betsugo-omishimae (Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto) Miho-jinja-shinmon.JPG|Shinmon gate The current main shrine was rebuilt in 1813 (Bunka 10) after a fire in 1800 (Kansei 12). The shrine is in a unique style called ''Miho-zukuri'' or ''Hiyoku Taisha-zukuri'', which features two interconnected shrine buildings, and is designated as an Important Cultural Property of Japan. The origin of this style is unclear. A document from 1763 (Hōreki 13) called ''Hakusama Goyō no Oboe'' refers to the shrine as ''Miho Jinja'' in the 3rd year of Tenbun (1534), and as ''Miho Ryōsha'' in the 11th year of Tenshō (1583). According to the ''National Intermediate Shrine Miho Shrine Detailed Records'' from 1886 (Meiji 19), the main shrine was originally one building until it was destroyed during the wars of the Genki era (1570-1573). It was rebuilt in its current form with two interconnected buildings between 1593 and 1596 (Bunroku era). In 1928 (Shōwa 3), the shrine buildings were moved about 100 meters from their original location, and the grounds were expanded to their current form. The roofs of the main shrine, haiden, shinmon, corridors, and walls are currently made of cypress bark, but before the repairs, they were made of shingles. {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Shimane Prefecture, Japan}} {{Use dmy dates|date=November 2019}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Miho Jinja
美保神社 | image = Mihojinja -01.jpg | caption = Miho Jinja | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|33|44|N|133|18|22|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Miho Jinja'''|美保神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] in [[Matsue, Shimane|Matsue]], [[Shimane Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. The [[Taisha-zukuri]] [[Honden]] of 1813 is an [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Cultural Property]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2968 |title=Miho Jinja Honden |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 January 2012}} A collection of 846 [[Traditional Japanese musical instruments|musical instruments]] dedicated to the shrine, and two dugout-canoes used in the Morotabune rite have been designated as [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Property]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/301/135 |title=Miho Jinja hōnōnarimono |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 January 2012}} ==References== {{神社 |名称= Miho Shrine |画像= [[File:Miho-jinja_haiden.jpg|250px|Haiden]] |所在地= [[Shimane Prefecture]], [[Matsue]], Mihonoseki-cho Mihonoseki 608 |位置= {{Coord|35|33|44.32|N|133|18|21.77|E|region:JP-32_type:landmark_scale:60000|display=inline,title|name=Miho Shrine}} |祭神= [[Kotoshironushi|Kotoshironushi-no-Kami]]
[[Mihotsuhime|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto]] |社格= [[Shikinai-sha|Shikinaisha]] (small)
former [[Kokuheichusha|National Intermediate Shrine]]
[[Bekkaku Kanpeisha|Bekkaku Shrine]] |創建= Unknown |札所等= [[Izumo no Kuni Shinpureijo]] #8 |例祭= [[April 7]] (Aoshikagaki Festival) |神事= Kamimukae Festival
Mushitaku Festival
Morotabune Festival |本殿= Miho-zukuri |地図= {{Switcher |{{Infobox mapframe|zoom=10|frame-width=180|type=point|marker=religious-shinto|shape-fill=#f5fffa|stroke-color=#006400|stroke-width=1|frame-latitude=35.508|frame-longitude=133.277}} |Wikimedia maps を表示 |{{Location map|Japan Shimane|float=center|width=180}} |島根県地図を表示 }} }} [[File:島根・美保神社の社紋.png|250px|thumb|Crest of Miho Shrine]] '''Miho Shrine''' (みほじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Matsue]], [[Shimane Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is a [[Shikinai-sha|Shikinaisha]], and its former rank was that of a [[Kokuheichusha|National Intermediate Shrine]]. The shrine is known for its deity of prosperity in business as Ebisu, and is also worshipped as a deity of fishing, maritime safety, and protection from pests in rice fields. Additionally, it is revered as a deity of musical instruments, leading to many offerings of musical instruments. == Deities == The right hall enshrines [[Kotoshironushi|Kotoshironushi-no-Kami]], a child of [[Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi-no-Kami]], and the left hall enshrines [[Mihotsuhime|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto]], the wife of Ōkuninushi-no-Kami. Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto is the consort of [[Ōmononushi|Ōmononushi-no-Kami]], the spirit of fortune and mystery, making her Kotoshironushi-no-Kami's stepmother. According to the ''[[Izumo no Kuni Fudoki]]'', ''Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto'', born to Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto (another name for Ōkuninushi-no-Kami) and Nunakawa-hime-no-Mikoto, resides in Miho no Sato. Originally, the shrine only enshrined Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto, but under the influence of the ''Kojiki'' and ''Nihon Shoki'' myths, it came to enshrine Kotoshironushi-no-Kami and Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto. == History == The exact origin of the shrine is unknown, but it is an ancient shrine listed in the ''[[Izumo no Kuni Fudoki]]'' compiled in the 8th century. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'' it is listed as a minor shrine. Since the medieval period, the Yokoyama clan has held hereditary control over the shrine. From the early modern period, it was said that visiting only the Grand Shrine (Izumo Taisha) was an incomplete pilgrimage, leading to an increase in visitors to both Izumo Taisha and Miho Shrine. Together, they are referred to as ''Izumo no Ebisu Daikoku''. In 1885 (Meiji 18), the shrine was ranked as a National Intermediate Shrine, and after World War II, it became a [[Bekkaku Kanpeisha|Bekkaku Shrine]] under the administration of the Association of Shinto Shrines. == Grounds == Miho-jinja-shaden.JPG|Shrine buildings Betsugo-nimishimae.JPG|Betsugo-nimishimae (Kotoshironushi-no-Ōkami) Betsugo-omishimae.JPG|Betsugo-omishimae (Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto) Miho-jinja-shinmon.JPG|Shinmon gate The current main shrine was rebuilt in 1813 (Bunka 10) after a fire in 1800 (Kansei 12). The shrine is in a unique style called ''Miho-zukuri'' or ''Hiyoku Taisha-zukuri'', which features two interconnected shrine buildings, and is designated as an Important Cultural Property of Japan. The origin of this style is unclear. A document from 1763 (Hōreki 13) called ''Hakusama Goyō no Oboe'' refers to the shrine as ''Miho Jinja'' in the 3rd year of Tenbun (1534), and as ''Miho Ryōsha'' in the 11th year of Tenshō (1583). According to the ''National Intermediate Shrine Miho Shrine Detailed Records'' from 1886 (Meiji 19), the main shrine was originally one building until it was destroyed during the wars of the Genki era (1570-1573). It was rebuilt in its current form with two interconnected buildings between 1593 and 1596 (Bunroku era). In 1928 (Shōwa 3), the shrine buildings were moved about 100 meters from their original location, and the grounds were expanded to their current form. The roofs of the main shrine, haiden, shinmon, corridors, and walls are currently made of cypress bark, but before the repairs, they were made of shingles. Between the two main shrines is a subsidiary shrine, Ōgo-sha, enshrining five deities. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === ; Buildings * Miho Shrine Main Shrine, including 18 ridge tags - Built in 1813 (Bunka 10) === Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Morotabune, 2 boats * Miho Shrine Dedicated Musical Instruments, 846 items * Soriko, 1 boat === Prefecturally Designated Tangible Cultural Properties === * Ink on Paper Hand Mirror (tekagami) ==== Prefecturally Designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties ==== * Abani, 1 boat (including 17 oars and 20 anchors) * Tomodo, 1 boat == Festivals == The Aoshikagaki Festival and the Morotabune Festival are based on the ''Kuniyuzuri'' myth. The December Morotabune Festival reenacts the story of Ōkuninushi-no-Kami sending a messenger to his son Kotoshironushi-no-Kami to consult on the transfer of the land, while the April Aoshikagaki Festival reenacts Kotoshironushi-no-Kami's decision to transfer the land and his subsequent revival as a deity. * [[January 1]] -- Saitansai * [[January 7]] -- Hatsuebisu Festival * Mid-January -- Bakuchiku-shiki (Tondosan) * [[February]] (Setsubun) -- Setsubunsai * [[April 7]] -- Annual Festival (Aoshikagaki Festival): The annual festival is held in the morning, and the Aoshikagaki Festival is held in the afternoon. * [[April 13]] -- Gyoko Festival * [[May 5]] -- Kamimukae Festival * [[August 7]] -- Mushitaku Festival * Mid-September -- Urajimai (performed by junior high school girls in traditional attire) * [[December 3]] -- Niiname Festival and Morotabune Festival === Namikiri Gohei and Tsukinami Gohei === ; Namikiri Gohei : Dedicated during the Aoshikagaki Festival. ; Tsukinami Gohei : Dedicated during the monthly festival held on the 7th of each month. == Access == From [[Matsue Station]], take the [[Ichibata Bus]] bound for Mihonoseki Terminal (approx. 40 minutes). Transfer to the Mihonoseki Community Bus at Mihonoseki Terminal and get off at the Mihonoseki stop (approx. 30 minutes). It is about a 1-minute walk from the Miho Shrine Entrance bus stop. During the New Year’s season, [[Golden Week]], Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays from summer to early winter, and on December 3rd, the direct bus "Ebisu Liner" runs from [[Yonago Airport]] and [[Sakaiminato Station]] operated by [[Hinomarubus|Hinomaru Bus]]. There is a parking lot (free, space for about a dozen cars) and a public restroom next to the community center, a 1-minute walk from the shrine. == Notes == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist}} == References == * [[Atsu Sone]] and [[Yoshihiko Umeda]], eds. ''Shinto Dictionary'' ([[Jinja Shinpō-sha]], 1968), p. 58 * [[Eiji Shirai]] and [[Masakuni Toki]], eds. ''Jinja Dictionary'' ([[Tōkyōdō Shuppan]], 1979), pp. 322-323 * [[Masaki Suda]], ''An Encyclopedia to Know Japanese Shrines'' ([[Nihon Bungeisha]], 1989), p. 203 * [[Shunpei Ueyama]] et al., ''Japanese Shrine Directory'' ([[Shin Jinbutsu Ōraisha]], 1992), pp. 238-239 * {{Cite book |和書 |author=Yasuhiro Nonomura|authorlink=野々村安浩 |chapter=The Origin of Miho Shrine |title=Quarterly Cultural Heritage April 2002 Issue|publisher=[[Soeisha]] |date=2002-4 |isbn=978-4-921070-13-7 |ref=Nonomura 2002 }} == See Also == {{Commons|Category:Miho-jinja}} * [[Hagoromo Legend]] * [[Miho Shrine (Shizuoka)]] * [[Izumo Taisha]] * [[Aoshi Ishidatami Street]] * [[Sunny Yokoyama]] - A descendant of the shrine’s priests, who became an aerobatic pilot and currently flies for [[Peach Aviation]]. == External Links == * [http://mihojinja.or.jp/ Miho Shrine Official Website] {{ja icon}} {{神道 横}} {{Normdaten}} {{shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:みほしんしや}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:National Intermediate Shrines]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines|*Miho Shrine]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties (buildings)]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Matsue]] [[Category:Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Shimane Prefecture designated tangible cultural properties]] [[Category:Prefectural designated tangible folk cultural properties]] [[Category:Edo period architecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Matsue]] [[Category:History of Matsue]] [[Category:Taisha-zukuri]] [[Category:Tourist attractions in Shimane Prefecture]] ==See also== * [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] * [[Modern system of ranked Shinto Shrines]] * [[Yaegaki Shrine|Yaegaki Jinja]] * [[Kamosu Jinja]] * [[Sada Jinja]] * [[Izumo Taisha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] ==References== {{Commons category|Miho-jinja}} {{Reflist}} {{Shinto shrine}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[en:Miho Shrine]][[Category:Shikinai Shosha]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines]] [[Category:Shimane Prefecture designated tangible cultural property]] [[Category:Prefecture-designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Taisha-zukuri]] [[Category:Shinto]] [[Category:Pages from wikipedia]] [[Category:Pages with hiragana sorting]] [[en:Miho Shrine]][[Category:Shinto]] [[Category:Expanded pages from wikipedia]] [[ja:美保神社]] [[en:Miho Shrine]] {{Japan-religious-struct-stub}}

美保神社 | image = Mihojinja -01.jpg | caption = Miho Jinja | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|33|44|N|133|18|22|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Miho Jinja'''|美保神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] in [[Matsue, Shimane|Matsue]], [[Shimane Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. The [[Taisha-zukuri]] [[Honden]] of 1813 is an [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Cultural Property]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2968 |title=Miho Jinja Honden |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 January 2012}} A collection of 846 [[Traditional Japanese musical instruments|musical instruments]] dedicated to the shrine, and two dugout-canoes used in the Morotabune rite have been designated as [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Property]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/301/135 |title=Miho Jinja hōnōnarimono |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 January 2012}} ==References== {{神社 |名称= Miho Shrine |画像= [[File:Miho-jinja_haiden.jpg|250px|Haiden]] |所在地= [[Shimane Prefecture]], [[Matsue]], Mihonoseki-cho Mihonoseki 608 |位置= {{Coord|35|33|44.32|N|133|18|21.77|E|region:JP-32_type:landmark_scale:60000|display=inline,title|name=Miho Shrine}} |祭神= [[Kotoshironushi|Kotoshironushi-no-Kami]]
[[Mihotsuhime|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto]] |社格= [[Shikinai-sha|Shikinaisha]] (small)
former [[Kokuheichusha|National Intermediate Shrine]]
[[Bekkaku Kanpeisha|Bekkaku Shrine]] |創建= Unknown |札所等= [[Izumo no Kuni Shinpureijo]] #8 |例祭= [[April 7]] (Aoshikagaki Festival) |神事= Kamimukae Festival
Mushitaku Festival
Morotabune Festival |本殿= Miho-zukuri |地図= {{Switcher |{{Infobox mapframe|zoom=10|frame-width=180|type=point|marker=religious-shinto|shape-fill=#f5fffa|stroke-color=#006400|stroke-width=1|frame-latitude=35.508|frame-longitude=133.277}} |Wikimedia maps を表示 |{{Location map|Japan Shimane|float=center|width=180}} |島根県地図を表示 }} }} [[File:島根・美保神社の社紋.png|250px|thumb|Crest of Miho Shrine]] '''Miho Shrine''' (みほじんじゃ) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Matsue]], [[Shimane Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is a [[Shikinai-sha|Shikinaisha]], and its former rank was that of a [[Kokuheichusha|National Intermediate Shrine]]. The shrine is known for its deity of prosperity in business as Ebisu, and is also worshipped as a deity of fishing, maritime safety, and protection from pests in rice fields. Additionally, it is revered as a deity of musical instruments, leading to many offerings of musical instruments. == Deities == The right hall enshrines [[Kotoshironushi|Kotoshironushi-no-Kami]], a child of [[Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi-no-Kami]], and the left hall enshrines [[Mihotsuhime|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto]], the wife of Ōkuninushi-no-Kami. Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto is the consort of [[Ōmononushi|Ōmononushi-no-Kami]], the spirit of fortune and mystery, making her Kotoshironushi-no-Kami's stepmother. According to the ''[[Izumo no Kuni Fudoki]]'', ''Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto'', born to Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto (another name for Ōkuninushi-no-Kami) and Nunakawa-hime-no-Mikoto, resides in Miho no Sato. Originally, the shrine only enshrined Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto, but under the influence of the ''Kojiki'' and ''Nihon Shoki'' myths, it came to enshrine Kotoshironushi-no-Kami and Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto. == History == The exact origin of the shrine is unknown, but it is an ancient shrine listed in the ''[[Izumo no Kuni Fudoki]]'' compiled in the 8th century. In the ''[[Engishiki]]'' it is listed as a minor shrine. Since the medieval period, the Yokoyama clan has held hereditary control over the shrine. From the early modern period, it was said that visiting only the Grand Shrine (Izumo Taisha) was an incomplete pilgrimage, leading to an increase in visitors to both Izumo Taisha and Miho Shrine. Together, they are referred to as ''Izumo no Ebisu Daikoku''. In 1885 (Meiji 18), the shrine was ranked as a National Intermediate Shrine, and after World War II, it became a [[Bekkaku Kanpeisha|Bekkaku Shrine]] under the administration of the Association of Shinto Shrines. == Grounds == Miho-jinja-shaden.JPG|Shrine buildings Betsugo-nimishimae.JPG|Betsugo-nimishimae (Kotoshironushi-no-Ōkami) Betsugo-omishimae.JPG|Betsugo-omishimae (Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto) Miho-jinja-shinmon.JPG|Shinmon gate The current main shrine was rebuilt in 1813 (Bunka 10) after a fire in 1800 (Kansei 12). The shrine is in a unique style called ''Miho-zukuri'' or ''Hiyoku Taisha-zukuri'', which features two interconnected shrine buildings, and is designated as an Important Cultural Property of Japan. The origin of this style is unclear. A document from 1763 (Hōreki 13) called ''Hakusama Goyō no Oboe'' refers to the shrine as ''Miho Jinja'' in the 3rd year of Tenbun (1534), and as ''Miho Ryōsha'' in the 11th year of Tenshō (1583). According to the ''National Intermediate Shrine Miho Shrine Detailed Records'' from 1886 (Meiji 19), the main shrine was originally one building until it was destroyed during the wars of the Genki era (1570-1573). It was rebuilt in its current form with two interconnected buildings between 1593 and 1596 (Bunroku era). In 1928 (Shōwa 3), the shrine buildings were moved about 100 meters from their original location, and the grounds were expanded to their current form. The roofs of the main shrine, haiden, shinmon, corridors, and walls are currently made of cypress bark, but before the repairs, they were made of shingles. Between the two main shrines is a subsidiary shrine, Ōgo-sha, enshrining five deities. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === ; Buildings * Miho Shrine Main Shrine, including 18 ridge tags - Built in 1813 (Bunka 10) === Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Morotabune, 2 boats * Miho Shrine Dedicated Musical Instruments, 846 items * Soriko, 1 boat === Prefecturally Designated Tangible Cultural Properties === * Ink on Paper Hand Mirror (tekagami) ==== Prefecturally Designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties ==== * Abani, 1 boat (including 17 oars and 20 anchors) * Tomodo, 1 boat == Festivals == The Aoshikagaki Festival and the Morotabune Festival are based on the ''Kuniyuzuri'' myth. The December Morotabune Festival reenacts the story of Ōkuninushi-no-Kami sending a messenger to his son Kotoshironushi-no-Kami to consult on the transfer of the land, while the April Aoshikagaki Festival reenacts Kotoshironushi-no-Kami's decision to transfer the land and his subsequent revival as a deity. * [[January 1]] -- Saitansai * [[January 7]] -- Hatsuebisu Festival * Mid-January -- Bakuchiku-shiki (Tondosan) * [[February]] (Setsubun) -- Setsubunsai * [[April 7]] -- Annual Festival (Aoshikagaki Festival): The annual festival is held in the morning, and the Aoshikagaki Festival is held in the afternoon. * [[April 13]] -- Gyoko Festival * [[May 5]] -- Kamimukae Festival * [[August 7]] -- Mushitaku Festival * Mid-September -- Urajimai (performed by junior high school girls in traditional attire) * [[December 3]] -- Niiname Festival and Morotabune Festival === Namikiri Gohei and Tsukinami Gohei === ; Namikiri Gohei : Dedicated during the Aoshikagaki Festival. ; Tsukinami Gohei : Dedicated during the monthly festival held on the 7th of each month. == Access == From [[Matsue Station]], take the [[Ichibata Bus]] bound for Mihonoseki Terminal (approx. 40 minutes). Transfer to the Mihonoseki Community Bus at Mihonoseki Terminal and get off at the Mihonoseki stop (approx. 30 minutes). It is about a 1-minute walk from the Miho Shrine Entrance bus stop. During the New Year’s season, [[Golden Week]], Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays from summer to early winter, and on December 3rd, the direct bus "Ebisu Liner" runs from [[Yonago Airport]] and [[Sakaiminato Station]] operated by [[Hinomarubus|Hinomaru Bus]]. There is a parking lot (free, space for about a dozen cars) and a public restroom next to the community center, a 1-minute walk from the shrine. == Notes == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist}} == References == * [[Atsu Sone]] and [[Yoshihiko Umeda]], eds. ''Shinto Dictionary'' ([[Jinja Shinpō-sha]], 1968), p. 58 * [[Eiji Shirai]] and [[Masakuni Toki]], eds. ''Jinja Dictionary'' ([[Tōkyōdō Shuppan]], 1979), pp. 322-323 * [[Masaki Suda]], ''An Encyclopedia to Know Japanese Shrines'' ([[Nihon Bungeisha]], 1989), p. 203 * [[Shunpei Ueyama]] et al., ''Japanese Shrine Directory'' ([[Shin Jinbutsu Ōraisha]], 1992), pp. 238-239 * {{Cite book |和書 |author=Yasuhiro Nonomura|authorlink=野々村安浩 |chapter=The Origin of Miho Shrine |title=Quarterly Cultural Heritage April 2002 Issue|publisher=[[Soeisha]] |date=2002-4 |isbn=978-4-921070-13-7 |ref=Nonomura 2002 }} == See Also == {{Commons|Category:Miho-jinja}} * [[Hagoromo Legend]] * [[Miho Shrine (Shizuoka)]] * [[Izumo Taisha]] * [[Aoshi Ishidatami Street]] * [[Sunny Yokoyama]] - A descendant of the shrine’s priests, who became an aerobatic pilot and currently flies for [[Peach Aviation]]. == External Links == * [http://mihojinja.or.jp/ Miho Shrine Official Website] {{ja icon}} {{神道 横}} {{Normdaten}} {{shinto-stub}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:National Intermediate Shrines]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines|*Miho Shrine]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties (buildings)]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Matsue]] [[Category:Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Shimane Prefecture designated tangible cultural properties]] [[Category:Prefectural designated tangible folk cultural properties]] [[Category:Edo period architecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Matsue]] [[Category:History of Matsue]] [[Category:Taisha-zukuri]] [[Category:Tourist attractions in Shimane Prefecture]] ==See also== * [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] * [[Modern system of ranked Shinto Shrines]] * [[Yaegaki Shrine|Yaegaki Jinja]] * [[Kamosu Jinja]] * [[Sada Jinja]] * [[Izumo Taisha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] ==References== {{Commons category|Miho-jinja}} {{Reflist}} {{Shinto shrine}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[en:Miho Shrine]][[Category:Shikinai Shosha]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines]] [[Category:Shimane Prefecture designated tangible cultural property]] [[Category:Prefecture-designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Taisha-zukuri]] [[Category:Shinto]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from wikipedia]] [[Category:Pages with hiragana sorting]] [[en:Miho Shrine]][[Category:Shinto]] [[Category:Expanded pages from wikipedia]] [[ja:美保神社]] [[en:Miho Shrine]] {{Japan-religious-struct-stub}}

Haiden | Location = {{nihongo|Miho Sekicho, Matsue City, Shimane Prefecture|島根県松江市美保関町美保関608}} | Coordinates = {{Coord|35|33|44.32|N|133|18|21.77|E|region:JP-32_type:landmark_scale:60000|display=inline,title|name=Miho Shrine}} | Deities = {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神}}
{{ill|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|三穂津姫命}} | Shrine Rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine)
Former {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社}}
{{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} | Founded = Unknown | Pilgrimage Sites = {{ill|Izumo Province Kami-Buddha Pilgrimage|ja|出雲國神仏霊場}} #8 | Main Festival = {{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}} (Aoshibagaki Festival) | Rituals = Kami-Mukae Festival, Mushi-Sagashi Festival, Morotabune Festival | Honden = Miho-zukuri | Map = {{Location map|Japan Shimane|label=美保神社|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|position=left|float=center|width=180|caption=Miho Shrine}} }} '''Miho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|美保神社}}, {{nihongo|Miho-jinja}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{nihongo|Miho Sekicho, Matsue City, Shimane Prefecture|島根県松江市美保関町}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} and a former {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社}}. The shrine is revered as the home of {{ill|Ebisu (mythology)|ja|えびす}}, a deity of prosperity, fishing, and agriculture, and is also regarded as a guardian of musical instruments. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神}} in the right honden and {{ill|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|三穂津姫命}} in the left honden. Mihotsuhime is considered the consort of {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主神}}, the deity of prosperity and wonder, while Kotoshironushi is their son. According to the {{ill|Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|出雲国風土記}}, the original deity worshipped here was {{nihongo|Mihosusumi-no-Mikoto|御穂須須美命}}, who was later syncretized with Kotoshironushi and Mihotsuhime. == History == The shrine's origins are unclear, but it is mentioned in the {{ill|Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|出雲国風土記}} (8th century). During the medieval period, the {{ill|Yokoyama clan|ja|横山氏}} served as hereditary priests. By the Edo period, Miho Shrine gained prominence as a companion shrine to {{ill|Izumo Taisha|ja|出雲大社}}, and it became customary to visit both shrines during pilgrimages. In 1885 (Meiji 18), Miho Shrine was designated as a {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社}}, and after World War II, it was listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. == Grounds == File:美保神社社殿.JPG|Main Shrine File:別号二御前.JPG|Right Honden (Kotoshironushi) File:別号大御前.JPG|Left Honden (Mihotsuhime) File:美保神社神門.JPG|Shrine Gate The current honden was reconstructed in 1813 (Bunka 10) after a fire in 1800 (Kansei 12). The shrine features a unique architectural style called {{nihongo|Miho-zukuri|美保造}} or {{nihongo|Biyoku Taisha-zukuri|比翼大社造}}, a variation of {{ill|Taisha-zukuri|ja|大社造}}. The shrine buildings, including the honden, haiden, and gate, are designated as {{ill|Important Cultural Properties of Japan|ja|重要文化財}}. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National) === * Miho Shrine Main Shrine (Honden), including 18 plaques (1813) === National Tangible Folk Cultural Properties === * {{nihongo|Morotabune Boats|諸手船}} (2) * 846 ceremonial instruments * Soriko Boat (1) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Calligraphy handscroll (Tekagami) == Festivals and Rituals == 1. **Aoshibagaki Festival** ({{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}}): This festival reenacts the myth where {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神}} secluded himself within a fence made of green twigs during the {{ill|Kuniyuzuri|ja|国譲り}} myth. 2. **Morotabune Festival** ({{nihongo|December 3|12月3日}}): Reenacts {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主}} consulting Kotoshironushi about ceding the land to the {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神}}. == Transportation == The shrine can be reached by the {{nihongo|Ichibata Bus|一畑バス}} from Matsue Station (about 40 minutes). Visitors can transfer to a community bus at Miho Shrine's terminal stop and reach the shrine entrance in 1 minute on foot. == References == {{Reflist}} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Izumo Taisha|ja|出雲大社}} * {{ill|Kuniyuzuri|ja|国譲り}} * {{ill|Ebisu (mythology)|ja|えびす}} * {{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市}} == External Links == * [http://mihojinja.or.jp/ Official Website] ({{lang|ja|Japanese}}) == See Also == {{Commons|Category:Miho-jinja}} * [[Hagoromo Legend]] * [[Miho Shrine (Shizuoka)]] * [[Izumo Taisha]] * [[Aoshi Ishidatami Street]] * [[Sunny Yokoyama]] - A descendant of the shrine’s priests, who became an aerobatic pilot and currently flies for [[Peach Aviation]]. == External Links == * [http://mihojinja.or.jp/ Miho Shrine Official Website] {{ja icon}} {{神道 横}} {{Normdaten}} {{shinto-stub}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:National Intermediate Shrines]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines|*Miho Shrine]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties (buildings)]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Matsue]] [[Category:Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Shimane Prefecture designated tangible cultural properties]] [[Category:Prefectural designated tangible folk cultural properties]] [[Category:Edo period architecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Matsue]] [[Category:History of Matsue]] [[Category:Taisha-zukuri]] [[Category:Tourist attractions in Shimane Prefecture]] ==See also== * [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] * [[Modern system of ranked Shinto Shrines]] * [[Yaegaki Shrine|Yaegaki Jinja]] * [[Kamosu Jinja]] * [[Sada Jinja]] * [[Izumo Taisha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] ==References== {{Commons category|Miho-jinja}} {{Reflist}} {{Shinto shrine}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[en:Miho Shrine]][[Category:Shikinai Shosha]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines]] [[Category:Shimane Prefecture designated tangible cultural property]] [[Category:Prefecture-designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Taisha-zukuri]] [[Category:Shinto]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from wikipedia]] [[en:Miho Shrine]][[Category:Shinto]] [[Category:Expanded pages from wikipedia]] [[ja:美保神社]] [[en:Miho Shrine]] {{Japan-religious-struct-stub}}

The [[Taisha-zukuri]] [[Honden]] of 1813 is an [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Cultural Property]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2968 |title=Miho Jinja Honden |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 January 2012}} A collection of 846 [[Traditional Japanese musical instruments|musical instruments]] dedicated to the shrine, and two dugout-canoes used in the Morotabune rite have been designated as [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Property]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/301/135 |title=Miho Jinja hōnōnarimono |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 January 2012}} ==References== {{Infobox Shinto shrine | name = Miho Shrine | image = [[File:Miho-jinja_haiden.jpg|250px|Haiden]]
Haiden | Location = {{nihongo|Miho Sekicho, Matsue City, Shimane Prefecture|島根県松江市美保関町美保関608}} | coordinates = {{Coord|35|33|44.32|N|133|18|21.77|E|region:JP-32_type:landmark_scale:60000|display=inline,title|name=Miho Shrine}} | Deities = {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神}}
{{ill|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|三穂津姫命}} | Shrine Rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine)
Former {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社}}
{{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} | founded = Unknown | Pilgrimage Sites = {{ill|Izumo Province Kami-Buddha Pilgrimage|ja|出雲國神仏霊場}} #8 | Main Festival = {{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}} (Aoshibagaki Festival) | Rituals = Kami-Mukae Festival, Mushi-Sagashi Festival, Morotabune Festival | Honden = Miho-zukuri | Map = {{Location map|Japan Shimane|label=美保神社|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|position=left|float=center|width=180|caption=Miho Shrine}} }} '''Miho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|美保神社}}, {{nihongo|Miho-jinja}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{nihongo|Miho Sekicho, Matsue City, Shimane Prefecture|島根県松江市美保関町}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} and a former {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社}}. The shrine is revered as the home of {{ill|Ebisu (mythology)|ja|えびす}}, a deity of prosperity, fishing, and agriculture, and is also regarded as a guardian of musical instruments. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神}} in the right honden and {{ill|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|三穂津姫命}} in the left honden. Mihotsuhime is considered the consort of {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主神}}, the deity of prosperity and wonder, while Kotoshironushi is their son. According to the {{ill|Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|出雲国風土記}}, the original deity worshipped here was {{nihongo|Mihosusumi-no-Mikoto|御穂須須美命}}, who was later syncretized with Kotoshironushi and Mihotsuhime. == History == The shrine's origins are unclear, but it is mentioned in the {{ill|Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|出雲国風土記}} (8th century). During the medieval period, the {{ill|Yokoyama clan|ja|横山氏}} served as hereditary priests. By the Edo period, Miho Shrine gained prominence as a companion shrine to {{ill|Izumo Taisha|ja|出雲大社}}, and it became customary to visit both shrines during pilgrimages. In 1885 (Meiji 18), Miho Shrine was designated as a {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社}}, and after World War II, it was listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. == Grounds == File:美保神社社殿.JPG|Main Shrine File:別号二御前.JPG|Right Honden (Kotoshironushi) File:別号大御前.JPG|Left Honden (Mihotsuhime) File:美保神社神門.JPG|Shrine Gate The current honden was reconstructed in 1813 (Bunka 10) after a fire in 1800 (Kansei 12). The shrine features a unique architectural style called {{nihongo|Miho-zukuri|美保造}} or {{nihongo|Biyoku Taisha-zukuri|比翼大社造}}, a variation of {{ill|Taisha-zukuri|ja|大社造}}. The shrine buildings, including the honden, haiden, and gate, are designated as {{ill|Important Cultural Properties of Japan|ja|重要文化財}}. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National) === * Miho Shrine Main Shrine (Honden), including 18 plaques (1813) === National Tangible Folk Cultural Properties === * {{nihongo|Morotabune Boats|諸手船}} (2) * 846 ceremonial instruments * Soriko Boat (1) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Calligraphy handscroll (Tekagami) == Festivals and Rituals == 1. **Aoshibagaki Festival** ({{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}}): This festival reenacts the myth where {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神}} secluded himself within a fence made of green twigs during the {{ill|Kuniyuzuri|ja|国譲り}} myth. 2. **Morotabune Festival** ({{nihongo|December 3|12月3日}}): Reenacts {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主}} consulting Kotoshironushi about ceding the land to the {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神}}. == Transportation == The shrine can be reached by the {{nihongo|Ichibata Bus|一畑バス}} from Matsue Station (about 40 minutes). Visitors can transfer to a community bus at Miho Shrine's terminal stop and reach the shrine entrance in 1 minute on foot. == References == {{Reflist}} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Izumo Taisha|ja|出雲大社}} * {{ill|Kuniyuzuri|ja|国譲り}} * {{ill|Ebisu (mythology)|ja|えびす}} * {{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市}} == External Links == * [http://mihojinja.or.jp/ Official Website] ({{lang|ja|Japanese}}) == See Also == {{Commons|Category:Miho-jinja}} * {{ill|Hagoromo Legend|ja|羽衣伝説}} * {{ill|Miho Shrine (Shizuoka)|ja|御穂神社}} * [[Izumo Taisha]] * {{ill|Aoshi Ishidatami Street|ja|青石畳通り}} * {{ill|Sunny Yokoyama|ja|サニー横山}} - A descendant of the shrine’s priests, who became an aerobatic pilot and currently flies for [[Peach Aviation]]. == External Links == * [http://mihojinja.or.jp/ Miho Shrine Official Website] {{ja icon}} {{神道 横}} {{Normdaten}} {{shinto-stub}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:National Intermediate Shrines]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines|*Miho Shrine]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties (buildings)]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Matsue]] [[Category:Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Shimane Prefecture designated tangible cultural properties]] [[Category:Prefectural designated tangible folk cultural properties]] [[Category:Edo period architecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Matsue]] [[Category:History of Matsue]] [[Category:Taisha-zukuri]] [[Category:Tourist attractions in Shimane Prefecture]] ==See also== * [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] * [[Modern system of ranked Shinto Shrines]] * [[Yaegaki Shrine|Yaegaki Jinja]] * [[Kamosu Jinja]] * [[Sada Jinja]] * [[Izumo Taisha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] ==References== {{Commons category|Miho-jinja}} {{Reflist}} {{Shinto shrine}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[en:Miho Shrine]][[Category:Shikinai Shosha]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines]] [[Category:Shimane Prefecture designated tangible cultural property]] [[Category:Prefecture-designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Taisha-zukuri]] [[Category:Shinto]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from wikipedia]] [[en:Miho Shrine]][[Category:Shinto]] [[Category:Expanded pages from wikipedia]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from wikipedia5]][[en:Miho Shrine]][[Category:Pages and Categories from wikipedia5]] [[ja:美保神社]] [[en:Miho Shrine]] {{Japan-religious-struct-stub}}

According to the {{ill|Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|出雲国風土記}}, the original deity worshipped here was {{nihongo|Mihosusumi-no-Mikoto|御穂須須美命}}, who was later syncretized with Kotoshironushi and Mihotsuhime. == History == The shrine's origins are unclear, but it is mentioned in the {{ill|Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|出雲国風土記}} (8th century). During the medieval period, the {{ill|Yokoyama clan|ja|横山氏}} served as hereditary priests. By the Edo period, Miho Shrine gained prominence as a companion shrine to {{ill|Izumo Taisha|ja|出雲大社}}, and it became customary to visit both shrines during pilgrimages. In 1885 (Meiji 18), Miho Shrine was designated as a {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社}}, and after World War II, it was listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. == Grounds == File:美保神社社殿.JPG|Main Shrine File:別号二御前.JPG|Right Honden (Kotoshironushi) File:別号大御前.JPG|Left Honden (Mihotsuhime) File:美保神社神門.JPG|Shrine Gate The current honden was reconstructed in 1813 (Bunka 10) after a fire in 1800 (Kansei 12). The shrine features a unique architectural style called {{nihongo|Miho-zukuri|美保造}} or {{nihongo|Biyoku Taisha-zukuri|比翼大社造}}, a variation of {{ill|Taisha-zukuri|ja|大社造}}. The shrine buildings, including the honden, haiden, and gate, are designated as {{ill|Important Cultural Properties of Japan|ja|重要文化財}}. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National) === * Miho Shrine Main Shrine (Honden), including 18 plaques (1813) === National Tangible Folk Cultural Properties === * {{nihongo|Morotabune Boats|諸手船}} (2) * 846 ceremonial instruments * Soriko Boat (1) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Calligraphy handscroll (Tekagami) == festivals and Rituals == 1. **Aoshibagaki festival** ({{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}}): This festival reenacts the myth where {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神}} secluded himself within a fence made of green twigs during the {{ill|Kuniyuzuri|ja|国譲り}} myth. 2. **Morotabune festival** ({{nihongo|December 3|12月3日}}): Reenacts {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主}} consulting Kotoshironushi about ceding the land to the {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神}}. == Transportation == The shrine can be reached by the {{nihongo|Ichibata Bus|一畑バス}} from Matsue Station (about 40 minutes). {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} | founded = Unknown | Pilgrimage Sites = {{ill|Izumo Province Kami-Buddha Pilgrimage|ja|出雲國神仏霊場}} #8 | Main festival = {{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}} (Aoshibagaki festival) | Rituals = Kami-Mukae festival, Mushi-Sagashi festival, Morotabune festival | Honden = Miho-zukuri | map = {{location map|Japan Shimane|label=美保神社|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|position=left|float=center|width=180|caption=Miho Shrine}} }} '''Miho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|美保神社}}, {{nihongo|Miho-jinja}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{nihongo|Miho Sekicho, Matsue City, Shimane Prefecture|島根県松江市美保関町}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} and a former {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社}}. The shrine is revered as the home of {{ill|Ebisu (mythology)|ja|えびす}}, a deity of prosperity, fishing, and agriculture, and is also regarded as a guardian of musical instruments. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神}} in the right honden and {{ill|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|三穂津姫命}} in the left honden. Mihotsuhime is considered the consort of {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主神}}, the deity of prosperity and wonder, while Kotoshironushi is their son. According to the {{ill|Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|出雲国風土記}}, the original deity worshipped here was {{nihongo|Mihosusumi-no-Mikoto|御穂須須美命}}, who was later syncretized with Kotoshironushi and Mihotsuhime. == History == The shrine's origins are unclear, but it is mentioned in the {{ill|Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|出雲国風土記}} (8th century). During the medieval period, the {{ill|Yokoyama clan|ja|横山氏}} served as hereditary priests. By the Edo period, Miho Shrine gained prominence as a companion shrine to {{ill|Izumo Taisha|ja|出雲大社}}, and it became customary to visit both shrines during pilgrimages. In 1885 (Meiji 18), Miho Shrine was designated as a {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社}}, and after World War II, it was listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. == Grounds == File:美保神社社殿.JPG|Main Shrine File:別号二御前.JPG|Right Honden (Kotoshironushi) File:別号大御前.JPG|Left Honden (Mihotsuhime) File:美保神社神門.JPG|Shrine Gate The current honden was reconstructed in 1813 (Bunka 10) after a fire in 1800 (Kansei 12). The shrine features a unique architectural style called {{nihongo|Miho-zukuri|美保造}} or {{nihongo|Biyoku Taisha-zukuri|比翼大社造}}, a variation of {{ill|Taisha-zukuri|ja|大社造}}. The shrine buildings, including the honden, haiden, and gate, are designated as {{ill|Important Cultural Properties of Japan|ja|重要文化財}}. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National) === * Miho Shrine Main Shrine (Honden), including 18 plaques (1813) === National Tangible Folk Cultural Properties === * {{nihongo|Morotabune Boats|諸手船}} (2) * 846 ceremonial instruments * Soriko Boat (1) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Calligraphy handscroll (Tekagami) == festivals and Rituals == 1. **Aoshibagaki festival** ({{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}}): This festival reenacts the myth where {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神}} secluded himself within a fence made of green twigs during the {{ill|Kuniyuzuri|ja|国譲り}} myth. 2. **Morotabune festival** ({{nihongo|December 3|12月3日}}): Reenacts {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主}} consulting Kotoshironushi about ceding the land to the {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神}}. == Transportation == The shrine can be reached by the {{nihongo|Ichibata Bus|一畑バス}} from Matsue Station (about 40 minutes). Visitors can transfer to a community bus at Miho Shrine's terminal stop and reach the shrine entrance in 1 minute on foot. == References == {{Reflist}} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Izumo Taisha|ja|出雲大社}} * {{ill|Kuniyuzuri|ja|国譲り}} * {{ill|Ebisu (mythology)|ja|えびす}} * {{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市}} == External Links == * [http://mihojinja.or.jp/ Official Website] ({{lang|ja|Japanese}}) == See Also == {{Commons|Category:Miho-jinja}} * {{ill|Hagoromo Legend|ja|羽衣伝説}} * {{ill|Miho Shrine (Shizuoka)|ja|御穂神社}} * [[Izumo Taisha]] * {{ill|Aoshi Ishidatami Street|ja|青石畳通り}} * {{ill|Sunny Yokoyama|ja|サニー横山}} - A descendant of the shrine’s priests, who became an aerobatic pilot and currently flies for [[Peach Aviation]]. == External Links == * [http://mihojinja.or.jp/ Miho Shrine Official Website] {{ja icon}} {{神道 横}} {{Normdaten}} {{shinto-stub}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:National Intermediate Shrines]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines|*Miho Shrine]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties (buildings)]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Matsue]] [[Category:Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Shimane Prefecture designated tangible cultural properties]] [[Category:Prefectural designated tangible folk cultural properties]] [[Category:Edo period architecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Matsue]] [[Category:History of Matsue]] [[Category:Taisha-zukuri]] [[Category:Tourist attractions in Shimane Prefecture]] ==See also== * [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] * [[Modern system of ranked Shinto Shrines]] * [[Yaegaki Shrine|Yaegaki Jinja]] * [[Kamosu Jinja]] * [[Sada Jinja]] * [[Izumo Taisha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] ==References== {{Commons category|Miho-jinja}} {{Reflist}} {{Shinto shrine}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[en:Miho Shrine]][[Category:Shikinai Shosha]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines]] [[Category:Shimane Prefecture designated tangible cultural property]] [[Category:Prefecture-designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Taisha-zukuri]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from wikipedia]] [[en:Miho Shrine]][[Category:Expanded pages from wikipedia]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from wikipedia5]][[en:Miho Shrine]][[Category:Pages and Categories from wikipedia5]] [[ja:美保神社]] [[en:Miho Shrine]] {{Japan-religious-struct-stub}}

The [[Taisha-zukuri]] [[Honden]] of 1813 is an [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Cultural Property]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2968 |title=Miho Jinja Honden |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 January 2012}} A collection of 846 [[Traditional Japanese musical instruments|musical instruments]] dedicated to the shrine, and two dugout-canoes used in the Morotabune rite have been designated as [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Property]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/301/135 |title=Miho Jinja hōnōnarimono |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 January 2012}} ==References== {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miho Shrine | image = [[File:Miho-jinja_haiden.jpg|250px|Haiden]]
Haiden | location = {{nihongo|Miho Sekicho, Matsue City, Shimane Prefecture|島根県松江市美保関町美保関608}} | coordinates = {{Coord|35|33|44.32|N|133|18|21.77|E|region:JP-32_type:landmark_scale:60000|display=inline,title|name=Miho Shrine}} | deity = {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神}}
{{ill|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|三穂津姫命}} | Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (Minor Shrine)
Former {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社}}
{{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} | founded = Unknown | Pilgrimage Sites = {{ill|Izumo Province Kami-Buddha Pilgrimage|ja|出雲國神仏霊場}} #8 | Main festival = {{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}} (Aoshibagaki festival) | Rituals = Kami-Mukae festival, Mushi-Sagashi festival, Morotabune festival | Honden = Miho-zukuri | map = {{location map|Japan Shimane|label=美保神社|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|position=left|float=center|width=180|caption=Miho Shrine}} }} '''Miho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|美保神社}}, {{nihongo|Miho-jinja}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{nihongo|Miho Sekicho, Matsue City, Shimane Prefecture|島根県松江市美保関町}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} and a former {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社}}. The shrine is revered as the home of {{ill|Ebisu (mythology)|ja|えびす}}, a deity of prosperity, fishing, and agriculture, and is also regarded as a guardian of musical instruments. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神}} in the right honden and {{ill|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|三穂津姫命}} in the left honden. Mihotsuhime is considered the consort of {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主神}}, the deity of prosperity and wonder, while Kotoshironushi is their son. According to the {{ill|Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|出雲国風土記}}, the original deity worshipped here was {{nihongo|Mihosusumi-no-Mikoto|御穂須須美命}}, who was later syncretized with Kotoshironushi and Mihotsuhime. == History == The shrine's origins are unclear, but it is mentioned in the {{ill|Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|出雲国風土記}} (8th century). During the medieval period, the {{ill|Yokoyama clan|ja|横山氏}} served as hereditary priests. By the Edo period, Miho Shrine gained prominence as a companion shrine to {{ill|Izumo Taisha|ja|出雲大社}}, and it became customary to visit both shrines during pilgrimages. In 1885 (Meiji 18), Miho Shrine was designated as a {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社}}, and after World War II, it was listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. == Grounds == File:美保神社社殿.JPG|Main Shrine File:別号二御前.JPG|Right Honden (Kotoshironushi) File:別号大御前.JPG|Left Honden (Mihotsuhime) File:美保神社神門.JPG|Shrine Gate The current honden was reconstructed in 1813 (Bunka 10) after a fire in 1800 (Kansei 12). The shrine features a unique architectural style called {{nihongo|Miho-zukuri|美保造}} or {{nihongo|Biyoku Taisha-zukuri|比翼大社造}}, a variation of {{ill|Taisha-zukuri|ja|大社造}}. The shrine buildings, including the honden, haiden, and gate, are designated as {{ill|Important Cultural Properties of Japan|ja|重要文化財}}. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National) === * Miho Shrine Main Shrine (Honden), including 18 plaques (1813) === National Tangible Folk Cultural Properties === * {{nihongo|Morotabune Boats|諸手船}} (2) * 846 ceremonial instruments * Soriko Boat (1) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Calligraphy handscroll (Tekagami) == festivals and Rituals == 1. **Aoshibagaki festival** ({{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}}): This festival reenacts the myth where {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神}} secluded himself within a fence made of green twigs during the {{ill|Kuniyuzuri|ja|国譲り}} myth. 2. **Morotabune festival** ({{nihongo|December 3|12月3日}}): Reenacts {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主}} consulting Kotoshironushi about ceding the land to the {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神}}. == Transportation == The shrine can be reached by the {{nihongo|Ichibata Bus|一畑バス}} from Matsue Station (about 40 minutes). Visitors can transfer to a community bus at Miho Shrine's terminal stop and reach the shrine entrance in 1 minute on foot. == References == {{Reflist}} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Izumo Taisha|ja|出雲大社}} * {{ill|Kuniyuzuri|ja|国譲り}} * {{ill|Ebisu (mythology)|ja|えびす}} * {{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市}} == External Links == * [http://mihojinja.or.jp/ Official Website] ({{lang|ja|Japanese}}) == See Also == {{Commons|Category:Miho-jinja}} * {{ill|Hagoromo Legend|ja|羽衣伝説}} * {{ill|Miho Shrine (Shizuoka)|ja|御穂神社}} * [[Izumo Taisha]] * {{ill|Aoshi Ishidatami Street|ja|青石畳通り}} * {{ill|Sunny Yokoyama|ja|サニー横山}} - A descendant of the shrine’s priests, who became an aerobatic pilot and currently flies for [[Peach Aviation]]. == External Links == * [http://mihojinja.or.jp/ Miho Shrine Official Website] {{ja icon}} {{神道 横}} {{Normdaten}} {{shinto-stub}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:National Intermediate Shrines]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines|*Miho Shrine]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties (buildings)]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Matsue]] [[Category:Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Shimane Prefecture designated tangible cultural properties]] [[Category:Prefectural designated tangible folk cultural properties]] [[Category:Edo period architecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Matsue]] [[Category:History of Matsue]] [[Category:Taisha-zukuri]] [[Category:Tourist attractions in Shimane Prefecture]] ==See also== * [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] * [[Modern system of ranked Shinto Shrines]] * [[Yaegaki Shrine|Yaegaki Jinja]] * [[Kamosu Jinja]] * [[Sada Jinja]] * [[Izumo Taisha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] ==References== {{Commons category|Miho-jinja}} {{Reflist}} {{Shinto shrine}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[en:Miho Shrine]][[Category:Shikinai Shosha]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines]] [[Category:Shimane Prefecture designated tangible cultural property]] [[Category:Prefecture-designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Taisha-zukuri]] [[en:Miho Shrine]][[Category:Expanded pages from wikipedia]] [[Category:Pages from wikipedia]] [[en:Miho Shrine]] [[ja:美保神社]] [[en:Miho Shrine]] {{Japan-religious-struct-stub}}

{{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} | founded = Unknown | Pilgrimage Sites = {{ill|Izumo Province Kami-Buddha Pilgrimage|ja|出雲國神仏霊場}} #8 | Main festival = {{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}} (Aoshibagaki festival) | Rituals = Kami-Mukae festival, Mushi-Sagashi festival, Morotabune festival | Honden = Miho-zukuri | map = {{location map|Japan Shimane|label=美保神社|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|position=left|float=center|width=180|caption=Miho Shrine}} }} '''Miho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|美保神社}}, {{nihongo|Miho-jinja}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{nihongo|Miho Sekicho, Matsue City, Shimane Prefecture|島根県松江市美保関町}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} and a former {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社}}. The shrine is revered as the home of {{ill|Ebisu (mythology)|ja|えびす}}, a deity of prosperity, fishing, and agriculture, and is also regarded as a guardian of musical instruments. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神}} in the right honden and {{ill|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|三穂津姫命}} in the left honden. Mihotsuhime is considered the consort of {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主神}}, the deity of prosperity and wonder, while Kotoshironushi is their son. According to the {{ill|Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|出雲国風土記}}, the original deity worshipped here was {{nihongo|Mihosusumi-no-Mikoto|御穂須須美命}}, who was later syncretized with Kotoshironushi and Mihotsuhime. == History == The shrine's origins are unclear, but it is mentioned in the {{ill|Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|出雲国風土記}} (8th century). During the medieval period, the {{ill|Yokoyama clan|ja|横山氏}} served as hereditary priests. By the Edo period, Miho Shrine gained prominence as a companion shrine to {{ill|Izumo Taisha|ja|出雲大社}}, and it became customary to visit both shrines during pilgrimages. In 1885 (Meiji 18), Miho Shrine was designated as a {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社}}, and after World War II, it was listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. == Grounds == File:美保神社社殿.JPG|Main Shrine File:別号二御前.JPG|Right Honden (Kotoshironushi) File:別号大御前.JPG|Left Honden (Mihotsuhime) File:美保神社神門.JPG|Shrine Gate The current honden was reconstructed in 1813 (Bunka 10) after a fire in 1800 (Kansei 12). The shrine features a unique architectural style called {{nihongo|Miho-zukuri|美保造}} or {{nihongo|Biyoku Taisha-zukuri|比翼大社造}}, a variation of {{ill|Taisha-zukuri|ja|大社造}}. The shrine buildings, including the honden, haiden, and gate, are designated as {{ill|Important Cultural Properties of Japan|ja|重要文化財}}. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National) === * Miho Shrine Main Shrine (Honden), including 18 plaques (1813) === National Tangible Folk Cultural Properties === * {{nihongo|Morotabune Boats|諸手船}} (2) * 846 ceremonial instruments * Soriko Boat (1) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Calligraphy handscroll (Tekagami) == festivals and Rituals == 1. **Aoshibagaki festival** ({{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}}): This festival reenacts the myth where {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神}} secluded himself within a fence made of green twigs during the {{ill|Kuniyuzuri|ja|国譲り}} myth. 2. **Morotabune festival** ({{nihongo|December 3|12月3日}}): Reenacts {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主}} consulting Kotoshironushi about ceding the land to the {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神}}. == Transportation == The shrine can be reached by the {{nihongo|Ichibata Bus|一畑バス}} from Matsue Station (about 40 minutes). The shrine is revered as the home of {{ill|Ebisu (mythology)|ja|えびす}}, a deity of prosperity, fishing, and agriculture, and is also regarded as a guardian of musical instruments. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神}} in the right honden and {{ill|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|三穂津姫命}} in the left honden. Mihotsuhime is considered the consort of {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主神}}, the deity of prosperity and wonder, while Kotoshironushi is their son. According to the {{ill|Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|出雲国風土記}}, the original deity worshipped here was {{nihongo|Mihosusumi-no-Mikoto|御穂須須美命}}, who was later syncretized with Kotoshironushi and Mihotsuhime. == History == The shrine's origins are unclear, but it is mentioned in the {{ill|Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|出雲国風土記}} (8th century). During the medieval period, the {{ill|Yokoyama clan|ja|横山氏}} served as hereditary priests. By the Edo period, Miho Shrine gained prominence as a companion shrine to {{ill|Izumo Taisha|ja|出雲大社}}, and it became customary to visit both shrines during pilgrimages. In 1885 (Meiji 18), Miho Shrine was designated as a {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社}}, and after World War II, it was listed as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. == Grounds == File:美保神社社殿.JPG|Main Shrine File:別号二御前.JPG|Right Honden (Kotoshironushi) File:別号大御前.JPG|Left Honden (Mihotsuhime) File:美保神社神門.JPG|Shrine Gate The current honden was reconstructed in 1813 (Bunka 10) after a fire in 1800 (Kansei 12). The shrine features a unique architectural style called {{nihongo|Miho-zukuri|美保造}} or {{nihongo|Biyoku Taisha-zukuri|比翼大社造}}, a variation of {{ill|Taisha-zukuri|ja|大社造}}. The shrine buildings, including the honden, haiden, and gate, are designated as {{ill|Important Cultural Properties of Japan|ja|重要文化財}}. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National) === * Miho Shrine Main Shrine (Honden), including 18 plaques (1813) === National Tangible Folk Cultural Properties === * {{nihongo|Morotabune Boats|諸手船}} (2) * 846 ceremonial instruments * Soriko Boat (1) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Calligraphy handscroll (Tekagami) == festivals and Rituals == 1. **Aoshibagaki festival** ({{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}}): This festival reenacts the myth where {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神}} secluded himself within a fence made of green twigs during the {{ill|Kuniyuzuri|ja|国譲り}} myth. 2. **Morotabune festival** ({{nihongo|December 3|12月3日}}): Reenacts {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主}} consulting Kotoshironushi about ceding the land to the {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神}}. == Transportation == The shrine can be reached by the {{nihongo|Ichibata Bus|一畑バス}} from Matsue Station (about 40 minutes). Visitors can transfer to a community bus at Miho Shrine's terminal stop and reach the shrine entrance in 1 minute on foot. == References == {{Reflist}} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Izumo Taisha|ja|出雲大社}} * {{ill|Kuniyuzuri|ja|国譲り}} * {{ill|Ebisu (mythology)|ja|えびす}} * {{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市}} == External Links == * [http://mihojinja.or.jp/ Official Website] ({{lang|ja|Japanese}}) == See Also == {{Commons|Category:Miho-jinja}} * {{ill|Hagoromo Legend|ja|羽衣伝説}} * {{ill|Miho Shrine (Shizuoka)|ja|御穂神社}} * [[Izumo Taisha]] * {{ill|Aoshi Ishidatami Street|ja|青石畳通り}} * {{ill|Sunny Yokoyama|ja|サニー横山}} - A descendant of the shrine’s priests, who became an aerobatic pilot and currently flies for [[Peach Aviation]]. == External Links == * [http://mihojinja.or.jp/ Miho Shrine Official Website] {{ja icon}} {{神道 横}} {{Normdaten}} {{shinto-stub}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:National Intermediate Shrines]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines|*Miho Shrine]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties (buildings)]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Matsue]] [[Category:Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Shimane Prefecture designated tangible cultural properties]] [[Category:Prefectural designated tangible folk cultural properties]] [[Category:Edo period architecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Matsue]] [[Category:History of Matsue]] [[Category:Taisha-zukuri]] [[Category:Tourist attractions in Shimane Prefecture]] ==See also== * [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] * [[Modern system of ranked Shinto Shrines]] * [[Yaegaki Shrine|Yaegaki Jinja]] * [[Kamosu Shrine]] * [[Sada Jinja]] * [[Izumo Taisha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] ==References== {{Commons category|Miho-jinja}} {{Reflist}} {{Shinto shrine}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[en:Miho Shrine]][[Category:Shikinai Shosha]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines]] [[Category:Shimane Prefecture designated tangible cultural property]] [[Category:Prefecture-designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Taisha-zukuri]] [[en:Miho Shrine]][[Category:Expanded pages from wikipedia]] [[en:Miho Shrine]] [[ja:美保神社]] [[en:Miho Shrine]] {{Japan-religious-struct-stub}}

{{神社 |名称= 美保神社 |画像= [[画像:Miho-jinja_haiden.jpg|250px|拝殿]]
拝殿 |所在地= [[島根県]][[松江市]]美保関町美保関608 |位置= {{Coord|35|33|44.32|N|133|18|21.77|E|region:JP-32_type:landmark_scale:60000|display=inline,title|name=美保神社}} |祭神= [[事代主|事代主神]]
[[三穂津姫|三穂津姫命]] |社格= [[式内社]]（小）
旧[[国幣中社]]
[[別表神社]] |創建= 不詳 |札所等= [[出雲國神仏霊場]]8番 |例祭= [[4月7日]]（青柴垣神事） |神事= 神迎神事
虫探神事
諸手船神事 |本殿= 美保造 |地図= {{Infobox mapframe|zoom=10|frame-width=180|type=point|marker=religious-shinto|shape-fill=#f5fffa|stroke-color=#006400|stroke-width=1|frame-latitude=35.508|frame-longitude=133.277}} {{Location map|Japan Shimane|label=美保神社|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|position=left|float=center|width=180|caption=}} }} [[File:島根・美保神社の社紋.png|250px|thumb|島根・美穂神社の社紋]] '''美保神社'''（みほじんじゃ）は、[[島根県]][[松江市]]にある[[神社]]である。[[式内社]]で、旧[[社格]]は[[国幣中社]]。 えびす神としての商売繁盛の神徳のほか、漁業・海運の神、田の虫除けの神として信仰を集める。また、「鳴り物」の神様として[[楽器]]の奉納も多い。 == 祭神 == 右殿に[[大国主|大国主神]]の子の[[事代主|事代主神]]、左殿に大国主神の后の[[三穂津姫|三穂津姫命]]を祀る。三穂津姫命は大国主神の幸魂奇魂（さきみたま・くしみたま）である「大物主神」の后神。事代主命は[[神屋楯比売|神屋楯比売神]]（かむやたてひめ）と大国主神との間の子供なので義理の母親にあたる。 『[[出雲国風土記]]』には、大穴持命（大国主神）と奴奈宣波比売命（[[奴奈川姫命]]）の間に生まれた「[[御穂須須美命]]」が美保郷に坐すとの記述がある。元々の当社の祭神は御穂須須美命のみであったのが、[[記紀]][[日本神話|神話]]の影響により事代主神と三穂津姫命とされたものと見られる。 == 歴史 == 創建の由緒は不詳であるが、[[8世紀]]に編纂された『[[出雲国風土記]]』の神社台帳に記載される古社である。[[延喜式神名帳]]では小社に列する。 [[中世]]より[[横山氏]]が[[神職]]を[[世襲]]した。[[近世]]頃から「大社（[[出雲大社]]）だけでは[[片参り|片詣り]]」と言われるようになり、出雲大社とともに参拝者が増えるようになった。出雲大社とあわせて「出雲のえびすだいこく」と総称される。 [[1885年]]（[[明治]]18年）に国幣中社に列せられ、[[第二次世界大戦]]後は[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]となった。 == 境内 == 美保神社社殿.JPG|社殿 別号二御前.JPG|別号二御前（事代主大神） 別号大御前.JPG|別号大御前（三穂津姫命） 美保神社神門.JPG|神門 [[2023年]]（[[令和]]5年）現在の本殿は[[寛政]]12年（[[1800年]]）の火災の後、[[文化 (元号)|文化10年]]（[[1813年]]）に再建されたものである[[#野々村 2002|野々村 2002]], p. 68。[[大社造]]の左右二殿連棟の特殊な形式で「美保造」または「比翼大社造」といわれ、国の重要文化財に指定されている。このような様式の成立時期は明らかではない。[[宝暦]]13年（1763年）の『伯様御用之覚』と呼ばれる文書では、[[天文 (元号)|天文]]3年（1534年）条に「美保'''神社'''」、[[天正]]11年（1583年）条に「美保'''両社'''」という社号で表記されている。また[[1886年]]（[[明治]]19年）の『国幣中社美保神社明細図書』によれば[[元亀]]年間（[[1570年]] - [[1573年]]）の戦災によって失われるまでは本殿は1棟であったが、その後、[[文禄]]年間（[[1593年]] - [[1596年]]）までの間に現在のように1つの基礎に2棟の本殿を持つ形式で再建されたという。この二つの文書から、天文3年（[[1534年]]）時点では1棟造りの神社であり、天正11年（[[1583年]]）までには2棟造りの「両社」と呼ばれるような構成になっていたと推定される。また、[[文禄]]5年（[[1596年]]）5月吉日と記された[[吉川広家|吉川廣家]]が[[文禄・慶長の役|朝鮮出兵]]での立願のため造営をした時の棟札にも「奉建立美保関'''両'''社御殿」とあり、当時既に2社殿が並立していたことを傍証している。ただし、当時の2社殿が現在のように連結された形態をとっていたかどうかは不明である。[[1928年]]（[[昭和]]3年）の修理によって本殿は原位置から現在の場所へ100メートル程度移築され、神域も拡張されて現在の形を完成させた[[#野々村 2002|野々村 2002]], p. 70。本殿を始め拝殿、神門、廻廊、通塀ともに屋根は現在では[[檜皮葺|桧皮葺]]であるが、修理以前はこけら葺であった。本殿2棟の間に末社・大后社があり、3社5神（大后社 [[神屋楯比売命]]、[[沼河比売|沼河比売命]]、姫子社 [[媛蹈鞴五十鈴媛命]]、[[五十鈴依媛命]]、神使社 稲脊脛命）を祀る。 == 文化財 == === 重要文化財（国指定） === ; 建造物 * 美保神社本殿 附:棟札18枚 - 文化10年（[[1813年]]） === 重要有形民俗文化財（国指定） === * [[諸手船]] 2隻 * 美保神社奉納鳴物 846点 * [[そりこ]] 1隻 === 県指定有形文化財 === * 紙本墨書手鑑（てかがみ） ==== 県指定有形民俗文化財 ==== * アバニ 1隻 附:櫂17本、アンバ20本 * ともど 1隻 == 祭事 == 青柴垣（あおふしがき）神事・[[諸手船]]（もろたぶね）神事は[[国譲り#国譲り神話と稲作|国譲り神話]]に因むものである。12月の諸手船神事は、[[大国主命|大国主神]]が国譲りの是非を相談するため息子の[[言代主神]]に使者を送ったという故事を再現、4月の青柴垣神事は、国譲りを決めた言代主神が船を青柴垣に変えてその中に身を隠すが、再び神として甦る様子を再現している[http://www.suntory.co.jp/enjoy/movie/d/843544699002.html　第36回サントリー地域文化賞島根県松江市美保神社大祭奉賛会] {{ja icon}} - サントリーチャンネル、2014。1年間鶏肉鶏卵を避け、毎日海で身を清めた2人の当屋が前日から断食し、青柴垣を飾った2隻の船に乗り、港内を一周後、美保神社に参拝、奉幣する[http://mihonoseki-kanko.jp/sinji/sinji_aofushigaki/　青柴垣神事] {{ja icon}} - 美保関地域観光振興協議会公式サイト。 * [[1月1日]] -- 歳旦祭 * [[1月7日]] -- 初ゑびす祭 * 1月中旬--爆竹式（とんどさん）[[ファイル:美保神社の爆竹式.jpg|サムネイル|美保神社爆竹式]] * 2月節分 -- 節分祭 * [[4月7日]] -- 例大祭（青柴垣神事）：例大祭が午前に、青柴垣神事は午後に行なわれる。 * [[4月13日]] -- 漁幸祭 * [[5月5日]] -- 神迎神事 * [[8月7日]] -- 虫探神事 * 9月中旬 -- [[浦安の舞]]（中学生の少女が正装で舞う。） * [[12月3日]] -- 新嘗祭・諸手船神事 === 波剪御幣（なみきりごへい）と月次御幣（つきなみごへい） === ; 波剪御幣 : 青柴垣神事で奉られる。 ; 月次御幣 : 毎月7日の月次祭の折に供えられる。 == 交通 == [[松江駅]]2番のりばから[[一畑バス]]美保関ターミナル行きに乗車（所要時間約40分）。美保関ターミナル終点より[[松江市コミュニティバス|美保関コミュニティバス]]美保関行きに乗り換えて美保関終点下車（所要時間約30分）。美保神社入口バス停から徒歩約1分。 [[初詣]]シーズンや[[ゴールデンウィーク]]、夏から初冬の土曜日・日曜日・祝日と[[12月3日]]には、[[日ノ丸自動車|日ノ丸バス]]により[[米子空港]]・[[境港駅]]との直行バス「えびすライナー」が運行される[http://mihojinja.or.jp/kotsu/#anchor0 【期間限定】えびすライナー] - 美保神社（2019年3月8日閲覧）。。 公民館の横に駐車場（無料：十数台分のスペース）と公衆便所があり、神社までは徒歩1分。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist}} == 関連図書 == * 安津素彦・梅田義彦編集兼監修者『神道辞典』[[神社新報]]社、1968年、58頁 * 白井永二・土岐昌訓編集『神社辞典』[[東京堂出版]]、1979年、322-323頁 * [[菅田正昭]]『日本の神社を知る「事典」』[[日本文芸社]]、1989年、203頁 * [[上山春平]]他『日本「神社」総覧』[[新人物往来社]]、1992年、238-239頁 * {{Cite book |和書 |author=野々村安浩|authorlink=野々村安浩 |chapter=美保神社の由来 |title=季刊 文化遺産 2002年4月号|publisher=[[創英社]] |date=2002-4 |isbn=978-4-921070-13-7 |ref=野々村 2002 }} == 関連項目 == {{Commons|Category:Miho-jinja}} * [[羽衣伝説]] * [[御穂神社]] * [[出雲大社]] * [[青石畳通り]] * [[サニー横山]] - 美保神社の[[社家]]。神職にはならず[[曲技飛行]]の道に進み、現在{{いつ|date= 2023年7月28日 (金) 17:34 (UTC)}}は[[Peach Aviation]]のパイロット。 == 外部リンク == * [http://mihojinja.or.jp/ 美保神社公式ウェブサイト] {{ja icon}} {{神道 横}} {{Normdaten}} {{shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:みほしんしや}} [[Category:島根県の神社]] [[Category:出雲国の式内社]] [[Category:国幣中社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:えびす神社|*みほしんしや]] [[Category:重要文化財 (建造物)]] [[Category:松江市の重要文化財]] [[Category:重要有形民俗文化財]] [[Category:島根県指定有形文化財]] [[Category:都道府県指定有形民俗文化財]] [[Category:江戸時代の建築]] [[Category:松江市の建築物]] [[Category:松江市の歴史]] [[Category:大社造]] [[Category:島根県の観光地]]
