The shrine is revered as the home of [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]], a deity of prosperity, fishing, and agriculture, and is also regarded as a guardian of musical instruments. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}} in the right honden and {{ill|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|三穂津姫命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 三穂津姫}} in the left honden. Mihotsuhime is considered the consort of {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmononushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大物主}}, the deity of prosperity and wonder, while Kotoshironushi is their son. According to the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Fudoki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the original deity worshipped here was {{nihongo|Mihosusumi-no-Mikoto|御穂須須美命}}, who was later syncretized with Kotoshironushi and Mihotsuhime. == History == The shrine's origins are unclear, but it is mentioned in the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Fudoki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (8th century). During the medieval period, the {{ill|Yokoyama clan|ja|横山氏|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoyama clan|qq=}} served as hereditary priests. By the Edo period, Miho Shrine gained prominence as a companion shrine to [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]], and it became customary to visit both shrines during pilgrimages. In 1885 (Meiji 18), Miho Shrine was designated as a {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuhē Chūsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}, and after World War II, it was listed as a [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. == Grounds == File:美保神社社殿.JPG|Main Shrine File:別号二御前.JPG|Right Honden (Kotoshironushi) File:別号大御前.JPG|Left Honden (Mihotsuhime) File:美保神社神門.JPG|Shrine Gate The current honden was reconstructed in 1813 (Bunka 10) after a fire in 1800 (Kansei 12). The shrine features a unique architectural style called {{nihongo|Miho-zukuri|美保造}} or {{nihongo|Biyoku Taisha-zukuri|比翼大社造}}, a variation of [[:en:Taisha-zukuri|Taisha-zukuri]]. The shrine buildings, including the honden, haiden, and gate, are designated as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National) === * Miho Shrine Main Shrine (Honden), including 18 plaques (1813) === National Tangible Folk Cultural Properties === * {{nihongo|Morotabune Boats|諸手船}} (2) * 846 ceremonial instruments * Soriko Boat (1) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Calligraphy handscroll (Tekagami) == festivals and Rituals == 1. **Aoshibagaki festival** ({{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}}): This festival reenacts the myth where {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}} secluded himself within a fence made of green twigs during the [[:en:Kuni-yuzuri|Kuniyuzuri]] myth. 2. **Morotabune festival** ({{nihongo|December 3|12月3日}}): Reenacts [[:en:Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi]] consulting Kotoshironushi about ceding the land to the {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/matsukami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天津神・国津神|comment=confirming this goes to Amatsukami|1=Amatsukami|2=zh|3=天神 (日本神話)|4=fr|5=Amatsukami|6=mni|7=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ|comment=confirming this goes to Amatsukami|1=Amatsukami|2=zh|3=天神 (日本神話)|4=fr|5=Amatsukami|6=mni|7=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ}}. == Transportation == The shrine can be reached by the {{nihongo|Ichibata Bus|一畑バス}} from Matsue Station (about 40 minutes). Visitors can transfer to a community bus at Miho Shrine's terminal stop and reach the shrine entrance in 1 minute on foot. == See Also == *[[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * [[:en:Kuni-yuzuri|Kuniyuzuri]] * [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]] * [[:en:Matsue|Matsue City]] * [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] * [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines]] * [[Yaegaki Shrine|Yaegaki Jinja]] * [[:en:Kamosu Shrine|Kamosu Shrine]] * [[Sada Shrine|Sada Jinja]] * [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * [[:en:Swan maiden|Hagoromo Legend]] * {{ill|Miho Shrine (Shizuoka)|ja|御穂神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miho Shrine (Shizuoka)|qq=}} * [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * {{ill|Aoshi Ishidatami Street|ja|青石畳通り|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aoshi Ishidatami Street|qq=}} * {{ill|Sunny Yokoyama|ja|サニー横山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sunny Yokoyama|qq=}} - The [[Taisha-zukuri]] [[Honden]] of 1813 is an [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2968 |title=Miho Jinja Honden |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 January 2012}} A collection of 846 [[:en:Traditional Japanese musical instruments|musical instruments]] dedicated to the shrine, and two dugout-canoes used in the Morotabune rite have been designated as [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Property]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/301/135 |title=Miho Jinja hōnōnarimono |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 January 2012}} ==Overview== '''Miho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|美保神社}}, {{nihongo|Miho-jinja}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in {{nihongo|Miho Sekicho, Matsue City, Shimane Prefecture|島根県松江市美保関町}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and a former {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuhē Chūsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. The shrine is revered as the home of [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]], a deity of prosperity, fishing, and agriculture, and is also regarded as a guardian of musical instruments. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}} in the right honden and {{ill|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|三穂津姫命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 三穂津姫}} in the left honden. Mihotsuhime is considered the consort of {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmononushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大物主}}, the deity of prosperity and wonder, while Kotoshironushi is their son. According to the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Fudoki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the original deity worshipped here was {{nihongo|Mihosusumi-no-Mikoto|御穂須須美命}}, who was later syncretized with Kotoshironushi and Mihotsuhime. == History == The shrine's origins are unclear, but it is mentioned in the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Fudoki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (8th century). During the medieval period, the {{ill|Yokoyama clan|ja|横山氏|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoyama clan|qq=|1=Yokoyama clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q119822420}} served as hereditary priests. By the Edo period, Miho Shrine gained prominence as a companion shrine to [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]], and it became customary to visit both shrines during pilgrimages. In 1885 (Meiji 18), Miho Shrine was designated as a {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuhē Chūsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}, and after World War II, it was listed as a [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. == Grounds == File:美保神社社殿.JPG|Main Shrine File:別号二御前.JPG|Right Honden (Kotoshironushi) File:別号大御前.JPG|Left Honden (Mihotsuhime) File:美保神社神門.JPG|Shrine Gate The current honden was reconstructed in 1813 (Bunka 10) after a fire in 1800 (Kansei 12). The shrine features a unique architectural style called {{nihongo|Miho-zukuri|美保造}} or {{nihongo|Biyoku Taisha-zukuri|比翼大社造}}, a variation of [[:en:Taisha-zukuri|Taisha-zukuri]]. The shrine buildings, including the honden, haiden, and gate, are designated as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National) === * Miho Shrine Main Shrine (Honden), including 18 plaques (1813) === National Tangible Folk Cultural Properties === * {{nihongo|Morotabune Boats|諸手船}} (2) * 846 ceremonial instruments * Soriko Boat (1) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Calligraphy handscroll (Tekagami) == festivals and Rituals == 1. **Aoshibagaki festival** ({{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}}): This festival reenacts the myth where {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}} secluded himself within a fence made of green twigs during the [[:en:Kuni-yuzuri|Kuniyuzuri]] myth. 2. **Morotabune festival** ({{nihongo|December 3|12月3日}}): Reenacts [[:en:Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi]] consulting Kotoshironushi about ceding the land to the {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/matsukami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天津神・国津神|comment=confirming this goes to Amatsukami|1=Amatsukami|2=zh|3=天神 (日本神話)|4=fr|5=Amatsukami|6=mni|7=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ|comment=confirming this goes to Amatsukami|1=Amatsukami|2=zh|3=天神 (日本神話)|4=fr|5=Amatsukami|6=mni|7=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ}}. == Transportation == The shrine can be reached by the {{nihongo|Ichibata Bus|一畑バス}} from Matsue Station (about 40 minutes). Visitors can transfer to a community bus at Miho Shrine's terminal stop and reach the shrine entrance in 1 minute on foot. == See Also == *[[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * [[:en:Kuni-yuzuri|Kuniyuzuri]] * [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]] * [[:en:Matsue|Matsue City]] * [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] * [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines]] * [[Yaegaki Shrine|Yaegaki Jinja]] * [[:en:Kamosu Shrine|Kamosu Shrine]] * [[Sada Shrine|Sada Jinja]] * [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * [[:en:Swan maiden|Hagoromo Legend]] * {{ill|Miho Shrine (Shizuoka)|ja|御穂神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miho Shrine (Shizuoka)|qq=|1=Miho Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11489249}} * [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * {{ill|Aoshi Ishidatami Street|ja|青石畳通り|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aoshi Ishidatami Street|qq=|1=Aoishidatami Street|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11662622}} * {{ill|Sunny Yokoyama|ja|サニー横山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sunny Yokoyama|qq=|1=Sunny Yokoyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11304946}} - A descendant of the shrine’s priests, who became an aerobatic pilot and currently flies for [[:en:Peach Aviation|Peach Aviation]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Related Articles == * == External Links == * [http://mihojinja.or.jp/ Official Website] ({{lang|ja|Japanese}}) == See Also == {{Commons|Category:Miho-jinja}} * == External Links == * [http://mihojinja.or.jp/ Miho Shrine Official Website] {{ja icon}} {{shinto-stub}} ==See also== * ==References== {{Commons category|Miho-jinja}} {{Reflist}} {{Japan-religious-struct-stub}} {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{translated page|ja|美保神社|version=104529581|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines|*Miho Shrine]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties (buildings)]] [[Category:Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Edo period architecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Matsue]] [[Category:History of Matsue]] [[Category:Taisha-zukuri]] [[Category:Tourist attractions in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Shikinai Shosha]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines]] [[Category:Shimane Prefecture designated tangible cultural property]] [[Category:Prefecture-designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]]}} [[sn:Miho Shrine]] [[en:Miho Shrine]] [[ja:美保神社]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Izumo Province]] [[Category:Architecture of the Taisho era]] [[Category:Registered Tangible Cultural Property of Japan in Shimane prefecture]] [[Category:History of Matsue]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties in Matsue City]] [[Category:Cultural heritage monuments in Japan]] [[fr:Miho-jinja]] [[zh:美保神社]] [[fr:Miho-jinja]] [[zh:美保神社]] [[Category:translated pages with valid en interwikis]]

Former {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuhē Chūsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}
[[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] | founded = Unknown | Pilgrimage Sites = {{ill|Izumo Province Kami-Buddha Pilgrimage|ja|出雲國神仏霊場|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Kami-Buddha Pilgrimage|qq=|1=Izumo Shinbutsu Pilgrimage|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11395860}} #8 | Main festival = {{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}} (Aoshibagaki festival) | Rituals = Kami-Mukae festival, Mushi-Sagashi festival, Morotabune festival | Honden = Miho-zukuri | map = {{location map|Japan Shimane|label=美保神社|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|position=left|float=center|width=180|caption=Miho Shrine}} | location = {{ill|Matsue|qid=Q207321}} }} {{nihongo|'''Miho Jinja'''|美保神社}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] in [[:en:Matsue|Matsue]], [[:en:Shimane Prefecture|Shimane Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. The [[Taisha-zukuri]] [[Honden]] of 1813 is an [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2968 |title=Miho Jinja Honden |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 January 2012}} A collection of 846 [[:en:Traditional Japanese musical instruments|musical instruments]] dedicated to the shrine, and two dugout-canoes used in the Morotabune rite have been designated as [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Property]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/301/135 |title=Miho Jinja hōnōnarimono |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 January 2012}} ==Overview== '''Miho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|美保神社}}, {{nihongo|Miho-jinja}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in {{nihongo|Miho Sekicho, Matsue City, Shimane Prefecture|島根県松江市美保関町}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and a former {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuhē Chūsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. The shrine is revered as the home of [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]], a deity of prosperity, fishing, and agriculture, and is also regarded as a guardian of musical instruments. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}} in the right honden and {{ill|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|三穂津姫命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 三穂津姫}} in the left honden. Mihotsuhime is considered the consort of {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmononushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大物主}}, the deity of prosperity and wonder, while Kotoshironushi is their son. According to the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Fudoki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the original deity worshipped here was {{nihongo|Mihosusumi-no-Mikoto|御穂須須美命}}, who was later syncretized with Kotoshironushi and Mihotsuhime. == History == The shrine's origins are unclear, but it is mentioned in the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Fudoki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (8th century). During the medieval period, the {{ill|Yokoyama clan|ja|横山氏|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoyama clan|qq=|1=Yokoyama clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q119822420}} served as hereditary priests. By the Edo period, Miho Shrine gained prominence as a companion shrine to [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]], and it became customary to visit both shrines during pilgrimages. In 1885 (Meiji 18), Miho Shrine was designated as a {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuhē Chūsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}, and after World War II, it was listed as a [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. == Grounds == File:美保神社社殿.JPG|Main Shrine File:別号二御前.JPG|Right Honden (Kotoshironushi) File:別号大御前.JPG|Left Honden (Mihotsuhime) File:美保神社神門.JPG|Shrine Gate The current honden was reconstructed in 1813 (Bunka 10) after a fire in 1800 (Kansei 12). The shrine features a unique architectural style called {{nihongo|Miho-zukuri|美保造}} or {{nihongo|Biyoku Taisha-zukuri|比翼大社造}}, a variation of [[:en:Taisha-zukuri|Taisha-zukuri]]. The shrine buildings, including the honden, haiden, and gate, are designated as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National) === * Miho Shrine Main Shrine (Honden), including 18 plaques (1813) === National Tangible Folk Cultural Properties === * {{nihongo|Morotabune Boats|諸手船}} (2) * 846 ceremonial instruments * Soriko Boat (1) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Calligraphy handscroll (Tekagami) == festivals and Rituals == 1. **Aoshibagaki festival** ({{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}}): This festival reenacts the myth where {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}} secluded himself within a fence made of green twigs during the [[:en:Kuni-yuzuri|Kuniyuzuri]] myth. 2. **Morotabune festival** ({{nihongo|December 3|12月3日}}): Reenacts [[:en:Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi]] consulting Kotoshironushi about ceding the land to the {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/matsukami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天津神・国津神|comment=confirming this goes to Amatsukami|1=Amatsukami|2=zh|3=天神 (日本神話)|4=fr|5=Amatsukami|6=mni|7=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ|comment=confirming this goes to Amatsukami|1=Amatsukami|2=zh|3=天神 (日本神話)|4=fr|5=Amatsukami|6=mni|7=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ}}. == Transportation == The shrine can be reached by the {{nihongo|Ichibata Bus|一畑バス}} from Matsue Station (about 40 minutes). Visitors can transfer to a community bus at Miho Shrine's terminal stop and reach the shrine entrance in 1 minute on foot. == See Also == *[[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * [[:en:Kuni-yuzuri|Kuniyuzuri]] * [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]] * [[:en:Matsue|Matsue City]] * [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] * [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines]] * [[Yaegaki Shrine|Yaegaki Jinja]] * [[:en:Kamosu Shrine|Kamosu Shrine]] * [[Sada Shrine|Sada Jinja]] * [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * [[:en:Swan maiden|Hagoromo Legend]] * {{ill|Miho Shrine (Shizuoka)|ja|御穂神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miho Shrine (Shizuoka)|qq=|1=Miho Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11489249}} * [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * {{ill|Aoshi Ishidatami Street|ja|青石畳通り|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aoshi Ishidatami Street|qq=|1=Aoishidatami Street|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11662622}} * {{ill|Sunny Yokoyama|ja|サニー横山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sunny Yokoyama|qq=|1=Sunny Yokoyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11304946}} - A descendant of the shrine’s priests, who became an aerobatic pilot and currently flies for [[:en:Peach Aviation|Peach Aviation]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Related Articles == * == External Links == * [http://mihojinja.or.jp/ Official Website] ({{lang|ja|Japanese}}) == See Also == {{Commons|Category:Miho-jinja}} * == External Links == * [http://mihojinja.or.jp/ Miho Shrine Official Website] {{ja icon}} {{shinto-stub}} ==See also== * ==References== {{Commons category|Miho-jinja}} {{Reflist}} {{Japan-religious-struct-stub}} {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{translated page|ja|美保神社|version=104529581|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines|*Miho Shrine]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties (buildings)]] [[Category:Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Edo period architecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Matsue]] [[Category:History of Matsue]] [[Category:Taisha-zukuri]] [[Category:Tourist attractions in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Shikinai Shosha]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines]] [[Category:Shimane Prefecture designated tangible cultural property]] [[Category:Prefecture-designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]]}} [[sn:Miho Shrine]] [[en:Miho Shrine]] [[ja:美保神社]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Izumo Province]] [[Category:Architecture of the Taisho era]] [[Category:Registered Tangible Cultural Property of Japan in Shimane prefecture]] [[Category:History of Matsue]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties in Matsue City]] [[Category:Cultural heritage monuments in Japan]] [[fr:Miho-jinja]] [[zh:美保神社]] [[fr:Miho-jinja]] [[zh:美保神社]] [[Category:translated pages with valid en interwikis]] [[Category:Shikinaisha]][[sn:Miho Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha]]

The [[Taisha-zukuri]] [[Honden]] of 1813 is an [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2968 |title=Miho Jinja Honden |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 January 2012}} A collection of 846 [[:en:Traditional Japanese musical instruments|musical instruments]] dedicated to the shrine, and two dugout-canoes used in the Morotabune rite have been designated as [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Property]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/301/135 |title=Miho Jinja hōnōnarimono |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 January 2012}} ==Overview== '''Miho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|美保神社}}, {{nihongo|Miho-jinja}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in {{nihongo|Miho Sekicho, Matsue City, Shimane Prefecture|島根県松江市美保関町}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and a former {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuhē Chūsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. The shrine is revered as the home of [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]], a deity of prosperity, fishing, and agriculture, and is also regarded as a guardian of musical instruments. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}} in the right honden and {{ill|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|三穂津姫命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 三穂津姫}} in the left honden. Mihotsuhime is considered the consort of {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmononushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大物主}}, the deity of prosperity and wonder, while Kotoshironushi is their son. According to the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Fudoki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the original deity worshipped here was {{nihongo|Mihosusumi-no-Mikoto|御穂須須美命}}, who was later syncretized with Kotoshironushi and Mihotsuhime. == History == The shrine's origins are unclear, but it is mentioned in the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Fudoki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (8th century). During the medieval period, the {{ill|Yokoyama clan|ja|横山氏|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoyama clan|qq=|1=Yokoyama clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q119822420}} served as hereditary priests. By the Edo period, Miho Shrine gained prominence as a companion shrine to [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]], and it became customary to visit both shrines during pilgrimages. In 1885 (Meiji 18), Miho Shrine was designated as a {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuhē Chūsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}, and after World War II, it was listed as a [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. == Grounds == File:美保神社社殿.JPG|Main Shrine File:別号二御前.JPG|Right Honden (Kotoshironushi) File:別号大御前.JPG|Left Honden (Mihotsuhime) File:美保神社神門.JPG|Shrine Gate The current honden was reconstructed in 1813 (Bunka 10) after a fire in 1800 (Kansei 12). The shrine features a unique architectural style called {{nihongo|Miho-zukuri|美保造}} or {{nihongo|Biyoku Taisha-zukuri|比翼大社造}}, a variation of [[:en:Taisha-zukuri|Taisha-zukuri]]. The shrine buildings, including the honden, haiden, and gate, are designated as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National) === * Miho Shrine Main Shrine (Honden), including 18 plaques (1813) === National Tangible Folk Cultural Properties === * {{nihongo|Morotabune Boats|諸手船}} (2) * 846 ceremonial instruments * Soriko Boat (1) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Calligraphy handscroll (Tekagami) == festivals and Rituals == 1. **Aoshibagaki festival** ({{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}}): This festival reenacts the myth where {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}} secluded himself within a fence made of green twigs during the [[:en:Kuni-yuzuri|Kuniyuzuri]] myth. 2. **Morotabune festival** ({{nihongo|December 3|12月3日}}): Reenacts [[:en:Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi]] consulting Kotoshironushi about ceding the land to the {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/matsukami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天津神・国津神|comment=confirming this goes to Amatsukami|1=Amatsukami|2=zh|3=天神 (日本神話)|4=fr|5=Amatsukami|6=mni|7=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ|comment=confirming this goes to Amatsukami|1=Amatsukami|2=zh|3=天神 (日本神話)|4=fr|5=Amatsukami|6=mni|7=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ}}. == Transportation == The shrine can be reached by the {{nihongo|Ichibata Bus|一畑バス}} from Matsue Station (about 40 minutes). Visitors can transfer to a community bus at Miho Shrine's terminal stop and reach the shrine entrance in 1 minute on foot. == See Also == *[[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * [[:en:Kuni-yuzuri|Kuniyuzuri]] * [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]] * [[:en:Matsue|Matsue City]] * [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] * [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines]] * [[Yaegaki Shrine|Yaegaki Jinja]] * [[:en:Kamosu Shrine|Kamosu Shrine]] * [[Sada Shrine|Sada Jinja]] * [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * [[:en:Swan maiden|Hagoromo Legend]] * {{ill|Miho Shrine (Shizuoka)|ja|御穂神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miho Shrine (Shizuoka)|qq=|1=Miho Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11489249}} * [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * {{ill|Aoshi Ishidatami Street|ja|青石畳通り|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aoshi Ishidatami Street|qq=|1=Aoishidatami Street|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11662622}} * {{ill|Sunny Yokoyama|ja|サニー横山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sunny Yokoyama|qq=|1=Sunny Yokoyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11304946}} - It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and a former {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuhē Chūsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. The shrine is revered as the home of [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]], a deity of prosperity, fishing, and agriculture, and is also regarded as a guardian of musical instruments. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}} in the right honden and {{ill|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|三穂津姫命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 三穂津姫}} in the left honden. Mihotsuhime is considered the consort of {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmononushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大物主}}, the deity of prosperity and wonder, while Kotoshironushi is their son. According to the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Fudoki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the original deity worshipped here was {{nihongo|Mihosusumi-no-Mikoto|御穂須須美命}}, who was later syncretized with Kotoshironushi and Mihotsuhime. == History == The shrine's origins are unclear, but it is mentioned in the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Fudoki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (8th century). In 1885 (Meiji 18), Miho Shrine was designated as a {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuhē Chūsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}, and after World War II, it was listed as a [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. == Grounds == File:美保神社社殿.JPG|Main Shrine File:別号二御前.JPG|Right Honden (Kotoshironushi) File:別号大御前.JPG|Left Honden (Mihotsuhime) File:美保神社神門.JPG|Shrine Gate The current honden was reconstructed in 1813 (Bunka 10) after a fire in 1800 (Kansei 12). The shrine is revered as the home of [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]], a deity of prosperity, fishing, and agriculture, and is also regarded as a guardian of musical instruments. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}} in the right honden and {{ill|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|三穂津姫命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 三穂津姫}} in the left honden. Mihotsuhime is considered the consort of {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmononushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大物主}}, the deity of prosperity and wonder, while Kotoshironushi is their son. According to the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Fudoki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the original deity worshipped here was {{nihongo|Mihosusumi-no-Mikoto|御穂須須美命}}, who was later syncretized with Kotoshironushi and Mihotsuhime. == History == The shrine's origins are unclear, but it is mentioned in the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Fudoki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (8th century). During the medieval period, the {{ill|Yokoyama clan|ja|横山氏|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoyama clan|qq=|1=Yokoyama clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q119822420}} served as hereditary priests. By the Edo period, Miho Shrine gained prominence as a companion shrine to [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]], and it became customary to visit both shrines during pilgrimages. In 1885 (Meiji 18), Miho Shrine was designated as a {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuhē Chūsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}, and after World War II, it was listed as a [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. == Grounds == File:美保神社社殿.JPG|Main Shrine File:別号二御前.JPG|Right Honden (Kotoshironushi) File:別号大御前.JPG|Left Honden (Mihotsuhime) File:美保神社神門.JPG|Shrine Gate The current honden was reconstructed in 1813 (Bunka 10) after a fire in 1800 (Kansei 12). The shrine features a unique architectural style called {{nihongo|Miho-zukuri|美保造}} or {{nihongo|Biyoku Taisha-zukuri|比翼大社造}}, a variation of [[:en:Taisha-zukuri|Taisha-zukuri]]. The shrine buildings, including the honden, haiden, and gate, are designated as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National) === * Miho Shrine Main Shrine (Honden), including 18 plaques (1813) === National Tangible Folk Cultural Properties === * {{nihongo|Morotabune Boats|諸手船}} (2) * 846 ceremonial instruments * Soriko Boat (1) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Calligraphy handscroll (Tekagami) == festivals and Rituals == 1. **Aoshibagaki festival** ({{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}}): This festival reenacts the myth where {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}} secluded himself within a fence made of green twigs during the [[:en:Kuni-yuzuri|Kuniyuzuri]] myth. 2. **Morotabune festival** ({{nihongo|December 3|12月3日}}): Reenacts [[:en:Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi]] consulting Kotoshironushi about ceding the land to the {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/matsukami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天津神・国津神|comment=confirming this goes to Amatsukami|1=Amatsukami|2=zh|3=天神 (日本神話)|4=fr|5=Amatsukami|6=mni|7=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ|comment=confirming this goes to Amatsukami|1=Amatsukami|2=zh|3=天神 (日本神話)|4=fr|5=Amatsukami|6=mni|7=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ}}. == Transportation == The shrine can be reached by the {{nihongo|Ichibata Bus|一畑バス}} from Matsue Station (about 40 minutes). Visitors can transfer to a community bus at Miho Shrine's terminal stop and reach the shrine entrance in 1 minute on foot. == See Also == *[[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * Former {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuhē Chūsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}

The [[Taisha-zukuri]] [[Honden]] of 1813 is an [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2968 |title=Miho Jinja Honden |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 January 2012}} A collection of 846 [[:en:Traditional Japanese musical instruments|musical instruments]] dedicated to the shrine, and two dugout-canoes used in the Morotabune rite have been designated as [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Property]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/301/135 |title=Miho Jinja hōnōnarimono |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 January 2012}} ==Overview== '''Miho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|美保神社}}, {{nihongo|Miho-jinja}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in {{nihongo|Miho Sekicho, Matsue City, Shimane Prefecture|島根県松江市美保関町}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and a former {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuhē Chūsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. The shrine is revered as the home of [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]], a deity of prosperity, fishing, and agriculture, and is also regarded as a guardian of musical instruments. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}} in the right honden and {{ill|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|三穂津姫命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 三穂津姫}} in the left honden. Mihotsuhime is considered the consort of {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmononushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大物主}}, the deity of prosperity and wonder, while Kotoshironushi is their son. According to the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Fudoki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the original deity worshipped here was {{nihongo|Mihosusumi-no-Mikoto|御穂須須美命}}, who was later syncretized with Kotoshironushi and Mihotsuhime. == History == The shrine's origins are unclear, but it is mentioned in the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Fudoki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (8th century). During the medieval period, the {{ill|Yokoyama clan|ja|横山氏|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoyama clan|qq=|1=Yokoyama clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q119822420}} served as hereditary priests. By the Edo period, Miho Shrine gained prominence as a companion shrine to [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]], and it became customary to visit both shrines during pilgrimages. In 1885 (Meiji 18), Miho Shrine was designated as a {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuhē Chūsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}, and after World War II, it was listed as a [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. == Grounds == File:美保神社社殿.JPG|Main Shrine File:別号二御前.JPG|Right Honden (Kotoshironushi) File:別号大御前.JPG|Left Honden (Mihotsuhime) File:美保神社神門.JPG|Shrine Gate The current honden was reconstructed in 1813 (Bunka 10) after a fire in 1800 (Kansei 12). The shrine features a unique architectural style called {{nihongo|Miho-zukuri|美保造}} or {{nihongo|Biyoku Taisha-zukuri|比翼大社造}}, a variation of [[:en:Taisha-zukuri|Taisha-zukuri]]. The shrine buildings, including the honden, haiden, and gate, are designated as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National) === * Miho Shrine Main Shrine (Honden), including 18 plaques (1813) === National Tangible Folk Cultural Properties === * {{nihongo|Morotabune Boats|諸手船}} (2) * 846 ceremonial instruments * Soriko Boat (1) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Calligraphy handscroll (Tekagami) == festivals and Rituals == 1. **Aoshibagaki festival** ({{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}}): This festival reenacts the myth where {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}} secluded himself within a fence made of green twigs during the [[:en:Kuni-yuzuri|Kuniyuzuri]] myth. 2. **Morotabune festival** ({{nihongo|December 3|12月3日}}): Reenacts [[:en:Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi]] consulting Kotoshironushi about ceding the land to the {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/matsukami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天津神・国津神|comment=confirming this goes to Amatsukami|1=Amatsukami|2=zh|3=天神 (日本神話)|4=fr|5=Amatsukami|6=mni|7=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ|comment=confirming this goes to Amatsukami|1=Amatsukami|2=zh|3=天神 (日本神話)|4=fr|5=Amatsukami|6=mni|7=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ}}. == Transportation == The shrine can be reached by the {{nihongo|Ichibata Bus|一畑バス}} from Matsue Station (about 40 minutes). Visitors can transfer to a community bus at Miho Shrine's terminal stop and reach the shrine entrance in 1 minute on foot. == See Also == *[[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] | founded = Unknown | Pilgrimage Sites = {{ill|Izumo Province Kami-Buddha Pilgrimage|ja|出雲國神仏霊場|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Kami-Buddha Pilgrimage|qq=|1=Izumo Shinbutsu Pilgrimage|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11395860}} #8 | Main festival = {{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}} (Aoshibagaki festival) | Rituals = Kami-Mukae festival, Mushi-Sagashi festival, Morotabune festival | Honden = Miho-zukuri | map = {{location map|Japan Shimane|label=美保神社|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|position=left|float=center|width=180|caption=Miho Shrine}} | location = {{ill|Matsue|qid=Q207321}} }} {{nihongo|'''Miho Jinja'''|美保神社}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] in [[:en:Matsue|Matsue]], [[:en:Shimane Prefecture|Shimane Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. The [[Taisha-zukuri]] [[Honden]] of 1813 is an [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2968 |title=Miho Jinja Honden |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 January 2012}} A collection of 846 [[:en:Traditional Japanese musical instruments|musical instruments]] dedicated to the shrine, and two dugout-canoes used in the Morotabune rite have been designated as [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Property]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/301/135 |title=Miho Jinja hōnōnarimono |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 January 2012}} ==Overview== '''Miho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|美保神社}}, {{nihongo|Miho-jinja}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in {{nihongo|Miho Sekicho, Matsue City, Shimane Prefecture|島根県松江市美保関町}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and a former {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuhē Chūsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. The shrine is revered as the home of [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]], a deity of prosperity, fishing, and agriculture, and is also regarded as a guardian of musical instruments. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}} in the right honden and {{ill|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|三穂津姫命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 三穂津姫}} in the left honden. Mihotsuhime is considered the consort of {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmononushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大物主}}, the deity of prosperity and wonder, while Kotoshironushi is their son. According to the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Fudoki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the original deity worshipped here was {{nihongo|Mihosusumi-no-Mikoto|御穂須須美命}}, who was later syncretized with Kotoshironushi and Mihotsuhime. == History == The shrine's origins are unclear, but it is mentioned in the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Fudoki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (8th century). During the medieval period, the {{ill|Yokoyama clan|ja|横山氏|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoyama clan|qq=|1=Yokoyama clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q119822420}} served as hereditary priests. By the Edo period, Miho Shrine gained prominence as a companion shrine to [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]], and it became customary to visit both shrines during pilgrimages. In 1885 (Meiji 18), Miho Shrine was designated as a {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuhē Chūsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}, and after World War II, it was listed as a [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. == Grounds == File:美保神社社殿.JPG|Main Shrine File:別号二御前.JPG|Right Honden (Kotoshironushi) File:別号大御前.JPG|Left Honden (Mihotsuhime) File:美保神社神門.JPG|Shrine Gate The current honden was reconstructed in 1813 (Bunka 10) after a fire in 1800 (Kansei 12). The shrine features a unique architectural style called {{nihongo|Miho-zukuri|美保造}} or {{nihongo|Biyoku Taisha-zukuri|比翼大社造}}, a variation of [[:en:Taisha-zukuri|Taisha-zukuri]]. The shrine buildings, including the honden, haiden, and gate, are designated as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National) === * Miho Shrine Main Shrine (Honden), including 18 plaques (1813) === National Tangible Folk Cultural Properties === * {{nihongo|Morotabune Boats|諸手船}} (2) * 846 ceremonial instruments * Soriko Boat (1) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Calligraphy handscroll (Tekagami) == festivals and Rituals == 1. **Aoshibagaki festival** ({{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}}): This festival reenacts the myth where {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}} secluded himself within a fence made of green twigs during the [[:en:Kuni-yuzuri|Kuniyuzuri]] myth. 2. **Morotabune festival** ({{nihongo|December 3|12月3日}}): Reenacts [[:en:Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi]] consulting Kotoshironushi about ceding the land to the {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/matsukami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天津神・国津神|comment=confirming this goes to Amatsukami|1=Amatsukami|2=zh|3=天神 (日本神話)|4=fr|5=Amatsukami|6=mni|7=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ|comment=confirming this goes to Amatsukami|1=Amatsukami|2=zh|3=天神 (日本神話)|4=fr|5=Amatsukami|6=mni|7=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ}}. == Transportation == The shrine can be reached by the {{nihongo|Ichibata Bus|一畑バス}} from Matsue Station (about 40 minutes). Visitors can transfer to a community bus at Miho Shrine's terminal stop and reach the shrine entrance in 1 minute on foot. == See Also == *[[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * [[:en:Kuni-yuzuri|Kuniyuzuri]] * [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]] * [[:en:Matsue|Matsue City]] * [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] * [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines]] * [[Yaegaki Shrine|Yaegaki Jinja]] * [[:en:Kamosu Shrine|Kamosu Shrine]] * [[Sada Shrine|Sada Jinja]] * [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * [[:en:Swan maiden|Hagoromo Legend]] * {{ill|Miho Shrine (Shizuoka)|ja|御穂神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miho Shrine (Shizuoka)|qq=|1=Miho Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11489249}} * [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * {{ill|Aoshi Ishidatami Street|ja|青石畳通り|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aoshi Ishidatami Street|qq=|1=Aoishidatami Street|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11662622}} * {{ill|Sunny Yokoyama|ja|サニー横山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sunny Yokoyama|qq=|1=Sunny Yokoyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11304946}} - [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] | founded = Unknown | Pilgrimage Sites = {{ill|Izumo Province Kami-Buddha Pilgrimage|ja|出雲國神仏霊場|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Kami-Buddha Pilgrimage|qq=|1=Izumo Shinbutsu Pilgrimage|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11395860}} #8 | Main festival = {{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}} (Aoshibagaki festival) | Rituals = Kami-Mukae festival, Mushi-Sagashi festival, Morotabune festival | Honden = Miho-zukuri | map = {{location map|Japan Shimane|label=美保神社|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|position=left|float=center|width=180|caption=Miho Shrine}} | location = {{ill|Matsue|qid=Q207321}} }} {{nihongo|'''Miho Jinja'''|美保神社}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] in [[:en:Matsue|Matsue]], [[:en:Shimane Prefecture|Shimane Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. The [[Taisha-zukuri]] [[Honden]] of 1813 is an [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2968 |title=Miho Jinja Honden |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 January 2012}} A collection of 846 [[:en:Traditional Japanese musical instruments|musical instruments]] dedicated to the shrine, and two dugout-canoes used in the Morotabune rite have been designated as [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Property]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/301/135 |title=Miho Jinja hōnōnarimono |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 January 2012}} ==Overview== '''Miho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|美保神社}}, {{nihongo|Miho-jinja}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in {{nihongo|Miho Sekicho, Matsue City, Shimane Prefecture|島根県松江市美保関町}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and a former {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuhē Chūsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. The shrine is revered as the home of [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]], a deity of prosperity, fishing, and agriculture, and is also regarded as a guardian of musical instruments. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}} in the right honden and {{ill|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|三穂津姫命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 三穂津姫}} in the left honden. Mihotsuhime is considered the consort of {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmononushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大物主}}, the deity of prosperity and wonder, while Kotoshironushi is their son. According to the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Fudoki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the original deity worshipped here was {{nihongo|Mihosusumi-no-Mikoto|御穂須須美命}}, who was later syncretized with Kotoshironushi and Mihotsuhime. == History == The shrine's origins are unclear, but it is mentioned in the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Fudoki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (8th century). During the medieval period, the {{ill|Yokoyama clan|ja|横山氏|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoyama clan|qq=|1=Yokoyama clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q119822420}} served as hereditary priests. By the Edo period, Miho Shrine gained prominence as a companion shrine to [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]], and it became customary to visit both shrines during pilgrimages. In 1885 (Meiji 18), Miho Shrine was designated as a {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuhē Chūsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}, and after World War II, it was listed as a [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. == Grounds == File:美保神社社殿.JPG|Main Shrine File:別号二御前.JPG|Right Honden (Kotoshironushi) File:別号大御前.JPG|Left Honden (Mihotsuhime) File:美保神社神門.JPG|Shrine Gate The current honden was reconstructed in 1813 (Bunka 10) after a fire in 1800 (Kansei 12). The shrine features a unique architectural style called {{nihongo|Miho-zukuri|美保造}} or {{nihongo|Biyoku Taisha-zukuri|比翼大社造}}, a variation of [[:en:Taisha-zukuri|Taisha-zukuri]]. The shrine buildings, including the honden, haiden, and gate, are designated as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National) === * Miho Shrine Main Shrine (Honden), including 18 plaques (1813) === National Tangible Folk Cultural Properties === * {{nihongo|Morotabune Boats|諸手船}} (2) * 846 ceremonial instruments * Soriko Boat (1) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Calligraphy handscroll (Tekagami) == festivals and Rituals == 1. **Aoshibagaki festival** ({{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}}): This festival reenacts the myth where {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}} secluded himself within a fence made of green twigs during the [[:en:Kuni-yuzuri|Kuniyuzuri]] myth. 2. **Morotabune festival** ({{nihongo|December 3|12月3日}}): Reenacts [[:en:Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi]] consulting Kotoshironushi about ceding the land to the {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/matsukami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天津神・国津神|comment=confirming this goes to Amatsukami|1=Amatsukami|2=zh|3=天神 (日本神話)|4=fr|5=Amatsukami|6=mni|7=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ|comment=confirming this goes to Amatsukami|1=Amatsukami|2=zh|3=天神 (日本神話)|4=fr|5=Amatsukami|6=mni|7=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ}}. == Transportation == The shrine can be reached by the {{nihongo|Ichibata Bus|一畑バス}} from Matsue Station (about 40 minutes). Visitors can transfer to a community bus at Miho Shrine's terminal stop and reach the shrine entrance in 1 minute on foot. == See Also == *[[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * [[:en:Kuni-yuzuri|Kuniyuzuri]] * [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]] * [[:en:Matsue|Matsue City]] * [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] * [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines]] * [[Yaegaki Shrine|Yaegaki Jinja]] * [[:en:Kamosu Shrine|Kamosu Shrine]] * [[Sada Shrine|Sada Jinja]] * [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * [[:en:Swan maiden|Hagoromo Legend]] * {{ill|Miho Shrine (Shizuoka)|ja|御穂神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miho Shrine (Shizuoka)|qq=|1=Miho Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11489249}} * [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * {{ill|Aoshi Ishidatami Street|ja|青石畳通り|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aoshi Ishidatami Street|qq=|1=Aoishidatami Street|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11662622}} * {{ill|Sunny Yokoyama|ja|サニー横山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sunny Yokoyama|qq=|1=Sunny Yokoyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11304946}} - By the Edo period, Miho Shrine gained prominence as a companion shrine to [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]], and it became customary to visit both shrines during pilgrimages. In 1885 (Meiji 18), Miho Shrine was designated as a {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuhē Chūsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}, and after World War II, it was listed as a [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. == Grounds == File:美保神社社殿.JPG|Main Shrine File:別号二御前.JPG|Right Honden (Kotoshironushi) File:別号大御前.JPG|Left Honden (Mihotsuhime) File:美保神社神門.JPG|Shrine Gate The current honden was reconstructed in 1813 (Bunka 10) after a fire in 1800 (Kansei 12). The shrine features a unique architectural style called {{nihongo|Miho-zukuri|美保造}} or {{nihongo|Biyoku Taisha-zukuri|比翼大社造}}, a variation of [[:en:Taisha-zukuri|Taisha-zukuri]]. The shrine is revered as the home of [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]], a deity of prosperity, fishing, and agriculture, and is also regarded as a guardian of musical instruments. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}} in the right honden and {{ill|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|三穂津姫命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 三穂津姫}} in the left honden. Mihotsuhime is considered the consort of {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmononushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大物主}}, the deity of prosperity and wonder, while Kotoshironushi is their son. According to the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Fudoki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the original deity worshipped here was {{nihongo|Mihosusumi-no-Mikoto|御穂須須美命}}, who was later syncretized with Kotoshironushi and Mihotsuhime. == History == The shrine's origins are unclear, but it is mentioned in the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Fudoki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (8th century). During the medieval period, the {{ill|Yokoyama clan|ja|横山氏|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoyama clan|qq=|1=Yokoyama clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q119822420}} served as hereditary priests. By the Edo period, Miho Shrine gained prominence as a companion shrine to [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]], and it became customary to visit both shrines during pilgrimages. In 1885 (Meiji 18), Miho Shrine was designated as a {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuhē Chūsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}, and after World War II, it was listed as a [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. == Grounds == File:美保神社社殿.JPG|Main Shrine File:別号二御前.JPG|Right Honden (Kotoshironushi) File:別号大御前.JPG|Left Honden (Mihotsuhime) File:美保神社神門.JPG|Shrine Gate The current honden was reconstructed in 1813 (Bunka 10) after a fire in 1800 (Kansei 12). The shrine features a unique architectural style called {{nihongo|Miho-zukuri|美保造}} or {{nihongo|Biyoku Taisha-zukuri|比翼大社造}}, a variation of [[:en:Taisha-zukuri|Taisha-zukuri]]. The shrine buildings, including the honden, haiden, and gate, are designated as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National) === * Miho Shrine Main Shrine (Honden), including 18 plaques (1813) === National Tangible Folk Cultural Properties === * {{nihongo|Morotabune Boats|諸手船}} (2) * 846 ceremonial instruments * Soriko Boat (1) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Calligraphy handscroll (Tekagami) == festivals and Rituals == 1. **Aoshibagaki festival** ({{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}}): This festival reenacts the myth where {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}} secluded himself within a fence made of green twigs during the [[:en:Kuni-yuzuri|Kuniyuzuri]] myth. 2. **Morotabune festival** ({{nihongo|December 3|12月3日}}): Reenacts [[:en:Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi]] consulting Kotoshironushi about ceding the land to the {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/matsukami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天津神・国津神|comment=confirming this goes to Amatsukami|1=Amatsukami|2=zh|3=天神 (日本神話)|4=fr|5=Amatsukami|6=mni|7=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ|comment=confirming this goes to Amatsukami|1=Amatsukami|2=zh|3=天神 (日本神話)|4=fr|5=Amatsukami|6=mni|7=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ}}. == Transportation == The shrine can be reached by the {{nihongo|Ichibata Bus|一畑バス}} from Matsue Station (about 40 minutes). Visitors can transfer to a community bus at Miho Shrine's terminal stop and reach the shrine entrance in 1 minute on foot. == See Also == *[[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * [[:en:Kuni-yuzuri|Kuniyuzuri]] * [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]] * [[:en:Matsue|Matsue City]] * [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] * [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines]] * [[Yaegaki Shrine|Yaegaki Jinja]] * [[:en:Kamosu Shrine|Kamosu Shrine]] * [[Sada Shrine|Sada Jinja]] * [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * [[:en:Swan maiden|Hagoromo Legend]] * {{ill|Miho Shrine (Shizuoka)|ja|御穂神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miho Shrine (Shizuoka)|qq=|1=Miho Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11489249}} * [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * {{ill|Aoshi Ishidatami Street|ja|青石畳通り|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aoshi Ishidatami Street|qq=|1=Aoishidatami Street|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11662622}} * {{ill|Sunny Yokoyama|ja|サニー横山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sunny Yokoyama|qq=|1=Sunny Yokoyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11304946}} - [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] | founded = Unknown | Pilgrimage Sites = {{ill|Izumo Province Kami-Buddha Pilgrimage|ja|出雲國神仏霊場|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Kami-Buddha Pilgrimage|1=Izumo Shinbutsu Pilgrimage|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11395860}} #8 | Main festival = {{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}} (Aoshibagaki festival) | Rituals = Kami-Mukae festival, Mushi-Sagashi festival, Morotabune festival | Honden = Miho-zukuri | map = {{location map|Japan Shimane|label=美保神社|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|position=left|float=center|width=180|caption=Miho Shrine}} | location = {{ill|Matsue|WD=Q207321}} }} {{nihongo|'''Miho Jinja'''|美保神社}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] in [[:en:Matsue|Matsue]], [[:en:Shimane Prefecture|Shimane Prefecture]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. The [[Taisha-zukuri]] [[Honden]] of 1813 is an [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/2968 |title=Miho Jinja Honden |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 January 2012}} A collection of 846 [[:en:Traditional Japanese musical instruments|musical instruments]] dedicated to the shrine, and two dugout-canoes used in the Morotabune rite have been designated as [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Property]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/301/135 |title=Miho Jinja hōnōnarimono |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=31 January 2012}} ==Overview== '''Miho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|美保神社}}, {{nihongo|Miho-jinja}}) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in {{nihongo|Miho Sekicho, Matsue City, Shimane Prefecture|島根県松江市美保関町}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and a former {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuhē Chūsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. The shrine is revered as the home of [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]], a deity of prosperity, fishing, and agriculture, and is also regarded as a guardian of musical instruments. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}} in the right honden and {{ill|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|三穂津姫命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 三穂津姫}} in the left honden. Mihotsuhime is considered the consort of {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmononushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大物主}}, the deity of prosperity and wonder, while Kotoshironushi is their son. According to the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Fudoki|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the original deity worshipped here was {{nihongo|Mihosusumi-no-Mikoto|御穂須須美命}}, who was later syncretized with Kotoshironushi and Mihotsuhime. == History == The shrine's origins are unclear, but it is mentioned in the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Province Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province Fudoki|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (8th century). During the medieval period, the {{ill|Yokoyama clan|ja|横山氏|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoyama clan|1=Yokoyama clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q119822420}} served as hereditary priests. By the Edo period, Miho Shrine gained prominence as a companion shrine to [[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]], and it became customary to visit both shrines during pilgrimages. In 1885 (Meiji 18), Miho Shrine was designated as a {{ill|Kokuhē Chūsha|ja|国幣中社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuhē Chūsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}, and after World War II, it was listed as a [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. == Grounds == File:美保神社社殿.JPG|Main Shrine File:別号二御前.JPG|Right Honden (Kotoshironushi) File:別号大御前.JPG|Left Honden (Mihotsuhime) File:美保神社神門.JPG|Shrine Gate The current honden was reconstructed in 1813 (Bunka 10) after a fire in 1800 (Kansei 12). The shrine features a unique architectural style called {{nihongo|Miho-zukuri|美保造}} or {{nihongo|Biyoku Taisha-zukuri|比翼大社造}}, a variation of [[:en:Taisha-zukuri|Taisha-zukuri]]. The shrine buildings, including the honden, haiden, and gate, are designated as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]]. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National) === * Miho Shrine Main Shrine (Honden), including 18 plaques (1813) === National Tangible Folk Cultural Properties === * {{nihongo|Morotabune Boats|諸手船}} (2) * 846 ceremonial instruments * Soriko Boat (1) === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * Calligraphy handscroll (Tekagami) == festivals and Rituals == 1. **Aoshibagaki festival** ({{nihongo|April 7|4月7日}}): This festival reenacts the myth where {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}} secluded himself within a fence made of green twigs during the [[:en:Kuni-yuzuri|Kuniyuzuri]] myth. 2. **Morotabune festival** ({{nihongo|December 3|12月3日}}): Reenacts [[:en:Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi]] consulting Kotoshironushi about ceding the land to the {{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/matsukami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天津神・国津神|comment=confirming this goes to Amatsukami|1=Amatsukami|2=zh|3=天神 (日本神話)|4=fr|5=Amatsukami|6=mni|7=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ|comment=confirming this goes to Amatsukami|1=Amatsukami|2=zh|3=天神 (日本神話)|4=fr|5=Amatsukami|6=mni|7=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ}}. == Transportation == The shrine can be reached by the {{nihongo|Ichibata Bus|一畑バス}} from Matsue Station (about 40 minutes). Visitors can transfer to a community bus at Miho Shrine's terminal stop and reach the shrine entrance in 1 minute on foot. == See Also == *[[:en:Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * [[:en:Kuni-yuzuri|Kuniyuzuri]] * [[:en:Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu (mythology)]] * [[:en:Matsue|Matsue City]] * [[Cultural Properties of Japan#Folk Cultural Properties|Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] * [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines]] * [[Yaegaki Shrine|Yaegaki Jinja]] * [[:en:Kamosu Shrine|Kamosu Shrine]] * [[Sada Shrine|Sada Jinja]] * [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * [[:en:Swan maiden|Hagoromo Legend]] * {{ill|Miho Shrine (Shizuoka)|ja|御穂神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miho Shrine (Shizuoka)|1=Miho Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11489249}} * [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Taisha]] * {{ill|Aoshi Ishidatami Street|ja|青石畳通り|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aoshi Ishidatami Street|1=Aoishidatami Street|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11662622}} * {{ill|Sunny Yokoyama|ja|サニー横山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sunny Yokoyama|1=Sunny Yokoyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11304946}} - A descendant of the shrine’s priests, who became an aerobatic pilot and currently flies for [[:en:Peach Aviation|Peach Aviation]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Related Articles == * == External Links == * [http://mihojinja.or.jp/ Official Website] ({{lang|ja|Japanese}}) == See Also == {{Commons|Category:Miho-jinja}} * == External Links == * [http://mihojinja.or.jp/ Miho Shrine Official Website] {{ja icon}} {{shinto-stub}} ==See also== * ==References== {{Commons category|Miho-jinja}} {{Reflist}} {{Japan-religious-struct-stub}} {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{translated page|ja|美保神社|version=104529581|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines|*Miho Shrine]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties (buildings)]] [[Category:Important Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Edo period architecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Matsue]] [[Category:History of Matsue]] [[Category:Taisha-zukuri]] [[Category:Tourist attractions in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Shikinai Shosha]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines]] [[Category:Shimane Prefecture designated tangible cultural property]] [[Category:Prefecture-designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]]}} [[en:Miho Shrine]] [[ja:美保神社]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Izumo Province]] [[Category:Architecture of the Taisho era]] [[Category:Registered Tangible Cultural Property of Japan in Shimane prefecture]] [[Category:History of Matsue]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties in Matsue City]] [[Category:Cultural heritage monuments in Japan]] [[fr:Miho-jinja]] [[zh:美保神社]] [[fr:Miho-jinja]] [[zh:美保神社]] [[Category:translated pages with valid en interwikis]] {{wikidata link|Q3313076}}
