Morotefune ritual |Main shrine = Mihozo|Map= {{Infobox mapframe|zoom=10|frame-width=180|type=point|marker=religious-shinto|shape-fill=#f5fffa|stroke-color=#006400|stroke-width=1|frame-latitude=35.508|frame-longitude=133.277}} {{Location map|Japan Shimane|label=Miho Shrine|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|position=left|float=center|width=180|caption=}} }} [[File: Shimane/Miho Shrine crest.png|250px|thumb|Shimane/Miho Shrine crest]] ``Miho Shrine'' is a {{ill|lt=Shrine|Q845945|WD=Q845945|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|lt=Shimane Prefecture|Q132751|WD=Q132751|1=Shimane Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Matsue City|Q207321|WD=Q207321|1=Matsue}}. {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinaisha|1=Shikinaisha|WD=Q134917286}}, and the former {{ill|lt=shakaku|Q10444029|WD=Q10444029|1=Shakaku}} was {{ill|UNKNOWN|WD=Q134917280|lt=Kokuheichusha|1=Kokuhei Chūsha}}. In addition to the divine virtue of prosperous business as Ebisu, he is also worshiped as the god of fishing and shipping, and the god of warding off insects in rice fields. Also, many {{ill|lt=musical instruments|Q34379|WD=Q34379|1=Musical instrument}} are dedicated to the god of ``noisemono''. === Enshrined God === {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi-kami|1=Ōkuninushi}}'s son {{ill|lt=Kotoshiro-nushi|Q8009611|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshiro-nushi|1=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto}} is enshrined in the right shrine, and {{ill|lt=Mihotsuhime|Q6378698|WD=Q6378698|lt=Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|1=Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto}}, the son of Okuninushi, is enshrined in the left shrine. Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto is the consort of ``Omononushi-kami,'' who is the Sakimitama/Kushimitama of Okuninushi-kami. Kotoshironushi no Mikoto is the child of {{ill|lt=Kamiya Tatehime|Q30935372|WD=Q30935372|lt=Kamuya Tatehime|1=Kamuyatate hime no mikoto}} and Okuninushi, so she is her stepmother. In ``{{ill|lt=Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|Q11395858|WD=Q11395858|1=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki}},'' there is a description that ``{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mihosusumi no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}},'' born between Ōanamochi no Mikoto (Okuninushi deity) and Nunasenamihime no Mikoto ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nunagawahime no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}}), sits in Mihosato. Originally, the only deity enshrined at our company was Mihosumi-no-Mikoto, but it seems that due to the influence of {{ill|lt=Kiki|Q842308|WD=Q842308|1=Kiki (Shinto)}}{{ill|lt=Japanese mythology|Q814158|WD=Q814158|lt=Mythology|1=Japanese mythology}}, Kotoshiro-nushi-kami and Mihotsu-hime-no-Mikoto were enshrined. === History === The origin of its founding is unknown, but it is an old shrine listed in the shrine register of ``{{ill|lt=Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|Q11395858|WD=Q11395858|1=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki}}'' compiled in {{ill|lt=8th century|Q8086|WD=Q8086|1=8th century}}. In {{ill|lt=Engishiki Shinmecho|Q11064932|WD=Q11064932|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}, you line up at a small shrine. From {{ill|lt=Medieval|Q12554|WD=Q12554|1=Middle Ages}}, {{ill|lt=Mr. Yokoyama|Q119822420|WD=Q119822420|1=Yokoyama clan}} became {{ill|lt=Shinto priest|Q60523|WD=Q60523|1=Kannushi}} {{ill|lt=hereditary|Q756689|WD=Q756689|1=Line of hereditary succession}}. From around {{ill|lt=early modern times|Q5308718|WD=Q5308718|1=Early modern period}}, it was said that ``Taisha ({{ill|lt=Izumo Taisha|Q696362|WD=Q696362|1=Izumo-taisha}}) alone is {{ill|lt=one visit|UNKNOWN|lt=one visit}},'' and the number of worshipers started to increase along with Izumo Taisha. Together with Izumo Taisha Shrine, it is collectively known as ``Izumo's Ebisu Daikoku''. In {{ill|lt=1885|Q7821|WD=Q7821|1=1885}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}18), it was listed as Kokupei Chusha, and after {{ill|lt=World War II|Q362|WD=Q362|1=World War II}} it became {{ill|lt=Beppyō Shrine|Q10898274|WD=Q10898274|1=Beppyo shrine}} of {{ill|lt=Shinja Honcho|Q908077|WD=Q908077|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. === Precincts === Miho Shrine building.JPG|Shrine building Betsugo Nigozen.JPG|Betsugo Nigozen (Koshirosu Okami) Betsugo Ogozen.JPG | Betsugo Ogozen (Mihotsuhime no Mikoto) Miho Shrine Shinto Gate.JPG|Shinmon {{ill|lt=2023|Q49622|WD=Q49622|1=2023}} ({{ill|lt=Reiwa|Q62609017|WD=Q62609017|1=Reiwa era}}5) The current main shrine was built after a fire in {{ill|lt=Kansei|Q1195131|WD=Q1195131|1=Kansei}}12 ({{ill|lt=1800|Q6875|WD=Q6875|1=1800}}). (era name)|Q1373146|Bunka 10th year}} ({{ill|lt=1813|Q6937|WD=Q6937|1=1813}}) {{ill|lt=#Nonomura 2002|UNKNOWN|lt=Nonomura 2002}}, p. 68. It is a special form of {{ill|lt=Taisha-zukuri|Q387874|WD=Q387874|1=Taisha-zukuri}} with two consecutive buildings on the left and right sides, and is called ``Miho-zukuri'' or ``Hiyoku Taisha-zukuri'' and is designated as an important cultural property of the country. It is not clear when this style was established. {{ill|lt=Horeki|Q1194397|WD=Q1194397|1=Hōreki}} In a document called "Haku-sama Goyo no Kaku" written in 1763, {{ill|lt=astronomical (era name)|Q1192853|WD=Q1192853|lt=Tenbun|1=Tenbun}} The company name is written as ``Miho''' Shrine'''' in the 3rd year (1534) article, and ``Miho'''Ryosha'''' in the 11th year (1583) article. Also, according to the "Kokuhei Chusha Miho Shrine Detailed Book" written in {{ill|lt=1886|Q7822|WD=Q7822|1=1886}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}19), for {{ill|lt=Motogame|Q1145064|WD=Q1145064|1=Genki (era)}} years ({{ill|lt=1570|Q6659|WD=Q6659|1=1570}} - There was only one main shrine until it was lost in the war in {{ill|lt=1573|Q6678|WD=Q6678|1=1573}}), but after that, for {{ill|lt=Bunroku|Q1373039|WD=Q1373039|1=Bunroku}} ({{ill|lt=1593|Q6772|WD=Q6772|1=1593}} - Until {{ill|lt=1596|Q6785|WD=Q6785|1=1596}}), it was rebuilt as it is today, with two main halls built on one foundation. From these two documents, it is estimated that as of the 3rd year of Tenbun ({{ill|lt=1534|Q6447|WD=Q6447|1=1534}}), it was a single-building shrine, and by the 11th year of Tensho ({{ill|lt=1583|Q6726|WD=Q6726|1=1583}}), it had become a two-building shrine called ``Ryosha.'' In addition, {{ill|lt=Hiroie Yoshikawa|Q1049766|WD=Q1049766|lt=Hiroie Yoshikawa|1=Kikkawa Hiroie}}, which was recorded as an auspicious day in May in {{ill|lt=Bunroku|Q1373039|WD=Q1373039|1=Bunroku}} 5th year ({{ill|lt=1596|Q6785|WD=Q6785|1=1596}}), is {{ja link|Bunroku-Keicho War|Q576338|When the building was built for the dispatch of troops to Korea}}, the ridge plate also read ``Hokenri Mihonoseki'''Ryo'' Shrine Palace, which proves that two shrine buildings were already standing side by side at that time. However, it is unknown whether the two shrine buildings at that time were connected as they are now. Due to repairs in {{ill|lt=1928|Q19715|WD=Q19715|1=1928}} ({{ill|lt=Showa|Q327567|WD=Q327567|1=Shōwa era}}3), the main shrine was moved about 100 meters from its original location to its current location, and the sacred area was expanded to complete its current form. 2002}}, p. 70. The roofs of the main shrine, worship hall, shrine gate, corridors, and entrance walls are currently {{ill|lt=cypress bark roofing|Q90373477|WD=Q90373477|lt=cypress bark|1=cypress bark roof}}, but before the repair, they were shingle roofs. There is a subsidiary shrine and Daigosha between the two main shrines, and three shrines and five shrines (Daigosha {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kamiya Tatehime no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}}, {{ill|lt=Numakawa Hime|Q11142832|WD=Q11142832|lt=Numakawa Hime no Mikoto|1=Nunakawahime}}, Himeko Shrine {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Himekeka Isuzuhime no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}}, {{ill|lt=Isuzuyorihime no Mikoto|Q10881557|WD=Q10881557|1=Isuzuyori-hime}}, Jinshisha Inasehime no Mikoto) is enshrined here. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === ; building * Miho Shrine main hall attached: 18 ridge plates - Bunka 10 ({{ill|lt=1813|Q6937|WD=Q6937|1=1813}}) === Important tangible folk cultural property (designated by the country) === * {{ill|lt=Morotebune|Q11632096|WD=Q11632096|1=Morotebune}} 2 ships * 846 songs dedicated to Miho Shrine * {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Soriko|1=UNKNOWN}} 1 ship === Prefecturally designated tangible cultural property === * Paper book and ink calligraphy handbook (Tekagami) ==== Prefecturally designated tangible folk cultural property ==== * 1 Avani included: 17 paddles, 20 Amba * 1 ship ==== Registered tangible cultural property ==== * Worship Hall - 1924 (Taisho 13) [https://www3.pref.shimane.jp/houdou/articles/156407 Shimane Prefecture Homepage (Press Release Materials)]. Designed by {{ill|lt=Chuta Ito|Q1050457|WD=Q1050457|1=Itō Chūta}} [https://www.fukumakan.jp/travel/8/1/ Fukumakan homepage (Miho Shrine/Ebisu Shrine)]. === Festival === The Aofushigaki ritual and the {{ill|lt=Morotebune|Q11632096|WD=Q11632096|1=Morotebune}} (Morotabune) ritual originate from the {{ill|lt=Kuniyoshi #Kokuyoshi myth and rice cultivation|Q11621119|WD=Q11621119|lt=Kokuyoshi myth|1=Kuni-yuzuri}}. The Morotefune ritual in December reenacts the story of {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi-no-Mikoto|UNKNOWN|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi-kami|1=Ōkuninushi}} sending a messenger to his son {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kotodai-nushi-kami|1=UNKNOWN}} to consult with him about the pros and cons of ceding the country, and the Aoshibagaki-gaki ritual in April, where Kotodai-nushi-kami, who had decided to cede the country, changed his ship into an Ao-shibagaki fence and carried it inside. He hides himself, but recreates the scene of being resurrected as a god again. {{ja icon}} - Suntory Channel, 2014. Our two members, who have avoided eating chicken, chicken, and eggs for a year and purified themselves at sea every day, fasted the day before, boarded two boats decorated with blue shibagaki, and after circling the port, visited Miho Shrine and offered offerings. Mihonoseki Regional Tourism Promotion Council official website. * {{ill|lt=January 1st|Q2150|WD=Q2150|1=January 1}} -- Saitan Festival * {{ill|lt=January 7th|Q2228|WD=Q2228|1=January 7}} -- First Ebisu Festival * Mid-January--Firecracker Ceremony (Tondo-san) [[File:Miho Shrine Firecracker Ceremony.jpg|Thumbnail|Miho Shrine Firecracker Ceremony]] * February Setsubun -- Setsubun Festival* {{ill|lt=April 7th|Q2505|WD=Q2505|1=April 7}} -- Reitaisai (Aoshibagaki Shinto Ritual): The Reitaisai is held in the morning, and the Aoshibagaki Shinto ritual is held in the afternoon. * {{ill|lt=April 13th|Q2498|WD=Q2498|1=April 13}} -- Fishing Festival * {{ill|lt=May 5th|Q2550|WD=Q2550|1=May 5}} -- Shinto ritual * {{ill|lt=August 7th|Q2781|WD=Q2781|1=August 7}} -- Insect detection ritual * Mid-September -- {{ill|lt=Urayasu no Mai|Q11558194|WD=Q11558194|1=Urayasu no mai}} (A junior high school girl dances in formal wear.) * {{ill|lt=December 3rd|Q2298|WD=Q2298|1=December 3}} -- Niiname-sai/Morotebune ritual === Namikiri Gohei and Tsukinami Gohei === ; Namisaki Gohei : Dedicated at the Aoshibagaki Shinto ritual. ; Monthly gohei : It is offered during the monthly festival on the 7th of every month. === Transportation === {{ill|lt=Matsue Station|Q1058652|WD=Q1058652|1=Matsue Station}} From platform 2, take the {{ill|lt=Ichibata Bus|Q11352955|WD=Q11352955|1=Ichibata Bus}} bound for Mihonoseki Terminal (about 40 minutes). From the Mihonoseki terminal end, transfer to the {{ill|lt=Matsue city community bus|Q11531653|WD=Q11531653|lt=Mihonoseki community bus|1=Mihonoseki community bus}} bound for {{ill|lt=Mihonoseki town|Q6845336|WD=Q6845336|lt=Mihonoseki|1=Mihonoseki, Shimane}} and get off at the Mihonoseki terminal (about 30 minutes). About 1 minute walk from Miho Shrine Iriguchi bus stop. {{ill|lt=Hatsumode|Q1032381|WD=Q1032381|1=Hatsumōde}} season, {{ill|lt=Golden Week|Q1137351|WD=Q1137351|1=Golden Week (Japan)}}, Saturdays, Sundays, holidays from summer to early winter, and {{ill|lt=December 3rd|Q2298|WD=Q2298|1=December 3}}, {{ill|lt=Hinomaru Motors|Q115 04700|WD=Q115 04700|lt=Hinomaru Bus}} operates the direct bus "Ebisu Liner" between {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yonago Airport|1=UNKNOWN}} and {{ill|lt=Sakaiminato Station|Q7402786|WD=Q7402786|1=Sakaiminato Station}}[http://mihojinja.or.jp/kotsu/#anchor0 [Limited Time] Ebisu Liner] - Miho Shrine (viewed March 8, 2019). . There is a parking lot next to the community center (free of charge, with space for more than a dozen cars) and a public toilet, and it is a 1-minute walk from the shrine. === Related books === * "Shinto Dictionary" edited and supervised by Motohiko Anzu and Yoshihiko Umeda, {{ill|lt=Jinja Shimpo|Q11590705|WD=Q11590705|1=Jinja Shinpō}}sha, 1968, 58 pages * Edited by Eiji Shirai and Masanori Toki, "Dictionary of Shrines" {{ill|lt=Tokyodo Publishing|Q11524645|WD=Q11524645|1=Tōkyōdō Shuppan}}, 1979, pp. 322-323 * {{ill|lt=Masaaki Suda|Q11619352|WD=Q11619352|1=Masaaki Sugata}} "Encyclopedia" to know about Japanese shrines, {{ill|lt=Nippon Bungeisha|Q7034281|WD=Q7034281|1=Nihon Bungeisha}}, 1989, 203 pages * {{ill|lt=Shunpei Ueyama|Q403579|WD=Q403579|1=Shunpei Ueyama}} et al., "Comprehensive list of Japanese shrines" {{ill|lt=Shinjinbutsu Oraisha|Q11501312|WD=Q11501312|1=Shin Jinbutsu Ōraisha. "Rekishi Dokuhon" Henshūbu}}, 1992, pp. 238-239 * {{Cite book |Japanese book |author=Yasuhiro Nonomura|authorlink=Yasuhiro Nonomura |chapter=Origin of Miho Shrine |title=Quarterly Cultural Heritage |issue=April 2002 issue |publisher={{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Soeisha|1=UNKNOWN}} |date=2002-04 |isbn=978-4-921070-13-7 |ref=Nonomura 2002 }} === Footnotes === {{Footnote help}} {{Reflist}} === Related items === {{Commons|Category:Miho-jinja}} * {{ill|lt=Legend of Hagoromo|Q1326754|WD=Q1326754|1=Swan maiden}} * {{ill|lt=Miho Shrine|Q11489249|WD=Q11489249|1=Miho Shrine (Q11489249)}} * {{ill|lt=Izumo Taisha|Q696362|WD=Q696362|1=Izumo-taisha}} * {{ill|lt=Blue Cobblestone Street|Q11662622|WD=Q11662622|1=Aoishidatami Street}} * {{ill|lt=Sunny Yokoyama|Q11304946|WD=Q11304946|1=Sunny Yokoyama}} - {{ill|lt=Shake|Q11588367|WD=Q11588367|1=Shake (social class)}} of Miho Shrine. Rather than becoming a priest, he pursued the path of {{ill|lt=aerobatics|Q373557|WD=Q373557|1=Aerobatics}}, and is currently a pilot for {{ill|lt=Peach Aviation|Q1376634|WD=Q1376634|1=Peach Aviation}}. === External link === * [http://mihojinja.or.jp/ Miho Shrine official website] {{ja icon}} {{Shinto horizontal}} {{Normdaten}} {{shinto-stub}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Miho Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Miho Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shinto shrine]] [[Category:Shikinaisha|Miho Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Izumo Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Izumo Province]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines]] [[Category:重要文化財 (建造物)]] [[Category:松江市の重要文化財]] [[Category:重要有形民俗文化財]] [[Category:島根県指定有形文化財]] [[Category:都道府県指定有形民俗文化財]] [[Category:島根県の登録有形文化財]] [[Category:江戸時代の建築]] [[Category:Architecture of the Taisho era]] [[Category:松江市の建築物]] [[Category:松江市の歴史]] [[Category:Taisha-zukuri]] [[Category:島根県の観光地]] [[Category:kkkkkkkkkkkkkk]] [[Category:nnnnnnnnn]] [[Category:qqqqqqq]]

Morotefune ritual |Main shrine = Mihozo|Map= {{Infobox mapframe|zoom=10|frame-width=180|type=point|marker=religious-shinto|shape-fill=#f5fffa|stroke-color=#006400|stroke-width=1|frame-latitude=35.508|frame-longitude=133.277}} {{Location map|Japan Shimane|label=Miho Shrine|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|position=left|float=center|width=180|caption=}} }} [[File: Shimane/Miho Shrine crest.png|250px|thumb|Shimane/Miho Shrine crest]] ``Miho Shrine'' is a {{ill|lt=Shrine|Q845945|WD=Q845945|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|lt=Shimane Prefecture|Q132751|WD=Q132751|1=Shimane Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Matsue City|Q207321|WD=Q207321|1=Matsue}}. {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinaisha|1=Shikinaisha|WD=Q134917286}}, and the former {{ill|lt=shakaku|Q10444029|WD=Q10444029|1=Shakaku}} was {{ill|UNKNOWN|WD=Q134917280|lt=Kokuheichusha|1=Kokuhei Chūsha}}. In addition to the divine virtue of prosperous business as Ebisu, he is also worshiped as the god of fishing and shipping, and the god of warding off insects in rice fields. Also, many {{ill|lt=musical instruments|Q34379|WD=Q34379|1=Musical instrument}} are dedicated to the god of ``noisemono''. === Enshrined God === {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi-kami|1=Ōkuninushi}}'s son {{ill|lt=Kotoshiro-nushi|Q8009611|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshiro-nushi|1=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto}} is enshrined in the right shrine, and {{ill|lt=Mihotsuhime|Q6378698|WD=Q6378698|lt=Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|1=Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto}}, the son of Okuninushi, is enshrined in the left shrine. Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto is the consort of ``Omononushi-kami,'' who is the Sakimitama/Kushimitama of Okuninushi-kami. Kotoshironushi no Mikoto is the child of {{ill|lt=Kamiya Tatehime|Q30935372|WD=Q30935372|lt=Kamuya Tatehime|1=Kamuyatate hime no mikoto}} and Okuninushi, so she is her stepmother. In ``{{ill|lt=Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|Q11395858|WD=Q11395858|1=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki}},'' there is a description that ``{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mihosusumi no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}},'' born between Ōanamochi no Mikoto (Okuninushi deity) and Nunasenamihime no Mikoto ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nunagawahime no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}}), sits in Mihosato. Originally, the only deity enshrined at our company was Mihosumi-no-Mikoto, but it seems that due to the influence of {{ill|lt=Kiki|Q842308|WD=Q842308|1=Kiki (Shinto)}}{{ill|lt=Japanese mythology|Q814158|WD=Q814158|lt=Mythology|1=Japanese mythology}}, Kotoshiro-nushi-kami and Mihotsu-hime-no-Mikoto were enshrined. === History === The origin of its founding is unknown, but it is an old shrine listed in the shrine register of ``{{ill|lt=Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|Q11395858|WD=Q11395858|1=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki}}'' compiled in {{ill|lt=8th century|Q8086|WD=Q8086|1=8th century}}. In {{ill|lt=Engishiki Shinmecho|Q11064932|WD=Q11064932|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}, you line up at a small shrine. From {{ill|lt=Medieval|Q12554|WD=Q12554|1=Middle Ages}}, {{ill|lt=Mr. Yokoyama|Q119822420|WD=Q119822420|1=Yokoyama clan}} became {{ill|lt=Shinto priest|Q60523|WD=Q60523|1=Kannushi}} {{ill|lt=hereditary|Q756689|WD=Q756689|1=Line of hereditary succession}}. From around {{ill|lt=early modern times|Q5308718|WD=Q5308718|1=Early modern period}}, it was said that ``Taisha ({{ill|lt=Izumo Taisha|Q696362|WD=Q696362|1=Izumo-taisha}}) alone is {{ill|lt=one visit|UNKNOWN|lt=one visit}},'' and the number of worshipers started to increase along with Izumo Taisha. Together with Izumo Taisha Shrine, it is collectively known as ``Izumo's Ebisu Daikoku''. In {{ill|lt=1885|Q7821|WD=Q7821|1=1885}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}18), it was listed as Kokupei Chusha, and after {{ill|lt=World War II|Q362|WD=Q362|1=World War II}} it became {{ill|lt=Beppyō Shrine|Q10898274|WD=Q10898274|1=Beppyo shrine}} of {{ill|lt=Shinja Honcho|Q908077|WD=Q908077|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. === Precincts === Miho Shrine building.JPG|Shrine building Betsugo Nigozen.JPG|Betsugo Nigozen (Koshirosu Okami) Betsugo Ogozen.JPG | Betsugo Ogozen (Mihotsuhime no Mikoto) Miho Shrine Shinto Gate.JPG|Shinmon {{ill|lt=2023|Q49622|WD=Q49622|1=2023}} ({{ill|lt=Reiwa|Q62609017|WD=Q62609017|1=Reiwa era}}5) The current main shrine was built after a fire in {{ill|lt=Kansei|Q1195131|WD=Q1195131|1=Kansei}}12 ({{ill|lt=1800|Q6875|WD=Q6875|1=1800}}). (era name)|Q1373146|Bunka 10th year}} ({{ill|lt=1813|Q6937|WD=Q6937|1=1813}}) {{ill|lt=#Nonomura 2002|UNKNOWN|lt=Nonomura 2002}}, p. 68. It is a special form of {{ill|lt=Taisha-zukuri|Q387874|WD=Q387874|1=Taisha-zukuri}} with two consecutive buildings on the left and right sides, and is called ``Miho-zukuri'' or ``Hiyoku Taisha-zukuri'' and is designated as an important cultural property of the country. It is not clear when this style was established. {{ill|lt=Horeki|Q1194397|WD=Q1194397|1=Hōreki}} In a document called "Haku-sama Goyo no Kaku" written in 1763, {{ill|lt=astronomical (era name)|Q1192853|WD=Q1192853|lt=Tenbun|1=Tenbun}} The company name is written as ``Miho''' Shrine'''' in the 3rd year (1534) article, and ``Miho'''Ryosha'''' in the 11th year (1583) article. Also, according to the "Kokuhei Chusha Miho Shrine Detailed Book" written in {{ill|lt=1886|Q7822|WD=Q7822|1=1886}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}19), for {{ill|lt=Motogame|Q1145064|WD=Q1145064|1=Genki (era)}} years ({{ill|lt=1570|Q6659|WD=Q6659|1=1570}} - There was only one main shrine until it was lost in the war in {{ill|lt=1573|Q6678|WD=Q6678|1=1573}}), but after that, for {{ill|lt=Bunroku|Q1373039|WD=Q1373039|1=Bunroku}} ({{ill|lt=1593|Q6772|WD=Q6772|1=1593}} - Until {{ill|lt=1596|Q6785|WD=Q6785|1=1596}}), it was rebuilt as it is today, with two main halls built on one foundation. From these two documents, it is estimated that as of the 3rd year of Tenbun ({{ill|lt=1534|Q6447|WD=Q6447|1=1534}}), it was a single-building shrine, and by the 11th year of Tensho ({{ill|lt=1583|Q6726|WD=Q6726|1=1583}}), it had become a two-building shrine called ``Ryosha.'' In addition, {{ill|lt=Hiroie Yoshikawa|Q1049766|WD=Q1049766|lt=Hiroie Yoshikawa|1=Kikkawa Hiroie}}, which was recorded as an auspicious day in May in {{ill|lt=Bunroku|Q1373039|WD=Q1373039|1=Bunroku}} 5th year ({{ill|lt=1596|Q6785|WD=Q6785|1=1596}}), is {{ja link|Bunroku-Keicho War|Q576338|When the building was built for the dispatch of troops to Korea}}, the ridge plate also read ``Hokenri Mihonoseki'''Ryo'' Shrine Palace, which proves that two shrine buildings were already standing side by side at that time. However, it is unknown whether the two shrine buildings at that time were connected as they are now. Due to repairs in {{ill|lt=1928|Q19715|WD=Q19715|1=1928}} ({{ill|lt=Showa|Q327567|WD=Q327567|1=Shōwa era}}3), the main shrine was moved about 100 meters from its original location to its current location, and the sacred area was expanded to complete its current form. 2002}}, p. 70. The roofs of the main shrine, worship hall, shrine gate, corridors, and entrance walls are currently {{ill|lt=cypress bark roofing|Q90373477|WD=Q90373477|lt=cypress bark|1=cypress bark roof}}, but before the repair, they were shingle roofs. There is a subsidiary shrine and Daigosha between the two main shrines, and three shrines and five shrines (Daigosha {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kamiya Tatehime no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}}, {{ill|lt=Numakawa Hime|Q11142832|WD=Q11142832|lt=Numakawa Hime no Mikoto|1=Nunakawahime}}, Himeko Shrine {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Himekeka Isuzuhime no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}}, {{ill|lt=Isuzuyorihime no Mikoto|Q10881557|WD=Q10881557|1=Isuzuyori-hime}}, Jinshisha Inasehime no Mikoto) is enshrined here. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === ; building * Miho Shrine main hall attached: 18 ridge plates - Bunka 10 ({{ill|lt=1813|Q6937|WD=Q6937|1=1813}}) === Important tangible folk cultural property (designated by the country) === * {{ill|lt=Morotebune|Q11632096|WD=Q11632096|1=Morotebune}} 2 ships * 846 songs dedicated to Miho Shrine * {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Soriko|1=UNKNOWN}} 1 ship === Prefecturally designated tangible cultural property === * Paper book and ink calligraphy handbook (Tekagami) ==== Prefecturally designated tangible folk cultural property ==== * 1 Avani included: 17 paddles, 20 Amba * 1 ship ==== Registered tangible cultural property ==== * Worship Hall - 1924 (Taisho 13) [https://www3.pref.shimane.jp/houdou/articles/156407 Shimane Prefecture Homepage (Press Release Materials)]. Designed by {{ill|lt=Chuta Ito|Q1050457|WD=Q1050457|1=Itō Chūta}} [https://www.fukumakan.jp/travel/8/1/ Fukumakan homepage (Miho Shrine/Ebisu Shrine)]. === Festival === The Aofushigaki ritual and the {{ill|lt=Morotebune|Q11632096|WD=Q11632096|1=Morotebune}} (Morotabune) ritual originate from the {{ill|lt=Kuniyoshi #Kokuyoshi myth and rice cultivation|Q11621119|WD=Q11621119|lt=Kokuyoshi myth|1=Kuni-yuzuri}}. The Morotefune ritual in December reenacts the story of {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi-no-Mikoto|UNKNOWN|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi-kami|1=Ōkuninushi}} sending a messenger to his son {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kotodai-nushi-kami|1=UNKNOWN}} to consult with him about the pros and cons of ceding the country, and the Aoshibagaki-gaki ritual in April, where Kotodai-nushi-kami, who had decided to cede the country, changed his ship into an Ao-shibagaki fence and carried it inside. He hides himself, but recreates the scene of being resurrected as a god again. {{ja icon}} - Suntory Channel, 2014. Our two members, who have avoided eating chicken, chicken, and eggs for a year and purified themselves at sea every day, fasted the day before, boarded two boats decorated with blue shibagaki, and after circling the port, visited Miho Shrine and offered offerings. Mihonoseki Regional Tourism Promotion Council official website. * {{ill|lt=January 1st|Q2150|WD=Q2150|1=January 1}} -- Saitan Festival * {{ill|lt=January 7th|Q2228|WD=Q2228|1=January 7}} -- First Ebisu Festival * Mid-January--Firecracker Ceremony (Tondo-san) [[File:Miho Shrine Firecracker Ceremony.jpg|Thumbnail|Miho Shrine Firecracker Ceremony]] * February Setsubun -- Setsubun Festival* {{ill|lt=April 7th|Q2505|WD=Q2505|1=April 7}} -- Reitaisai (Aoshibagaki Shinto Ritual): The Reitaisai is held in the morning, and the Aoshibagaki Shinto ritual is held in the afternoon. * {{ill|lt=April 13th|Q2498|WD=Q2498|1=April 13}} -- Fishing Festival * {{ill|lt=May 5th|Q2550|WD=Q2550|1=May 5}} -- Shinto ritual * {{ill|lt=August 7th|Q2781|WD=Q2781|1=August 7}} -- Insect detection ritual * Mid-September -- {{ill|lt=Urayasu no Mai|Q11558194|WD=Q11558194|1=Urayasu no mai}} (A junior high school girl dances in formal wear.) * {{ill|lt=December 3rd|Q2298|WD=Q2298|1=December 3}} -- Niiname-sai/Morotebune ritual === Namikiri Gohei and Tsukinami Gohei === ; Namisaki Gohei : Dedicated at the Aoshibagaki Shinto ritual. ; Monthly gohei : It is offered during the monthly festival on the 7th of every month. === Transportation === {{ill|lt=Matsue Station|Q1058652|WD=Q1058652|1=Matsue Station}} From platform 2, take the {{ill|lt=Ichibata Bus|Q11352955|WD=Q11352955|1=Ichibata Bus}} bound for Mihonoseki Terminal (about 40 minutes). From the Mihonoseki terminal end, transfer to the {{ill|lt=Matsue city community bus|Q11531653|WD=Q11531653|lt=Mihonoseki community bus|1=Mihonoseki community bus}} bound for {{ill|lt=Mihonoseki town|Q6845336|WD=Q6845336|lt=Mihonoseki|1=Mihonoseki, Shimane}} and get off at the Mihonoseki terminal (about 30 minutes). About 1 minute walk from Miho Shrine Iriguchi bus stop. {{ill|lt=Hatsumode|Q1032381|WD=Q1032381|1=Hatsumōde}} season, {{ill|lt=Golden Week|Q1137351|WD=Q1137351|1=Golden Week (Japan)}}, Saturdays, Sundays, holidays from summer to early winter, and {{ill|lt=December 3rd|Q2298|WD=Q2298|1=December 3}}, {{ill|lt=Hinomaru Motors|Q115 04700|WD=Q115 04700|lt=Hinomaru Bus}} operates the direct bus "Ebisu Liner" between {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yonago Airport|1=UNKNOWN}} and {{ill|lt=Sakaiminato Station|Q7402786|WD=Q7402786|1=Sakaiminato Station}}[http://mihojinja.or.jp/kotsu/#anchor0 [Limited Time] Ebisu Liner] - Miho Shrine (viewed March 8, 2019). . There is a parking lot next to the community center (free of charge, with space for more than a dozen cars) and a public toilet, and it is a 1-minute walk from the shrine. === Related books === * "Shinto Dictionary" edited and supervised by Motohiko Anzu and Yoshihiko Umeda, {{ill|lt=Jinja Shimpo|Q11590705|WD=Q11590705|1=Jinja Shinpō}}sha, 1968, 58 pages * Edited by Eiji Shirai and Masanori Toki, "Dictionary of Shrines" {{ill|lt=Tokyodo Publishing|Q11524645|WD=Q11524645|1=Tōkyōdō Shuppan}}, 1979, pp. 322-323 * {{ill|lt=Masaaki Suda|Q11619352|WD=Q11619352|1=Masaaki Sugata}} "Encyclopedia" to know about Japanese shrines, {{ill|lt=Nippon Bungeisha|Q7034281|WD=Q7034281|1=Nihon Bungeisha}}, 1989, 203 pages * {{ill|lt=Shunpei Ueyama|Q403579|WD=Q403579|1=Shunpei Ueyama}} et al., "Comprehensive list of Japanese shrines" {{ill|lt=Shinjinbutsu Oraisha|Q11501312|WD=Q11501312|1=Shin Jinbutsu Ōraisha. "Rekishi Dokuhon" Henshūbu}}, 1992, pp. 238-239 * {{Cite book |Japanese book |author=Yasuhiro Nonomura|authorlink=Yasuhiro Nonomura |chapter=Origin of Miho Shrine |title=Quarterly Cultural Heritage |issue=April 2002 issue |publisher={{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Soeisha|1=UNKNOWN}} |date=2002-04 |isbn=978-4-921070-13-7 |ref=Nonomura 2002 }} === Footnotes === {{Footnote help}} {{Reflist}} === Related items === {{Commons|Category:Miho-jinja}} * {{ill|lt=Legend of Hagoromo|Q1326754|WD=Q1326754|1=Swan maiden}} * {{ill|lt=Miho Shrine|Q11489249|WD=Q11489249|1=Miho Shrine (Q11489249)}} * {{ill|lt=Izumo Taisha|Q696362|WD=Q696362|1=Izumo-taisha}} * {{ill|lt=Blue Cobblestone Street|Q11662622|WD=Q11662622|1=Aoishidatami Street}} * {{ill|lt=Sunny Yokoyama|Q11304946|WD=Q11304946|1=Sunny Yokoyama}} - {{ill|lt=Shake|Q11588367|WD=Q11588367|1=Shake (social class)}} of Miho Shrine. Rather than becoming a priest, he pursued the path of {{ill|lt=aerobatics|Q373557|WD=Q373557|1=Aerobatics}}, and is currently a pilot for {{ill|lt=Peach Aviation|Q1376634|WD=Q1376634|1=Peach Aviation}}. === External link === * [http://mihojinja.or.jp/ Miho Shrine official website] {{ja icon}} {{Shinto horizontal}} {{Normdaten}} {{shinto-stub}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Miho Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Miho Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shinto shrine]] [[Category:Shikinaisha|Miho Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Izumo Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Izumo Province]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines]] [[Category:重要文化財 (建造物)]] [[Category:松江市の重要文化財]] [[Category:重要有形民俗文化財]] [[Category:島根県指定有形文化財]] [[Category:都道府県指定有形民俗文化財]] [[Category:島根県の登録有形文化財]] [[Category:江戸時代の建築]] [[Category:Architecture of the Taisho era]] [[Category:松江市の建築物]] [[Category:松江市の歴史]] [[Category:Taisha-zukuri]] [[Category:Tourist attractions in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:kkkkkkkkkkkkkk]] [[Category:nnnnnnnnn]] [[Category:qqqqqqq]]

Morotefune ritual |Main shrine = Mihozo|Map= {{Infobox mapframe|zoom=10|frame-width=180|type=point|marker=religious-shinto|shape-fill=#f5fffa|stroke-color=#006400|stroke-width=1|frame-latitude=35.508|frame-longitude=133.277}} {{Location map|Japan Shimane|label=Miho Shrine|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|position=left|float=center|width=180|caption=}} }} [[File: Shimane/Miho Shrine crest.png|250px|thumb|Shimane/Miho Shrine crest]] ``Miho Shrine'' is a {{ill|lt=Shrine|Q845945|WD=Q845945|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|lt=Shimane Prefecture|Q132751|WD=Q132751|1=Shimane Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Matsue City|Q207321|WD=Q207321|1=Matsue}}. {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinaisha|1=Shikinaisha|WD=Q134917286}}, and the former {{ill|lt=shakaku|Q10444029|WD=Q10444029|1=Shakaku}} was {{ill|UNKNOWN|WD=Q134917280|lt=Kokuheichusha|1=Kokuhei Chūsha}}. In addition to the divine virtue of prosperous business as Ebisu, he is also worshiped as the god of fishing and shipping, and the god of warding off insects in rice fields. Also, many {{ill|lt=musical instruments|Q34379|WD=Q34379|1=Musical instrument}} are dedicated to the god of ``noisemono''. === Enshrined God === {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi-kami|1=Ōkuninushi}}'s son {{ill|lt=Kotoshiro-nushi|Q8009611|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshiro-nushi|1=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto}} is enshrined in the right shrine, and {{ill|lt=Mihotsuhime|Q6378698|WD=Q6378698|lt=Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|1=Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto}}, the son of Okuninushi, is enshrined in the left shrine. Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto is the consort of ``Omononushi-kami,'' who is the Sakimitama/Kushimitama of Okuninushi-kami. Kotoshironushi no Mikoto is the child of {{ill|lt=Kamiya Tatehime|Q30935372|WD=Q30935372|lt=Kamuya Tatehime|1=Kamuyatate hime no mikoto}} and Okuninushi, so she is her stepmother. In ``{{ill|lt=Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|Q11395858|WD=Q11395858|1=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki}},'' there is a description that ``{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mihosusumi no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}},'' born between Ōanamochi no Mikoto (Okuninushi deity) and Nunasenamihime no Mikoto ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nunagawahime no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}}), sits in Mihosato. Originally, the only deity enshrined at our company was Mihosumi-no-Mikoto, but it seems that due to the influence of {{ill|lt=Kiki|Q842308|WD=Q842308|1=Kiki (Shinto)}}{{ill|lt=Japanese mythology|Q814158|WD=Q814158|lt=Mythology|1=Japanese mythology}}, Kotoshiro-nushi-kami and Mihotsu-hime-no-Mikoto were enshrined. === History === The origin of its founding is unknown, but it is an old shrine listed in the shrine register of ``{{ill|lt=Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|Q11395858|WD=Q11395858|1=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki}}'' compiled in {{ill|lt=8th century|Q8086|WD=Q8086|1=8th century}}. In {{ill|lt=Engishiki Shinmecho|Q11064932|WD=Q11064932|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}, you line up at a small shrine. From {{ill|lt=Medieval|Q12554|WD=Q12554|1=Middle Ages}}, {{ill|lt=Mr. Yokoyama|Q119822420|WD=Q119822420|1=Yokoyama clan}} became {{ill|lt=Shinto priest|Q60523|WD=Q60523|1=Kannushi}} {{ill|lt=hereditary|Q756689|WD=Q756689|1=Line of hereditary succession}}. From around {{ill|lt=early modern times|Q5308718|WD=Q5308718|1=Early modern period}}, it was said that ``Taisha ({{ill|lt=Izumo Taisha|Q696362|WD=Q696362|1=Izumo-taisha}}) alone is {{ill|lt=one visit|UNKNOWN|lt=one visit}},'' and the number of worshipers started to increase along with Izumo Taisha. Together with Izumo Taisha Shrine, it is collectively known as ``Izumo's Ebisu Daikoku''. In {{ill|lt=1885|Q7821|WD=Q7821|1=1885}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}18), it was listed as Kokupei Chusha, and after {{ill|lt=World War II|Q362|WD=Q362|1=World War II}} it became {{ill|lt=Beppyō Shrine|Q10898274|WD=Q10898274|1=Beppyo shrine}} of {{ill|lt=Shinja Honcho|Q908077|WD=Q908077|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. === Precincts === Miho Shrine building.JPG|Shrine building Betsugo Nigozen.JPG|Betsugo Nigozen (Koshirosu Okami) Betsugo Ogozen.JPG | Betsugo Ogozen (Mihotsuhime no Mikoto) Miho Shrine Shinto Gate.JPG|Shinmon {{ill|lt=2023|Q49622|WD=Q49622|1=2023}} ({{ill|lt=Reiwa|Q62609017|WD=Q62609017|1=Reiwa era}}5) The current main shrine was built after a fire in {{ill|lt=Kansei|Q1195131|WD=Q1195131|1=Kansei}}12 ({{ill|lt=1800|Q6875|WD=Q6875|1=1800}}). (era name)|Q1373146|Bunka 10th year}} ({{ill|lt=1813|Q6937|WD=Q6937|1=1813}}) {{ill|lt=#Nonomura 2002|UNKNOWN|lt=Nonomura 2002}}, p. 68. It is a special form of {{ill|lt=Taisha-zukuri|Q387874|WD=Q387874|1=Taisha-zukuri}} with two consecutive buildings on the left and right sides, and is called ``Miho-zukuri'' or ``Hiyoku Taisha-zukuri'' and is designated as an important cultural property of the country. It is not clear when this style was established. {{ill|lt=Horeki|Q1194397|WD=Q1194397|1=Hōreki}} In a document called "Haku-sama Goyo no Kaku" written in 1763, {{ill|lt=astronomical (era name)|Q1192853|WD=Q1192853|lt=Tenbun|1=Tenbun}} The company name is written as ``Miho''' Shrine'''' in the 3rd year (1534) article, and ``Miho'''Ryosha'''' in the 11th year (1583) article. Also, according to the "Kokuhei Chusha Miho Shrine Detailed Book" written in {{ill|lt=1886|Q7822|WD=Q7822|1=1886}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}19), for {{ill|lt=Motogame|Q1145064|WD=Q1145064|1=Genki (era)}} years ({{ill|lt=1570|Q6659|WD=Q6659|1=1570}} - There was only one main shrine until it was lost in the war in {{ill|lt=1573|Q6678|WD=Q6678|1=1573}}), but after that, for {{ill|lt=Bunroku|Q1373039|WD=Q1373039|1=Bunroku}} ({{ill|lt=1593|Q6772|WD=Q6772|1=1593}} - Until {{ill|lt=1596|Q6785|WD=Q6785|1=1596}}), it was rebuilt as it is today, with two main halls built on one foundation. From these two documents, it is estimated that as of the 3rd year of Tenbun ({{ill|lt=1534|Q6447|WD=Q6447|1=1534}}), it was a single-building shrine, and by the 11th year of Tensho ({{ill|lt=1583|Q6726|WD=Q6726|1=1583}}), it had become a two-building shrine called ``Ryosha.'' In addition, {{ill|lt=Hiroie Yoshikawa|Q1049766|WD=Q1049766|lt=Hiroie Yoshikawa|1=Kikkawa Hiroie}}, which was recorded as an auspicious day in May in {{ill|lt=Bunroku|Q1373039|WD=Q1373039|1=Bunroku}} 5th year ({{ill|lt=1596|Q6785|WD=Q6785|1=1596}}), is {{ja link|Bunroku-Keicho War|Q576338|When the building was built for the dispatch of troops to Korea}}, the ridge plate also read ``Hokenri Mihonoseki'''Ryo'' Shrine Palace, which proves that two shrine buildings were already standing side by side at that time. However, it is unknown whether the two shrine buildings at that time were connected as they are now. Due to repairs in {{ill|lt=1928|Q19715|WD=Q19715|1=1928}} ({{ill|lt=Showa|Q327567|WD=Q327567|1=Shōwa era}}3), the main shrine was moved about 100 meters from its original location to its current location, and the sacred area was expanded to complete its current form. 2002}}, p. 70. The roofs of the main shrine, worship hall, shrine gate, corridors, and entrance walls are currently {{ill|lt=cypress bark roofing|Q90373477|WD=Q90373477|lt=cypress bark|1=cypress bark roof}}, but before the repair, they were shingle roofs. There is a subsidiary shrine and Daigosha between the two main shrines, and three shrines and five shrines (Daigosha {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kamiya Tatehime no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}}, {{ill|lt=Numakawa Hime|Q11142832|WD=Q11142832|lt=Numakawa Hime no Mikoto|1=Nunakawahime}}, Himeko Shrine {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Himekeka Isuzuhime no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}}, {{ill|lt=Isuzuyorihime no Mikoto|Q10881557|WD=Q10881557|1=Isuzuyori-hime}}, Jinshisha Inasehime no Mikoto) is enshrined here. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === ; building * Miho Shrine main hall attached: 18 ridge plates - Bunka 10 ({{ill|lt=1813|Q6937|WD=Q6937|1=1813}}) === Important tangible folk cultural property (designated by the country) === * {{ill|lt=Morotebune|Q11632096|WD=Q11632096|1=Morotebune}} 2 ships * 846 songs dedicated to Miho Shrine * {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Soriko|1=UNKNOWN}} 1 ship === Prefecturally designated tangible cultural property === * Paper book and ink calligraphy handbook (Tekagami) ==== Prefecturally designated tangible folk cultural property ==== * 1 Avani included: 17 paddles, 20 Amba * 1 ship ==== Registered tangible cultural property ==== * Worship Hall - 1924 (Taisho 13) [https://www3.pref.shimane.jp/houdou/articles/156407 Shimane Prefecture Homepage (Press Release Materials)]. Designed by {{ill|lt=Chuta Ito|Q1050457|WD=Q1050457|1=Itō Chūta}} [https://www.fukumakan.jp/travel/8/1/ Fukumakan homepage (Miho Shrine/Ebisu Shrine)]. === Festival === The Aofushigaki ritual and the {{ill|lt=Morotebune|Q11632096|WD=Q11632096|1=Morotebune}} (Morotabune) ritual originate from the {{ill|lt=Kuniyoshi #Kokuyoshi myth and rice cultivation|Q11621119|WD=Q11621119|lt=Kokuyoshi myth|1=Kuni-yuzuri}}. The Morotefune ritual in December reenacts the story of {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi-no-Mikoto|UNKNOWN|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi-kami|1=Ōkuninushi}} sending a messenger to his son {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kotodai-nushi-kami|1=UNKNOWN}} to consult with him about the pros and cons of ceding the country, and the Aoshibagaki-gaki ritual in April, where Kotodai-nushi-kami, who had decided to cede the country, changed his ship into an Ao-shibagaki fence and carried it inside. He hides himself, but recreates the scene of being resurrected as a god again. {{ja icon}} - Suntory Channel, 2014. Our two members, who have avoided eating chicken, chicken, and eggs for a year and purified themselves at sea every day, fasted the day before, boarded two boats decorated with blue shibagaki, and after circling the port, visited Miho Shrine and offered offerings. Mihonoseki Regional Tourism Promotion Council official website. * {{ill|lt=January 1st|Q2150|WD=Q2150|1=January 1}} -- Saitan Festival * {{ill|lt=January 7th|Q2228|WD=Q2228|1=January 7}} -- First Ebisu Festival * Mid-January--Firecracker Ceremony (Tondo-san) [[File:Miho Shrine Firecracker Ceremony.jpg|Thumbnail|Miho Shrine Firecracker Ceremony]] * February Setsubun -- Setsubun Festival* {{ill|lt=April 7th|Q2505|WD=Q2505|1=April 7}} -- Reitaisai (Aoshibagaki Shinto Ritual): The Reitaisai is held in the morning, and the Aoshibagaki Shinto ritual is held in the afternoon. * {{ill|lt=April 13th|Q2498|WD=Q2498|1=April 13}} -- Fishing Festival * {{ill|lt=May 5th|Q2550|WD=Q2550|1=May 5}} -- Shinto ritual * {{ill|lt=August 7th|Q2781|WD=Q2781|1=August 7}} -- Insect detection ritual * Mid-September -- {{ill|lt=Urayasu no Mai|Q11558194|WD=Q11558194|1=Urayasu no mai}} (A junior high school girl dances in formal wear.) * {{ill|lt=December 3rd|Q2298|WD=Q2298|1=December 3}} -- Niiname-sai/Morotebune ritual === Namikiri Gohei and Tsukinami Gohei === ; Namisaki Gohei : Dedicated at the Aoshibagaki Shinto ritual. ; Monthly gohei : It is offered during the monthly festival on the 7th of every month. === Transportation === {{ill|lt=Matsue Station|Q1058652|WD=Q1058652|1=Matsue Station}} From platform 2, take the {{ill|lt=Ichibata Bus|Q11352955|WD=Q11352955|1=Ichibata Bus}} bound for Mihonoseki Terminal (about 40 minutes). From the Mihonoseki terminal end, transfer to the {{ill|lt=Matsue city community bus|Q11531653|WD=Q11531653|lt=Mihonoseki community bus|1=Mihonoseki community bus}} bound for {{ill|lt=Mihonoseki town|Q6845336|WD=Q6845336|lt=Mihonoseki|1=Mihonoseki, Shimane}} and get off at the Mihonoseki terminal (about 30 minutes). About 1 minute walk from Miho Shrine Iriguchi bus stop. {{ill|lt=Hatsumode|Q1032381|WD=Q1032381|1=Hatsumōde}} season, {{ill|lt=Golden Week|Q1137351|WD=Q1137351|1=Golden Week (Japan)}}, Saturdays, Sundays, holidays from summer to early winter, and {{ill|lt=December 3rd|Q2298|WD=Q2298|1=December 3}}, {{ill|lt=Hinomaru Motors|Q115 04700|WD=Q115 04700|lt=Hinomaru Bus}} operates the direct bus "Ebisu Liner" between {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yonago Airport|1=UNKNOWN}} and {{ill|lt=Sakaiminato Station|Q7402786|WD=Q7402786|1=Sakaiminato Station}}[http://mihojinja.or.jp/kotsu/#anchor0 [Limited Time] Ebisu Liner] - Miho Shrine (viewed March 8, 2019). . There is a parking lot next to the community center (free of charge, with space for more than a dozen cars) and a public toilet, and it is a 1-minute walk from the shrine. === Related books === * "Shinto Dictionary" edited and supervised by Motohiko Anzu and Yoshihiko Umeda, {{ill|lt=Jinja Shimpo|Q11590705|WD=Q11590705|1=Jinja Shinpō}}sha, 1968, 58 pages * Edited by Eiji Shirai and Masanori Toki, "Dictionary of Shrines" {{ill|lt=Tokyodo Publishing|Q11524645|WD=Q11524645|1=Tōkyōdō Shuppan}}, 1979, pp. 322-323 * {{ill|lt=Masaaki Suda|Q11619352|WD=Q11619352|1=Masaaki Sugata}} "Encyclopedia" to know about Japanese shrines, {{ill|lt=Nippon Bungeisha|Q7034281|WD=Q7034281|1=Nihon Bungeisha}}, 1989, 203 pages * {{ill|lt=Shunpei Ueyama|Q403579|WD=Q403579|1=Shunpei Ueyama}} et al., "Comprehensive list of Japanese shrines" {{ill|lt=Shinjinbutsu Oraisha|Q11501312|WD=Q11501312|1=Shin Jinbutsu Ōraisha. "Rekishi Dokuhon" Henshūbu}}, 1992, pp. 238-239 * {{Cite book |Japanese book |author=Yasuhiro Nonomura|authorlink=Yasuhiro Nonomura |chapter=Origin of Miho Shrine |title=Quarterly Cultural Heritage |issue=April 2002 issue |publisher={{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Soeisha|1=UNKNOWN}} |date=2002-04 |isbn=978-4-921070-13-7 |ref=Nonomura 2002 }} === Footnotes === {{Footnote help}} {{Reflist}} === Related items === {{Commons|Category:Miho-jinja}} * {{ill|lt=Legend of Hagoromo|Q1326754|WD=Q1326754|1=Swan maiden}} * {{ill|lt=Miho Shrine|Q11489249|WD=Q11489249|1=Miho Shrine (Q11489249)}} * {{ill|lt=Izumo Taisha|Q696362|WD=Q696362|1=Izumo-taisha}} * {{ill|lt=Blue Cobblestone Street|Q11662622|WD=Q11662622|1=Aoishidatami Street}} * {{ill|lt=Sunny Yokoyama|Q11304946|WD=Q11304946|1=Sunny Yokoyama}} - {{ill|lt=Shake|Q11588367|WD=Q11588367|1=Shake (social class)}} of Miho Shrine. Rather than becoming a priest, he pursued the path of {{ill|lt=aerobatics|Q373557|WD=Q373557|1=Aerobatics}}, and is currently a pilot for {{ill|lt=Peach Aviation|Q1376634|WD=Q1376634|1=Peach Aviation}}. === External link === * [http://mihojinja.or.jp/ Miho Shrine official website] {{ja icon}} {{Shinto horizontal}} {{Normdaten}} {{shinto-stub}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Miho Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Miho Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shinto shrine]] [[Category:Shikinaisha|Miho Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Izumo Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Izumo Province]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines]] [[Category:重要文化財 (建造物)]] [[Category:松江市の重要文化財]] [[Category:重要有形民俗文化財]] [[Category:Shimane Prefecture designated tangible cultural property]] [[Category:都道府県指定有形民俗文化財]] [[Category:島根県の登録有形文化財]] [[Category:江戸時代の建築]] [[Category:Architecture of the Taisho era]] [[Category:松江市の建築物]] [[Category:松江市の歴史]] [[Category:Taisha-zukuri]] [[Category:Tourist attractions in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:kkkkkkkkkkkkkk]] [[Category:nnnnnnnnn]] [[Category:qqqqqqq]]

Morotefune ritual |Main shrine = Mihozo|Map= {{Infobox mapframe|zoom=10|frame-width=180|type=point|marker=religious-shinto|shape-fill=#f5fffa|stroke-color=#006400|stroke-width=1|frame-latitude=35.508|frame-longitude=133.277}} {{Location map|Japan Shimane|label=Miho Shrine|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|position=left|float=center|width=180|caption=}} }} [[File: Shimane/Miho Shrine crest.png|250px|thumb|Shimane/Miho Shrine crest]] ``Miho Shrine'' is a {{ill|lt=Shrine|Q845945|WD=Q845945|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|lt=Shimane Prefecture|Q132751|WD=Q132751|1=Shimane Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Matsue City|Q207321|WD=Q207321|1=Matsue}}. {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinaisha|1=Shikinaisha|WD=Q134917286}}, and the former {{ill|lt=shakaku|Q10444029|WD=Q10444029|1=Shakaku}} was {{ill|UNKNOWN|WD=Q134917280|lt=Kokuheichusha|1=Kokuhei Chūsha}}. In addition to the divine virtue of prosperous business as Ebisu, he is also worshiped as the god of fishing and shipping, and the god of warding off insects in rice fields. Also, many {{ill|lt=musical instruments|Q34379|WD=Q34379|1=Musical instrument}} are dedicated to the god of ``noisemono''. === Enshrined God === {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi-kami|1=Ōkuninushi}}'s son {{ill|lt=Kotoshiro-nushi|Q8009611|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshiro-nushi|1=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto}} is enshrined in the right shrine, and {{ill|lt=Mihotsuhime|Q6378698|WD=Q6378698|lt=Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|1=Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto}}, the son of Okuninushi, is enshrined in the left shrine. Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto is the consort of ``Omononushi-kami,'' who is the Sakimitama/Kushimitama of Okuninushi-kami. Kotoshironushi no Mikoto is the child of {{ill|lt=Kamiya Tatehime|Q30935372|WD=Q30935372|lt=Kamuya Tatehime|1=Kamuyatate hime no mikoto}} and Okuninushi, so she is her stepmother. In ``{{ill|lt=Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|Q11395858|WD=Q11395858|1=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki}},'' there is a description that ``{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mihosusumi no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}},'' born between Ōanamochi no Mikoto (Okuninushi deity) and Nunasenamihime no Mikoto ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nunagawahime no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}}), sits in Mihosato. Originally, the only deity enshrined at our company was Mihosumi-no-Mikoto, but it seems that due to the influence of {{ill|lt=Kiki|Q842308|WD=Q842308|1=Kiki (Shinto)}}{{ill|lt=Japanese mythology|Q814158|WD=Q814158|lt=Mythology|1=Japanese mythology}}, Kotoshiro-nushi-kami and Mihotsu-hime-no-Mikoto were enshrined. === History === The origin of its founding is unknown, but it is an old shrine listed in the shrine register of ``{{ill|lt=Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|Q11395858|WD=Q11395858|1=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki}}'' compiled in {{ill|lt=8th century|Q8086|WD=Q8086|1=8th century}}. In {{ill|lt=Engishiki Shinmecho|Q11064932|WD=Q11064932|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}, you line up at a small shrine. From {{ill|lt=Medieval|Q12554|WD=Q12554|1=Middle Ages}}, {{ill|lt=Mr. Yokoyama|Q119822420|WD=Q119822420|1=Yokoyama clan}} became {{ill|lt=Shinto priest|Q60523|WD=Q60523|1=Kannushi}} {{ill|lt=hereditary|Q756689|WD=Q756689|1=Line of hereditary succession}}. From around {{ill|lt=early modern times|Q5308718|WD=Q5308718|1=Early modern period}}, it was said that ``Taisha ({{ill|lt=Izumo Taisha|Q696362|WD=Q696362|1=Izumo-taisha}}) alone is {{ill|lt=one visit|UNKNOWN|lt=one visit}},'' and the number of worshipers started to increase along with Izumo Taisha. Together with Izumo Taisha Shrine, it is collectively known as ``Izumo's Ebisu Daikoku''. In {{ill|lt=1885|Q7821|WD=Q7821|1=1885}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}18), it was listed as Kokupei Chusha, and after {{ill|lt=World War II|Q362|WD=Q362|1=World War II}} it became {{ill|lt=Beppyō Shrine|Q10898274|WD=Q10898274|1=Beppyo shrine}} of {{ill|lt=Shinja Honcho|Q908077|WD=Q908077|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. === Precincts === Miho Shrine building.JPG|Shrine building Betsugo Nigozen.JPG|Betsugo Nigozen (Koshirosu Okami) Betsugo Ogozen.JPG | Betsugo Ogozen (Mihotsuhime no Mikoto) Miho Shrine Shinto Gate.JPG|Shinmon {{ill|lt=2023|Q49622|WD=Q49622|1=2023}} ({{ill|lt=Reiwa|Q62609017|WD=Q62609017|1=Reiwa era}}5) The current main shrine was built after a fire in {{ill|lt=Kansei|Q1195131|WD=Q1195131|1=Kansei}}12 ({{ill|lt=1800|Q6875|WD=Q6875|1=1800}}). (era name)|Q1373146|Bunka 10th year}} ({{ill|lt=1813|Q6937|WD=Q6937|1=1813}}) {{ill|lt=#Nonomura 2002|UNKNOWN|lt=Nonomura 2002}}, p. 68. It is a special form of {{ill|lt=Taisha-zukuri|Q387874|WD=Q387874|1=Taisha-zukuri}} with two consecutive buildings on the left and right sides, and is called ``Miho-zukuri'' or ``Hiyoku Taisha-zukuri'' and is designated as an important cultural property of the country. It is not clear when this style was established. {{ill|lt=Horeki|Q1194397|WD=Q1194397|1=Hōreki}} In a document called "Haku-sama Goyo no Kaku" written in 1763, {{ill|lt=astronomical (era name)|Q1192853|WD=Q1192853|lt=Tenbun|1=Tenbun}} The company name is written as ``Miho''' Shrine'''' in the 3rd year (1534) article, and ``Miho'''Ryosha'''' in the 11th year (1583) article. Also, according to the "Kokuhei Chusha Miho Shrine Detailed Book" written in {{ill|lt=1886|Q7822|WD=Q7822|1=1886}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}19), for {{ill|lt=Motogame|Q1145064|WD=Q1145064|1=Genki (era)}} years ({{ill|lt=1570|Q6659|WD=Q6659|1=1570}} - There was only one main shrine until it was lost in the war in {{ill|lt=1573|Q6678|WD=Q6678|1=1573}}), but after that, for {{ill|lt=Bunroku|Q1373039|WD=Q1373039|1=Bunroku}} ({{ill|lt=1593|Q6772|WD=Q6772|1=1593}} - Until {{ill|lt=1596|Q6785|WD=Q6785|1=1596}}), it was rebuilt as it is today, with two main halls built on one foundation. From these two documents, it is estimated that as of the 3rd year of Tenbun ({{ill|lt=1534|Q6447|WD=Q6447|1=1534}}), it was a single-building shrine, and by the 11th year of Tensho ({{ill|lt=1583|Q6726|WD=Q6726|1=1583}}), it had become a two-building shrine called ``Ryosha.'' In addition, {{ill|lt=Hiroie Yoshikawa|Q1049766|WD=Q1049766|lt=Hiroie Yoshikawa|1=Kikkawa Hiroie}}, which was recorded as an auspicious day in May in {{ill|lt=Bunroku|Q1373039|WD=Q1373039|1=Bunroku}} 5th year ({{ill|lt=1596|Q6785|WD=Q6785|1=1596}}), is {{ja link|Bunroku-Keicho War|Q576338|When the building was built for the dispatch of troops to Korea}}, the ridge plate also read ``Hokenri Mihonoseki'''Ryo'' Shrine Palace, which proves that two shrine buildings were already standing side by side at that time. However, it is unknown whether the two shrine buildings at that time were connected as they are now. Due to repairs in {{ill|lt=1928|Q19715|WD=Q19715|1=1928}} ({{ill|lt=Showa|Q327567|WD=Q327567|1=Shōwa era}}3), the main shrine was moved about 100 meters from its original location to its current location, and the sacred area was expanded to complete its current form. 2002}}, p. 70. The roofs of the main shrine, worship hall, shrine gate, corridors, and entrance walls are currently {{ill|lt=cypress bark roofing|Q90373477|WD=Q90373477|lt=cypress bark|1=cypress bark roof}}, but before the repair, they were shingle roofs. There is a subsidiary shrine and Daigosha between the two main shrines, and three shrines and five shrines (Daigosha {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kamiya Tatehime no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}}, {{ill|lt=Numakawa Hime|Q11142832|WD=Q11142832|lt=Numakawa Hime no Mikoto|1=Nunakawahime}}, Himeko Shrine {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Himekeka Isuzuhime no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}}, {{ill|lt=Isuzuyorihime no Mikoto|Q10881557|WD=Q10881557|1=Isuzuyori-hime}}, Jinshisha Inasehime no Mikoto) is enshrined here. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === ; building * Miho Shrine main hall attached: 18 ridge plates - Bunka 10 ({{ill|lt=1813|Q6937|WD=Q6937|1=1813}}) === Important tangible folk cultural property (designated by the country) === * {{ill|lt=Morotebune|Q11632096|WD=Q11632096|1=Morotebune}} 2 ships * 846 songs dedicated to Miho Shrine * {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Soriko|1=UNKNOWN}} 1 ship === Prefecturally designated tangible cultural property === * Paper book and ink calligraphy handbook (Tekagami) ==== Prefecturally designated tangible folk cultural property ==== * 1 Avani included: 17 paddles, 20 Amba * 1 ship ==== Registered tangible cultural property ==== * Worship Hall - 1924 (Taisho 13) [https://www3.pref.shimane.jp/houdou/articles/156407 Shimane Prefecture Homepage (Press Release Materials)]. Designed by {{ill|lt=Chuta Ito|Q1050457|WD=Q1050457|1=Itō Chūta}} [https://www.fukumakan.jp/travel/8/1/ Fukumakan homepage (Miho Shrine/Ebisu Shrine)]. === Festival === The Aofushigaki ritual and the {{ill|lt=Morotebune|Q11632096|WD=Q11632096|1=Morotebune}} (Morotabune) ritual originate from the {{ill|lt=Kuniyoshi #Kokuyoshi myth and rice cultivation|Q11621119|WD=Q11621119|lt=Kokuyoshi myth|1=Kuni-yuzuri}}. The Morotefune ritual in December reenacts the story of {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi-no-Mikoto|UNKNOWN|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi-kami|1=Ōkuninushi}} sending a messenger to his son {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kotodai-nushi-kami|1=UNKNOWN}} to consult with him about the pros and cons of ceding the country, and the Aoshibagaki-gaki ritual in April, where Kotodai-nushi-kami, who had decided to cede the country, changed his ship into an Ao-shibagaki fence and carried it inside. He hides himself, but recreates the scene of being resurrected as a god again. {{ja icon}} - Suntory Channel, 2014. Our two members, who have avoided eating chicken, chicken, and eggs for a year and purified themselves at sea every day, fasted the day before, boarded two boats decorated with blue shibagaki, and after circling the port, visited Miho Shrine and offered offerings. Mihonoseki Regional Tourism Promotion Council official website. * {{ill|lt=January 1st|Q2150|WD=Q2150|1=January 1}} -- Saitan Festival * {{ill|lt=January 7th|Q2228|WD=Q2228|1=January 7}} -- First Ebisu Festival * Mid-January--Firecracker Ceremony (Tondo-san) [[File:Miho Shrine Firecracker Ceremony.jpg|Thumbnail|Miho Shrine Firecracker Ceremony]] * February Setsubun -- Setsubun Festival* {{ill|lt=April 7th|Q2505|WD=Q2505|1=April 7}} -- Reitaisai (Aoshibagaki Shinto Ritual): The Reitaisai is held in the morning, and the Aoshibagaki Shinto ritual is held in the afternoon. * {{ill|lt=April 13th|Q2498|WD=Q2498|1=April 13}} -- Fishing Festival * {{ill|lt=May 5th|Q2550|WD=Q2550|1=May 5}} -- Shinto ritual * {{ill|lt=August 7th|Q2781|WD=Q2781|1=August 7}} -- Insect detection ritual * Mid-September -- {{ill|lt=Urayasu no Mai|Q11558194|WD=Q11558194|1=Urayasu no mai}} (A junior high school girl dances in formal wear.) * {{ill|lt=December 3rd|Q2298|WD=Q2298|1=December 3}} -- Niiname-sai/Morotebune ritual === Namikiri Gohei and Tsukinami Gohei === ; Namisaki Gohei : Dedicated at the Aoshibagaki Shinto ritual. ; Monthly gohei : It is offered during the monthly festival on the 7th of every month. === Transportation === {{ill|lt=Matsue Station|Q1058652|WD=Q1058652|1=Matsue Station}} From platform 2, take the {{ill|lt=Ichibata Bus|Q11352955|WD=Q11352955|1=Ichibata Bus}} bound for Mihonoseki Terminal (about 40 minutes). From the Mihonoseki terminal end, transfer to the {{ill|lt=Matsue city community bus|Q11531653|WD=Q11531653|lt=Mihonoseki community bus|1=Mihonoseki community bus}} bound for {{ill|lt=Mihonoseki town|Q6845336|WD=Q6845336|lt=Mihonoseki|1=Mihonoseki, Shimane}} and get off at the Mihonoseki terminal (about 30 minutes). About 1 minute walk from Miho Shrine Iriguchi bus stop. {{ill|lt=Hatsumode|Q1032381|WD=Q1032381|1=Hatsumōde}} season, {{ill|lt=Golden Week|Q1137351|WD=Q1137351|1=Golden Week (Japan)}}, Saturdays, Sundays, holidays from summer to early winter, and {{ill|lt=December 3rd|Q2298|WD=Q2298|1=December 3}}, {{ill|lt=Hinomaru Motors|Q115 04700|WD=Q115 04700|lt=Hinomaru Bus}} operates the direct bus "Ebisu Liner" between {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yonago Airport|1=UNKNOWN}} and {{ill|lt=Sakaiminato Station|Q7402786|WD=Q7402786|1=Sakaiminato Station}}[http://mihojinja.or.jp/kotsu/#anchor0 [Limited Time] Ebisu Liner] - Miho Shrine (viewed March 8, 2019). . There is a parking lot next to the community center (free of charge, with space for more than a dozen cars) and a public toilet, and it is a 1-minute walk from the shrine. === Related books === * "Shinto Dictionary" edited and supervised by Motohiko Anzu and Yoshihiko Umeda, {{ill|lt=Jinja Shimpo|Q11590705|WD=Q11590705|1=Jinja Shinpō}}sha, 1968, 58 pages * Edited by Eiji Shirai and Masanori Toki, "Dictionary of Shrines" {{ill|lt=Tokyodo Publishing|Q11524645|WD=Q11524645|1=Tōkyōdō Shuppan}}, 1979, pp. 322-323 * {{ill|lt=Masaaki Suda|Q11619352|WD=Q11619352|1=Masaaki Sugata}} "Encyclopedia" to know about Japanese shrines, {{ill|lt=Nippon Bungeisha|Q7034281|WD=Q7034281|1=Nihon Bungeisha}}, 1989, 203 pages * {{ill|lt=Shunpei Ueyama|Q403579|WD=Q403579|1=Shunpei Ueyama}} et al., "Comprehensive list of Japanese shrines" {{ill|lt=Shinjinbutsu Oraisha|Q11501312|WD=Q11501312|1=Shin Jinbutsu Ōraisha. "Rekishi Dokuhon" Henshūbu}}, 1992, pp. 238-239 * {{Cite book |Japanese book |author=Yasuhiro Nonomura|authorlink=Yasuhiro Nonomura |chapter=Origin of Miho Shrine |title=Quarterly Cultural Heritage |issue=April 2002 issue |publisher={{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Soeisha|1=UNKNOWN}} |date=2002-04 |isbn=978-4-921070-13-7 |ref=Nonomura 2002 }} === Footnotes === {{Footnote help}} {{Reflist}} === Related items === {{Commons|Category:Miho-jinja}} * {{ill|lt=Legend of Hagoromo|Q1326754|WD=Q1326754|1=Swan maiden}} * {{ill|lt=Miho Shrine|Q11489249|WD=Q11489249|1=Miho Shrine (Q11489249)}} * {{ill|lt=Izumo Taisha|Q696362|WD=Q696362|1=Izumo-taisha}} * {{ill|lt=Blue Cobblestone Street|Q11662622|WD=Q11662622|1=Aoishidatami Street}} * {{ill|lt=Sunny Yokoyama|Q11304946|WD=Q11304946|1=Sunny Yokoyama}} - {{ill|lt=Shake|Q11588367|WD=Q11588367|1=Shake (social class)}} of Miho Shrine. Rather than becoming a priest, he pursued the path of {{ill|lt=aerobatics|Q373557|WD=Q373557|1=Aerobatics}}, and is currently a pilot for {{ill|lt=Peach Aviation|Q1376634|WD=Q1376634|1=Peach Aviation}}. === External link === * [http://mihojinja.or.jp/ Miho Shrine official website] {{ja icon}} {{Shinto horizontal}} {{Normdaten}} {{shinto-stub}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Miho Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Miho Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shinto shrine]] [[Category:Shikinaisha|Miho Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Izumo Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Izumo Province]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines]] [[Category:重要文化財 (建造物)]] [[Category:松江市の重要文化財]] [[Category:重要有形民俗文化財]] [[Category:Shimane Prefecture designated tangible cultural property]] [[Category:Prefecture-designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:島根県の登録有形文化財]] [[Category:江戸時代の建築]] [[Category:Architecture of the Taisho era]] [[Category:松江市の建築物]] [[Category:松江市の歴史]] [[Category:Taisha-zukuri]] [[Category:Tourist attractions in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:kkkkkkkkkkkkkk]] [[Category:nnnnnnnnn]] [[Category:qqqqqqq]]

Morotefune ritual |Main shrine = Mihozo|Map= {{Infobox mapframe|zoom=10|frame-width=180|type=point|marker=religious-shinto|shape-fill=#f5fffa|stroke-color=#006400|stroke-width=1|frame-latitude=35.508|frame-longitude=133.277}} {{Location map|Japan Shimane|label=Miho Shrine|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|position=left|float=center|width=180|caption=}} }} [[File: Shimane/Miho Shrine crest.png|250px|thumb|Shimane/Miho Shrine crest]] ``Miho Shrine'' is a {{ill|lt=Shrine|Q845945|WD=Q845945|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|lt=Shimane Prefecture|Q132751|WD=Q132751|1=Shimane Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Matsue City|Q207321|WD=Q207321|1=Matsue}}. {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinaisha|1=Shikinaisha|WD=Q134917286}}, and the former {{ill|lt=shakaku|Q10444029|WD=Q10444029|1=Shakaku}} was {{ill|UNKNOWN|WD=Q134917280|lt=Kokuheichusha|1=Kokuhei Chūsha}}. In addition to the divine virtue of prosperous business as Ebisu, he is also worshiped as the god of fishing and shipping, and the god of warding off insects in rice fields. Also, many {{ill|lt=musical instruments|Q34379|WD=Q34379|1=Musical instrument}} are dedicated to the god of ``noisemono''. === Enshrined God === {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi-kami|1=Ōkuninushi}}'s son {{ill|lt=Kotoshiro-nushi|Q8009611|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshiro-nushi|1=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto}} is enshrined in the right shrine, and {{ill|lt=Mihotsuhime|Q6378698|WD=Q6378698|lt=Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|1=Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto}}, the son of Okuninushi, is enshrined in the left shrine. Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto is the consort of ``Omononushi-kami,'' who is the Sakimitama/Kushimitama of Okuninushi-kami. Kotoshironushi no Mikoto is the child of {{ill|lt=Kamiya Tatehime|Q30935372|WD=Q30935372|lt=Kamuya Tatehime|1=Kamuyatate hime no mikoto}} and Okuninushi, so she is her stepmother. In ``{{ill|lt=Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|Q11395858|WD=Q11395858|1=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki}},'' there is a description that ``{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mihosusumi no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}},'' born between Ōanamochi no Mikoto (Okuninushi deity) and Nunasenamihime no Mikoto ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nunagawahime no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}}), sits in Mihosato. Originally, the only deity enshrined at our company was Mihosumi-no-Mikoto, but it seems that due to the influence of {{ill|lt=Kiki|Q842308|WD=Q842308|1=Kiki (Shinto)}}{{ill|lt=Japanese mythology|Q814158|WD=Q814158|lt=Mythology|1=Japanese mythology}}, Kotoshiro-nushi-kami and Mihotsu-hime-no-Mikoto were enshrined. === History === The origin of its founding is unknown, but it is an old shrine listed in the shrine register of ``{{ill|lt=Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|Q11395858|WD=Q11395858|1=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki}}'' compiled in {{ill|lt=8th century|Q8086|WD=Q8086|1=8th century}}. In {{ill|lt=Engishiki Shinmecho|Q11064932|WD=Q11064932|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}, you line up at a small shrine. From {{ill|lt=Medieval|Q12554|WD=Q12554|1=Middle Ages}}, {{ill|lt=Mr. Yokoyama|Q119822420|WD=Q119822420|1=Yokoyama clan}} became {{ill|lt=Shinto priest|Q60523|WD=Q60523|1=Kannushi}} {{ill|lt=hereditary|Q756689|WD=Q756689|1=Line of hereditary succession}}. From around {{ill|lt=early modern times|Q5308718|WD=Q5308718|1=Early modern period}}, it was said that ``Taisha ({{ill|lt=Izumo Taisha|Q696362|WD=Q696362|1=Izumo-taisha}}) alone is {{ill|lt=one visit|UNKNOWN|lt=one visit}},'' and the number of worshipers started to increase along with Izumo Taisha. Together with Izumo Taisha Shrine, it is collectively known as ``Izumo's Ebisu Daikoku''. In {{ill|lt=1885|Q7821|WD=Q7821|1=1885}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}18), it was listed as Kokupei Chusha, and after {{ill|lt=World War II|Q362|WD=Q362|1=World War II}} it became {{ill|lt=Beppyō Shrine|Q10898274|WD=Q10898274|1=Beppyo shrine}} of {{ill|lt=Shinja Honcho|Q908077|WD=Q908077|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. === Precincts === Miho Shrine building.JPG|Shrine building Betsugo Nigozen.JPG|Betsugo Nigozen (Koshirosu Okami) Betsugo Ogozen.JPG | Betsugo Ogozen (Mihotsuhime no Mikoto) Miho Shrine Shinto Gate.JPG|Shinmon {{ill|lt=2023|Q49622|WD=Q49622|1=2023}} ({{ill|lt=Reiwa|Q62609017|WD=Q62609017|1=Reiwa era}}5) The current main shrine was built after a fire in {{ill|lt=Kansei|Q1195131|WD=Q1195131|1=Kansei}}12 ({{ill|lt=1800|Q6875|WD=Q6875|1=1800}}). (era name)|Q1373146|Bunka 10th year}} ({{ill|lt=1813|Q6937|WD=Q6937|1=1813}}) {{ill|lt=#Nonomura 2002|UNKNOWN|lt=Nonomura 2002}}, p. 68. It is a special form of {{ill|lt=Taisha-zukuri|Q387874|WD=Q387874|1=Taisha-zukuri}} with two consecutive buildings on the left and right sides, and is called ``Miho-zukuri'' or ``Hiyoku Taisha-zukuri'' and is designated as an important cultural property of the country. It is not clear when this style was established. {{ill|lt=Horeki|Q1194397|WD=Q1194397|1=Hōreki}} In a document called "Haku-sama Goyo no Kaku" written in 1763, {{ill|lt=astronomical (era name)|Q1192853|WD=Q1192853|lt=Tenbun|1=Tenbun}} The company name is written as ``Miho''' Shrine'''' in the 3rd year (1534) article, and ``Miho'''Ryosha'''' in the 11th year (1583) article. Also, according to the "Kokuhei Chusha Miho Shrine Detailed Book" written in {{ill|lt=1886|Q7822|WD=Q7822|1=1886}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}19), for {{ill|lt=Motogame|Q1145064|WD=Q1145064|1=Genki (era)}} years ({{ill|lt=1570|Q6659|WD=Q6659|1=1570}} - There was only one main shrine until it was lost in the war in {{ill|lt=1573|Q6678|WD=Q6678|1=1573}}), but after that, for {{ill|lt=Bunroku|Q1373039|WD=Q1373039|1=Bunroku}} ({{ill|lt=1593|Q6772|WD=Q6772|1=1593}} - Until {{ill|lt=1596|Q6785|WD=Q6785|1=1596}}), it was rebuilt as it is today, with two main halls built on one foundation. From these two documents, it is estimated that as of the 3rd year of Tenbun ({{ill|lt=1534|Q6447|WD=Q6447|1=1534}}), it was a single-building shrine, and by the 11th year of Tensho ({{ill|lt=1583|Q6726|WD=Q6726|1=1583}}), it had become a two-building shrine called ``Ryosha.'' In addition, {{ill|lt=Hiroie Yoshikawa|Q1049766|WD=Q1049766|lt=Hiroie Yoshikawa|1=Kikkawa Hiroie}}, which was recorded as an auspicious day in May in {{ill|lt=Bunroku|Q1373039|WD=Q1373039|1=Bunroku}} 5th year ({{ill|lt=1596|Q6785|WD=Q6785|1=1596}}), is {{ja link|Bunroku-Keicho War|Q576338|When the building was built for the dispatch of troops to Korea}}, the ridge plate also read ``Hokenri Mihonoseki'''Ryo'' Shrine Palace, which proves that two shrine buildings were already standing side by side at that time. However, it is unknown whether the two shrine buildings at that time were connected as they are now. Due to repairs in {{ill|lt=1928|Q19715|WD=Q19715|1=1928}} ({{ill|lt=Showa|Q327567|WD=Q327567|1=Shōwa era}}3), the main shrine was moved about 100 meters from its original location to its current location, and the sacred area was expanded to complete its current form. 2002}}, p. 70. The roofs of the main shrine, worship hall, shrine gate, corridors, and entrance walls are currently {{ill|lt=cypress bark roofing|Q90373477|WD=Q90373477|lt=cypress bark|1=cypress bark roof}}, but before the repair, they were shingle roofs. There is a subsidiary shrine and Daigosha between the two main shrines, and three shrines and five shrines (Daigosha {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kamiya Tatehime no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}}, {{ill|lt=Numakawa Hime|Q11142832|WD=Q11142832|lt=Numakawa Hime no Mikoto|1=Nunakawahime}}, Himeko Shrine {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Himekeka Isuzuhime no Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}}, {{ill|lt=Isuzuyorihime no Mikoto|Q10881557|WD=Q10881557|1=Isuzuyori-hime}}, Jinshisha Inasehime no Mikoto) is enshrined here. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === ; building * Miho Shrine main hall attached: 18 ridge plates - Bunka 10 ({{ill|lt=1813|Q6937|WD=Q6937|1=1813}}) === Important tangible folk cultural property (designated by the country) === * {{ill|lt=Morotebune|Q11632096|WD=Q11632096|1=Morotebune}} 2 ships * 846 songs dedicated to Miho Shrine * {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Soriko|1=UNKNOWN}} 1 ship === Prefecturally designated tangible cultural property === * Paper book and ink calligraphy handbook (Tekagami) ==== Prefecturally designated tangible folk cultural property ==== * 1 Avani included: 17 paddles, 20 Amba * 1 ship ==== Registered tangible cultural property ==== * Worship Hall - 1924 (Taisho 13) [https://www3.pref.shimane.jp/houdou/articles/156407 Shimane Prefecture Homepage (Press Release Materials)]. Designed by {{ill|lt=Chuta Ito|Q1050457|WD=Q1050457|1=Itō Chūta}} [https://www.fukumakan.jp/travel/8/1/ Fukumakan homepage (Miho Shrine/Ebisu Shrine)]. === Festival === The Aofushigaki ritual and the {{ill|lt=Morotebune|Q11632096|WD=Q11632096|1=Morotebune}} (Morotabune) ritual originate from the {{ill|lt=Kuniyoshi #Kokuyoshi myth and rice cultivation|Q11621119|WD=Q11621119|lt=Kokuyoshi myth|1=Kuni-yuzuri}}. The Morotefune ritual in December reenacts the story of {{ill|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi-no-Mikoto|UNKNOWN|WD=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi-kami|1=Ōkuninushi}} sending a messenger to his son {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kotodai-nushi-kami|1=UNKNOWN}} to consult with him about the pros and cons of ceding the country, and the Aoshibagaki-gaki ritual in April, where Kotodai-nushi-kami, who had decided to cede the country, changed his ship into an Ao-shibagaki fence and carried it inside. He hides himself, but recreates the scene of being resurrected as a god again. {{ja icon}} - Suntory Channel, 2014. Our two members, who have avoided eating chicken, chicken, and eggs for a year and purified themselves at sea every day, fasted the day before, boarded two boats decorated with blue shibagaki, and after circling the port, visited Miho Shrine and offered offerings. Mihonoseki Regional Tourism Promotion Council official website. * {{ill|lt=January 1st|Q2150|WD=Q2150|1=January 1}} -- Saitan Festival * {{ill|lt=January 7th|Q2228|WD=Q2228|1=January 7}} -- First Ebisu Festival * Mid-January--Firecracker Ceremony (Tondo-san) [[File:Miho Shrine Firecracker Ceremony.jpg|Thumbnail|Miho Shrine Firecracker Ceremony]] * February Setsubun -- Setsubun Festival* {{ill|lt=April 7th|Q2505|WD=Q2505|1=April 7}} -- Reitaisai (Aoshibagaki Shinto Ritual): The Reitaisai is held in the morning, and the Aoshibagaki Shinto ritual is held in the afternoon. * {{ill|lt=April 13th|Q2498|WD=Q2498|1=April 13}} -- Fishing Festival * {{ill|lt=May 5th|Q2550|WD=Q2550|1=May 5}} -- Shinto ritual * {{ill|lt=August 7th|Q2781|WD=Q2781|1=August 7}} -- Insect detection ritual * Mid-September -- {{ill|lt=Urayasu no Mai|Q11558194|WD=Q11558194|1=Urayasu no mai}} (A junior high school girl dances in formal wear.) * {{ill|lt=December 3rd|Q2298|WD=Q2298|1=December 3}} -- Niiname-sai/Morotebune ritual === Namikiri Gohei and Tsukinami Gohei === ; Namisaki Gohei : Dedicated at the Aoshibagaki Shinto ritual. ; Monthly gohei : It is offered during the monthly festival on the 7th of every month. === Transportation === {{ill|lt=Matsue Station|Q1058652|WD=Q1058652|1=Matsue Station}} From platform 2, take the {{ill|lt=Ichibata Bus|Q11352955|WD=Q11352955|1=Ichibata Bus}} bound for Mihonoseki Terminal (about 40 minutes). From the Mihonoseki terminal end, transfer to the {{ill|lt=Matsue city community bus|Q11531653|WD=Q11531653|lt=Mihonoseki community bus|1=Mihonoseki community bus}} bound for {{ill|lt=Mihonoseki town|Q6845336|WD=Q6845336|lt=Mihonoseki|1=Mihonoseki, Shimane}} and get off at the Mihonoseki terminal (about 30 minutes). About 1 minute walk from Miho Shrine Iriguchi bus stop. {{ill|lt=Hatsumode|Q1032381|WD=Q1032381|1=Hatsumōde}} season, {{ill|lt=Golden Week|Q1137351|WD=Q1137351|1=Golden Week (Japan)}}, Saturdays, Sundays, holidays from summer to early winter, and {{ill|lt=December 3rd|Q2298|WD=Q2298|1=December 3}}, {{ill|lt=Hinomaru Motors|Q115 04700|WD=Q115 04700|lt=Hinomaru Bus}} operates the direct bus "Ebisu Liner" between {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yonago Airport|1=UNKNOWN}} and {{ill|lt=Sakaiminato Station|Q7402786|WD=Q7402786|1=Sakaiminato Station}}[http://mihojinja.or.jp/kotsu/#anchor0 [Limited Time] Ebisu Liner] - Miho Shrine (viewed March 8, 2019). . There is a parking lot next to the community center (free of charge, with space for more than a dozen cars) and a public toilet, and it is a 1-minute walk from the shrine. === Related books === * "Shinto Dictionary" edited and supervised by Motohiko Anzu and Yoshihiko Umeda, {{ill|lt=Jinja Shimpo|Q11590705|WD=Q11590705|1=Jinja Shinpō}}sha, 1968, 58 pages * Edited by Eiji Shirai and Masanori Toki, "Dictionary of Shrines" {{ill|lt=Tokyodo Publishing|Q11524645|WD=Q11524645|1=Tōkyōdō Shuppan}}, 1979, pp. 322-323 * {{ill|lt=Masaaki Suda|Q11619352|WD=Q11619352|1=Masaaki Sugata}} "Encyclopedia" to know about Japanese shrines, {{ill|lt=Nippon Bungeisha|Q7034281|WD=Q7034281|1=Nihon Bungeisha}}, 1989, 203 pages * {{ill|lt=Shunpei Ueyama|Q403579|WD=Q403579|1=Shunpei Ueyama}} et al., "Comprehensive list of Japanese shrines" {{ill|lt=Shinjinbutsu Oraisha|Q11501312|WD=Q11501312|1=Shin Jinbutsu Ōraisha. "Rekishi Dokuhon" Henshūbu}}, 1992, pp. 238-239 * {{Cite book |Japanese book |author=Yasuhiro Nonomura|authorlink=Yasuhiro Nonomura |chapter=Origin of Miho Shrine |title=Quarterly Cultural Heritage |issue=April 2002 issue |publisher={{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Soeisha|1=UNKNOWN}} |date=2002-04 |isbn=978-4-921070-13-7 |ref=Nonomura 2002 }} === Footnotes === {{Footnote help}} {{Reflist}} === Related items === {{Commons|Category:Miho-jinja}} * {{ill|lt=Legend of Hagoromo|Q1326754|WD=Q1326754|1=Swan maiden}} * {{ill|lt=Miho Shrine|Q11489249|WD=Q11489249|1=Miho Shrine (Q11489249)}} * {{ill|lt=Izumo Taisha|Q696362|WD=Q696362|1=Izumo-taisha}} * {{ill|lt=Blue Cobblestone Street|Q11662622|WD=Q11662622|1=Aoishidatami Street}} * {{ill|lt=Sunny Yokoyama|Q11304946|WD=Q11304946|1=Sunny Yokoyama}} - {{ill|lt=Shake|Q11588367|WD=Q11588367|1=Shake (social class)}} of Miho Shrine. Rather than becoming a priest, he pursued the path of {{ill|lt=aerobatics|Q373557|WD=Q373557|1=Aerobatics}}, and is currently a pilot for {{ill|lt=Peach Aviation|Q1376634|WD=Q1376634|1=Peach Aviation}}. === External link === * [http://mihojinja.or.jp/ Miho Shrine official website] {{ja icon}} {{Shinto horizontal}} {{Normdaten}} {{shinto-stub}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Miho Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Miho Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shinto shrine]] [[Category:Shikinaisha|Miho Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Izumo Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Izumo Province]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Ebisu shrines]] [[Category:Cultural heritage monuments in Japan]] [[Category:松江市の重要文化財]] [[Category:重要有形民俗文化財]] [[Category:Shimane Prefecture designated tangible cultural property]] [[Category:Prefecture-designated Tangible Folk Cultural Properties]] [[Category:島根県の登録有形文化財]] [[Category:江戸時代の建築]] [[Category:Architecture of the Taisho era]] [[Category:松江市の建築物]] [[Category:松江市の歴史]] [[Category:Taisha-zukuri]] [[Category:Tourist attractions in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:kkkkkkkkkkkkkk]] [[Category:nnnnnnnnn]] [[Category:qqqqqqq]]
